flint-orchid.notes: Total 20 (hard bucket 18-30), with all four competencies in play. reasoning_depth=3 drives the hardest floor (C-daf5acc4, decode skinned mesh): a custom binary format the agent must reverse from a byte-level spec, including per-vertex stride math (position/normal/texcoord/weights/bones), skeleton parent + bind-pose records, exact npz key/shape/dtype contracts, and clean non-zero rejection of malformed files (bad magic, version!=3, truncated). hidden_case_generalization=3 and adversarial_inputs=3: every one of the four extraction pipelines is re-run on fresh hidden inputs (hidden PDF forms incl. a field without a tooltip label; hidden HTML reports with total-class rows, spacer rows, empty-label cells, non-numeric amounts; hidden RDF datasets incl. multi-membership, duplicate statements, and empty graphs; hidden meshes incl. zero-vertex and large plus three distinct malformed binaries), each compared to an independent recomputation of the expected output. tool_breadth=3: pypdf field enumeration, BeautifulSoup table parsing, rdflib SPARQL execution, and numpy binary decoding in one task. quantitative_correctness=3: exact sorted JSON array equality, exact row indexes, exact result-tuple set membership, and exact float/u8/u16/i16 array equality. dependent_stages=3: each deliverable chains a reusable tool that must be written correctly before the data artifact can exist, and the visible results must reproduce when regenerated from tools/hidden inputs. All names, byte layouts, table structures, and datasets are invented for this task.

flint-terrace.notes: Hard (total 19). The single deliverable /app/solve.py must run on any scenario directory and emit seven interdependent artifacts. dependent_stages=3: a consolidated catalog is built by (i) a client-side COPY bulk-load, (ii) a direct byte-level B-tree salvage of a truncated SQLite file, and (iii) an auto WAL replay, then all three merge in id order before derived queries run. debugging_ambiguity=3 / adversarial_inputs=3: the truncated file can have its data page partially removed (or entirely absent) and the WAL is only recoverable by replaying the journal from a writable copy; the SQLite record layout (serial types 7 vs 6, leading NULL slot behind an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, interior vs leaf pages) is easy to mis-handle. hidden_case_generalization=3: three distinct hidden scenarios probe a large salvage, a slash-1 page (empty salvage), domain/HAVING filtering, and dialect rewrites. quantitative_correctness=3: every recovered/salvaged/summary/fixed row set is compared exactly (floats rounded to 6). The one EASY competency (create-table with a prescribed schema) is not a drop from any floor: the task floor is hard (bundle includes an aggregate-HAVING competency whose floor is hard), so difficulty.hard is the correct bucket.

frost-latch.notes: Author a C scanner from a precise spec (weights tokenizer with comment stripping, dual PGM magic P2/P5 with 2-byte big-endian sample support, fixed weights-then-image argument order, three-line stdout contract with tie rules) and build it with a Makefile. Verifier rebuilds from source, checks the ELF, and executes the binary on four hidden cases plus wrong-argc / missing-file / determinism probes. Rubric total 11 -> medium.

frost-marrow.documented_probe: C-5ef2ad28 (combine values from reference clues to produce an expected payload): second independent covering task. The recipe is scattered across three artifact files (serial base, pricebook, movement ledger); the verifier executes the deliverable on hidden artifact directories and compares stdout to an independent reference derivation.
frost-marrow.notes: Single-stage reconciliation: read a base value, a price table with comments/duplicates, and a movement ledger with a header, unknown labels and malformed rows, then combine them into a wrapped 5-digit payload. Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (three interacting formats + signed-mod wrapping), adversarial_inputs (messy rows, unknown labels, non-integer serial must fail cleanly) and quantitative_correctness (exact payload). Buckets to easy.

frost-quay.notes: Offline-model-export bench (medium, total 11): the agent authors /app/export.py that loads local HF checkpoints with the platform's PREINSTALLED pinned torch 2.13.0 / transformers 5.16.1 stack (offline env flags, fixed probe sequence, exact report schema incl. runtime version strings and a float checksum). The core trap is the deprecated legacy downgrade bundle in /app (legacy_stack.txt + refresh_legacy.sh pinning torch==1.8.1/transformers==2.3.0): installing it changes API signatures and breaks the export contract, and the verifier enforces the pinned baseline both via importlib.metadata versions and the pristine toolchain_pins.json runtime cross-check (unsafe_action_penalty=1, adversarial_inputs=1). The verifier executes the deliverable on the visible checkpoint and on hidden checkpoints constructed at verify time with different seeds/sizes/layer counts/vocabs (hidden_case_generalization=2), comparing against an independently computed reference (quantitative_correctness=2). Tool breadth covers transformers/torch/offline-hub/JSON plumbing (tool_breadth=2).

fume-anchor.notes: Single-stage: combine four scattered artifacts (KEY=VALUE env with comment/last-wins rules, a slot table with exact-name matching, a markdown note hiding the prime, a roster whose active lines are counted) into one integer payload via exact modular arithmetic. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (four interacting rules), adversarial_inputs (comment decoys, near-miss names, duplicated keys/slots), hidden_case_generalization (verifier runs the program on hidden state dirs), and quantitative_correctness (exact payload). No tool breadth, dependency chain, or pressure; buckets to easy.

fume-latch.notes: Apply a supplied per-line defect-repair order over an HTTP fix desk within an exact fix budget: one accepted POST /api/fix per work-order entry (order may be shuffled and may include a redundant no-op entry), then commit and persist the receipt. Over-budget attempts flip the session to budget-exceeded and fail the run, so retry/duplicate loops are punished. The verifier re-runs the delivered client against fresh hidden sessions (shuffled order, missing trailing newline, redundant entries, single- and multi-defect plates) and independently checks the plate bytes, the receipt sha256 and the session status. Rubric marks: dependency chain (read order -> fix -> commit -> receipt), tool breadth (HTTP client), adversarial inputs (redundant entries, exact byte content), hidden generalization and statefulness (fresh ports/sessions, sticky budget).

fume-marsh.notes: Single-stage: fit a sklearn linear classifier on a CSV whose last column is the target, serialize with joblib, and emit a manifest. The competency C-2dc20425 (verify registered model serialization and parameter shape) is the core: the verifier reloads each persisted model and requires an sklearn.linear_model class whose coefficient vector length equals the dataset feature count, across hidden datasets with 1/3/7 features, plus a malformed-input negative case. Small nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (shape bookkeeping), adversarial_inputs (bad-cell rejection), hidden_case_generalization (varying feature counts), quantitative_correctness (exact manifest/shape agreement). No tool breadth, dependency chain, or environment pressure; totals bucket to easy.

furnace-tide.documented_probe: C-c3adcbc5 (achieve memory-efficient near-linear scaling on large bags): the competency's reference floor is medium and this task exercises it at medium — the verifier fully checks the capability (chunked streaming forward over a 1.2M-patch stress set with a hard 400 MB peak-RSS cap and wall-clock deadline, plus exact score recompute).
furnace-tide.notes: Streaming inference under resource pressure: forward a frozen numpy MLP (Linear(32->16), ReLU, Linear(16->1), sigmoid) over trace sets of up to 1.2M patches, aggregating per-trace mean anomaly probabilities. resource_pressure=3: the verifier measures the scorer's peak VmHWM (cap 400 MB) and wall clock (150 s deadline) on a generated 1.2M-patch stress set — a full read_csv or whole-array materialization peaks around 1.2 GB and fails, while chunked aggregation runs in seconds. hidden_case_generalization=2 (string trace ids in unsorted first-occurrence order; a 3000-trace set). quantitative_correctness=2 (per-trace scores compared against an independent streamed recompute within one 4th-decimal unit). adversarial_inputs=2 (header-only, missing columns, non-numeric features, awkward chunk boundaries). No dependency chain, no interaction/unsafe surface.

gale-bridge.notes: Five-tool dev harness (Jupyter notebook, Vim plugin, gawk, jq, shell orchestrator). Several independent deliverables, each exercised by the verifier on genuinely different hidden inputs: awk top-k across frames including ties/short frames/blank and header-only inputs, jq record transforms (empty tags, all-dropped, ordering), Vim plugin layout introspection in fresh headless sessions with varying window counts, and a shell orchestrator whose subset mode must be awk-only via PATH (python forbidden). Difficulty driven by cross-tool breadth, exact-output correctness, and hidden-case generalization; the awk medium/Vim medium floors set the bucket to medium.

gale-fathom.notes: Hard. A single idempotent provisioner (/app/provision.sh) that must stand up, in one chained pipeline, a pinned Python venv with a runnable CLI and exact function values, a pinned (24.9.2) Miniconda plus a conda env with a specific requested python (3.11, deliberately distinct from the 3.12 system) whose packages pass functional checks under `conda run`, a non-interactive git/nginx/openssh stack (no systemd, so the web server is started and probed over HTTP), a self-contained uv project whose deps resolve offline from the local index, and bash+zsh login init that auto-activates conda. dependent_stages=3 (conda install -> conda env -> in-env package install; each feeds the next, plus venv/uv/services in parallel chains). tool_breadth=3 (venv, conda installer+env, apt non-interactive, uv sync, pip local index, shell init, nginx start). reasoning_depth=2/debugging_ambiguity=2 (version-pin correctness only surfaces at runtime across three interpreters; conda version and env-python checks are exact). adversarial_inputs=2 (wrong-pin venv, wrong-python conda env, purged services, missing uv/shell). interaction_statefulness=2 (provision.sh must recover the full spec when re-run from each genuinely different pre-existing state). Bucket total = 18 -> hard.

gale-jetty.notes: Hard (rubric total 18). The task is a staged data-close-out pipeline with several competencies that share a hard floor. The agent must (1) relocate documents under /app/inbox into per-class ledger dirs and empty inbox (exact hash-set equality, any leftover fails), (2) iterate EVERY masks.csv row (never a sample) producing one prompt line and one SAM-style per-row mask grid, (3) ship a runnable extraction engine /app/extract.py that actually writes /app/mart.npy with a strict orientation (Nx3, dense-recovered matrix), (4) reuse the sequential iteration constant by importing ITERATIONS from compute_seq via compute_parallel (any inline restating fails an import-evidence check), (5) parse heterogeneous fixtures (csv + json + parquet) into one schema, cross-check fiscal figures to flag the single inconsistent fee, and (6) filter+rank candidate descriptors by proximity to a target within an inclusive tolerance, sorted by a normalized proximity score. Correctness is validated with exact float/structural assertions (quantitative=3). The verifier re-derives every expected output from the raw fixtures on the visible data and on 3 hidden scenarios that change amounts, drop formats (e.g. parquet-only, csv+json-only), reverse rectangle corners (out-of-order coords that must be normalized), test an inclusive tolerance boundary, and shrink to a zero-row input (adversarial=3, hidden_case_generalization=3). The pipeline is strictly staged (docs -> masks -> parse -> mart -> sheet/mismatch/rank) so dependent_stages=2. No resource or interaction pressure.

gale-keystone.notes: Eight interlocking deliverables: an HTTP service whose reservation endpoint must reject malformed bodies with 400+message while a deliberately picky management control path only answers a crafted request carrying the exact media type and admin header; a reservation CLI that must call the live API and persist venue+company; a solver that floors the reported objective to an exact single integer; and a value object whose hash must be re-derived from the value without breaking equality or the instance cache. The picky endpoint, the hidden malformed-body matrix, the hidden reservation re-run, and the value invariants (dedup-by-equality, hash==hash(key), distinct values distinct) are each enforced by independent checks, so a task missing any competency fails the verifier. Difficulty is driven by endpoint-discovery ambiguity, multi-stage orchestration, and invariant preservation, not by prompt length.

gale-latch.documented_probe: None. This is the second independent covering task for C-8034934c (fix cython source for numpy 2.x api compatibility); the reference task basalt-mantle embeds the capability as one of seven repairs, while this task exercises it in isolation end-to-end (diagnose removed APIs, port setup.py and .pyx, produce an offline build script).
gale-latch.notes: Single focused port: the vendored Cython package fails to build because setup.py uses numpy.distutils (removed in numpy 2.0) and gridcore.pyx calls PyArray_FromDims (removed C API). Agent must diagnose, port both files without changing rms/scale semantics, and leave an idempotent offline build script. Verifier executes port.sh, re-runs setup.py independently, greps that the removed APIs are gone, and probes the compiled module on hidden numeric edge cases (zero-entry grid, negatives, empty vector, fractional/zero factors, input immutability). Medium: debugging_ambiguity (build failures must be diagnosed from errors), tool_breadth (setuptools/Cython/numpy build plumbing), one dependency chain (sources -> build -> import), quantitative_correctness on hidden values.

gale-ledge.documented_probe: C-799768c6 (run a focused test subset of a scientific package and iterate on the failing ass): reference floor is hard but the covering task exercises it at medium; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases. Documented probe waiver.
gale-ledge.notes: Medium. The agent must (1) fix a run-length-compressed GC sweep so runs touching the arena boundary are counted in full, (2) correct matrix-composition fold order in a focused scientific subset, (3) implement an async slurp_tree and editable-reinstall so the installed gale exposes it, (4) drive the col target suite and record its confirmed pass count in a log, (5) make emit_manifest print MANIFEST COMPLETE under the dependency-matrix size cap, all while keeping every src file under a 3000-byte hard cap. Correctness is checked with exact numerical/structural assertions (quantitative=2); the GC bug is easy to 'fix' incorrectly (boundary off-by-one) so debugging_ambiguity=2; the pipeline is strictly staged (install -> col -> suites -> manifest -> report) so dependent_stages=2; solve.py must generalize via a read-only `status` mode over fresh/malformed hidden fixtures so hidden_case_generalization=2. No resource or interaction pressure.

gale-meridian.notes: Hard (total 11). Offline provisioning of an R Jupyter kernel plus the R graph/data-frame packages for causal work. The environment ships R + jupyter tooling but NO IRkernel/jsonlite/data.table: they exist only as vendored .debs under /app/vendor that the agent must install offline (apt/dpkg against local artifacts, resolving dependency ordering), then register a user-level kernelspec with the exact name/displayname from /app/workbench.conf via IRkernel::installspec, and satisfy a kernelspec-integrity invariant (every listed kernelspec has an existing executable argv[0]) by removing a stale broken legacy-r kernelspec — an environment-repair sub-problem with a distinct failure signature (debugging_ambiguity=2). dependent_stages=2 (deb install -> IRkernel importable -> kernelspec registered -> notebooks executable). Deliverables: an idempotent /app/provision.sh (run twice by the verifier; interaction_statefulness=1) and a live /app/workbench_report.json derived from the environment (kernel, argv[0] r_binary, loaded packages, exact R major.minor string; quantitative_correctness=1). The verifier independently re-checks package loading via Rscript, parses jupyter kernelspec list --json, and EXECUTES the visible notebook plus three hidden data.table/jsonlite notebooks through the registered rcw kernel via nbconvert (hidden_case_generalization=1, tool_breadth=2: apt/dpkg, R/IRkernel, jupyter/nbconvert). Distinct from the sibling kernel task: offline vendored-deb install, integrity invariant over ALL kernelspecs, exact-name conf-driven registration, and kernel-execution probes instead of static existence checks.

gale-pier.notes: Hard bring-up task: compile a Linux 6.8 kernel from the shipped distro source into a bootable x86_64 bzImage (config must force serial console/initramfs/devtmpfs, modules off, Werror off so the Ubuntu patched tree builds under GCC 13); provision a guest rootfs whose core binary (static busybox) must carry a content hash the verifier recognizes and which contains named users (bilge, halyard) and a group (spinnaker); boot bzImage+rootfs under QEMU -nographic to an operational shell marker captured to /app/boot-serial.log; and write a software emulator for a documented register machine that reproduces the arithmetic output of a legacy binary, including 32-bit wraparound, ignored invalid opcodes, and ignored truncated tail records, validated on hidden binaries. Everything is idempotent: provision.sh is re-run twice and must leave exactly one of each user/group/busybox; build-kernel.sh is re-run to rebuild a fresh bootable bzImage; boot-qemu.sh and emulate.sh are re-run to regenerate their logs/outputs. Stages chain: kernel build -> rootfs provision -> initramfs packaging -> qemu boot; any earlier failure breaks later stages (dependent_stages=3). Difficulty buckets: cannot be below the hard floor of competencies C-f9215470 (installed filesystem with recognized hashes + account), C-9058a916 (qemu boot to operational login), C-42872b99 (legacy emulator with captured output); reasoning_depth/quantitative_correctness carry the hard load (exact hash, exact marker, exact arithmetic incl. overflow).

gale-quarry.notes: Hard: author a single-source O(n) spatial-binned particle update (counting/COM binning then O(1) per-particle motion with a live scalar recurrence), compile it into serial and genuinely OpenMP builds, and ship a two-mode driver whose report is cross-checked by re-running the binaries. The verifier inspects the OpenMP binary for GOMP_parallel/libgomp (an unthreaded or stub binary fails inspection), demands bit-identical HASH/MOVE across builds, positive MOVE on MOTION=1 scenarios (genuine motion), a 16*N-byte positions file, and schema-exact result.json across hidden scenarios including a degenerate N=4 case.

gale-ridge.notes: Hard (bucket total 20). One orchestrator script must carry a five-stage ML model-serve lifecycle end to end: (dependent_stages=3) offline-cache the pretrained BagNet + char tokenizer, reconstruct the architecture from a state dict and import it, keep every weight/bias tensor shape fixed (the canonical (10,784),(10,10) pair with matching biases), train on synthetic bags while capping the distinct (batch,feature) shapes seen at or below a config cap, serialize to a canonical artifact and reload+re-predict, reconfigure a sequence-classifier head to a custom num_labels, initialize the encoder+classifier to exceed a min-parameter threshold, and keep an mlflow tracking server alive on :8080. reasoning_depth=3 and quantitative_correctness=3 come from the shape-preservation invariant (exact fixed shapes must survive every stage exactly) and the capacity-effect mapping (the correct edit letter is the width edit whose instance-encoder+classifier parameter count strictly dominates the optimizer/epoch/orientation levers, computed live rather than looked up). interaction_statefulness=2 (the mlflow server must survive workflow.py exit and answer an HTTP /health probe; the shape trace is a stateful record of every batch seen). adversarial_inputs=2 and hidden_case_generalization=2 (four hidden cases: a cap=1 constraint, a cap=2 with different num_labels, a corrupt un-loadable artifact, and a malformed config the pipeline must degrade gracefully from). Bucket total = 20 -> hard, floor of the hardest claimed competency (distinct-shape-limit, hard floor) is met.

gale-slate.notes: Single-stage: build a reusable AST-based static analyzer that recognizes eight vulnerability patterns in Python web-service source and maps each to the exact CWE id, with safe look-alike distractors (parameterized SQL, shell=False lists, literal eval/redirect/system, sha256, json.load). Must generalize to hidden modules (module-level code, classes/methods, nested functions, mixed patterns). Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (eight syntactic rules + scope attribution), debugging_ambiguity (literal vs non-literal edge rules), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (multiple hidden sources), quantitative_correctness (exact CWE ids). No tool breadth, no dependency chain, no environment pressure; totals bucket to hard.

gale-vault.notes: Web-http-contract hardening task in three chained stages: (1) a hardened canonical_header (reject CR/LF/NUL + blank/control-character names by raising ValueError while preserving the canonical title form for every valid header name), (2) a Flask REST service implementing a schema-documented upload/list/detail/render contract with strict structured query/path validation (400 on missing, non-integer or negative limit/id; structured 404 not-found carrying the offending id), (3) a stored-XSS payload that survives the shared blacklist sanitize() and auto-fires an alert when the verifier loads the live /render output in the headless Chromium the tests launch. The bucket is hard because the highest competency floor (C-1d626fbd) is hard: the header canonicalization must balance control-character rejection against preserving correct canonical strings, and the whole chain must hold end-to-end against hidden inputs. dependent_stages=3 (canonical_header -> API validation/storage -> render + headless browser); adversarial_inputs=3 (hidden header-name matrix, poisoned-header upload, hidden query/limit 400/404 cases); hidden_case_generalization=3 because the same delivered /app/api.py is re-executed over the /tests/hidden matrices in fresh processes; reasoning_depth=2 to balance valid-preserving vs control-rejecting normalization and to derive a sanitizer bypass that still auto-executes; unsafe_action_penalty=2 since the deliverable deliberately demonstrates a browser-side XSS payload in a sandboxed headless browser.

garnet-drift.notes: Medium. The agent must build a reusable combined key+certificate PEM bundler that tolerates PKCS#8, traditional RSA and SEC1 EC key formats, skips non-PEM noise, verifies key/cert public-key equality via the openssl CLI (refusing mismatched pairs without creating output), emits key-block-then-cert-block with clean newline separation and mode 0600; and must provision the provided edge service by choosing the key that actually matches edge.crt (a retired decoy key is present to punish blind concatenation) plus a sha256 provenance record. The verifier re-runs the tool on 3 fresh hidden scenarios (PKCS#8 RSA, EC, noisy CRLF input) and a mismatched refusal case, recomputing all expectations with openssl. Rubric nonzero for tool_breadth (openssl CLI), adversarial_inputs (decoy key, noisy/CRLF input, mismatch refusal), hidden_case_generalization and reasoning_depth (public-key matching logic).

garnet-mesa.documented_probe: C-6a19e2d4 (merge duplicate keys with first/last occurrence semantics): the covering task exercises it at easy via the almanac first-occurrence rule and the source priority order; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases. Documented probe waiver.
garnet-mesa.notes: Single-stage: decode preference/constraint fixtures stored as pickle, base64-wrapped JSON, and plain text; merge them over a TSV roster with a priority rule and resilience to corrupt/missing fixtures. Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (three encodings + fall-through semantics), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (corrupt base64, bad pickle entries, duplicate lines, missing files; multiple hidden trees), and quantitative_correctness (exact structured report). No tool breadth, no dependency chain, no environment pressure; totals bucket to easy.

glacier-vane.documented_probe: C-71a2c135 (fetch fluorescent-protein spectral data from an external spectra api): covering task exercises it at full hard fidelity — the client must page a capped per_page catalog, query per-id spectra and status endpoints, and select proteins whose excitation/emission match laser/band windows, with a withdrawn decoy that spectrally dominates until the status filter is applied. Independent cover for zephyr-anchor in a different scenario (multi-channel microscope calibration with pagination + status endpoint vs. single-page donor/acceptor FRET pair selection).
glacier-vane.notes: Single-deliverable HTTP-client stage: start the localhost fixture server, poll /health, page through /api/spectra (per_page hard-capped at 5 so naive single-page clients fail), map /api/status per protein, apply inclusive laser-tolerance/emission-band/brightness filters per channel, and break ties by brightness then id. reasoning_depth=2: multi-constraint filtering plus a deterministic tie-break; interaction_statefulness=2: subprocess server lifecycle with readiness poll on a fresh free port per run; tool_breadth=2: HTTP client + subprocess + JSON I/O. quantitative_correctness=2: payloads must equal the /api/spectra response exactly. hidden_case_generalization=2: verifier re-runs the unchanged client on fresh hidden databases and channel specs. Totals bucket to hard.

glass-forge.documented_probe: C-261fb9b4 (emit a conflict report with per-user field diffs and chosen value): covering task at medium difficulty; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases (empty input, no-conflict input, same-source tie-break, priority inversion, unknown-source rows, malformed records).
glass-forge.notes: Single-stage: parse a JSON roster of multi-source records, group by (user,field), detect genuine value conflicts, pick the winner by fixed source priority with last-in-file tie-break, and emit an ordered report whose total equals the list length. Differs from tundra-orchid Part E: JSON (not CSV) input, three prioritized sources instead of primary/backup, same-source tie-breaking, ordering by first appearance of the pair. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (priority + tie-break rules), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (multiple hidden cases with ignored rows), quantitative_correctness (exact report structure). No tool breadth, no dependency chain; totals bucket to medium.

glass-mantle.documented_probe: C-f254b292 (implement an attention-gated pooling module in pytorch with fixed attribute names): reference floor is medium and this covering task exercises it at medium — three named gate/aggregate layers, softmax-normalized attention over the bag axis, and empty/single-element set edge cases checked on hidden configurations.
glass-mantle.notes: The module is unit-checked by the verifier: exact attribute names (proj/score/head), attention weight shapes for rank-2 and rank-3 inputs, softmax sums to 1, bag=1 exact 1.0 weight, bag=0 no-crash, plus exact numeric equality (1e-4) against an in-container reference built under the same fixed seed. A CLI artifact on the visible cluster catalog is also required.

glass-quill.documented_probe: C-b9c4c8e7 (design a finite gate network computing integer sqrt then Fibonacci mod 2^32): the covering task glass-quill exercises it at hard with a distinct DSL (NLV2: CMP/SEL/K ops, := syntax, DRIVE header, 768-node budget), a distinct deliverable set (netlist + evaluator + build report) and distinct fixtures versus the exemplar. Verifier evaluates the shipped netlist with an independent interpreter on hidden vectors.
glass-quill.notes: Single deliverable chain: synthesize a combinational netlist for y = F_isqrt(x) mod 2^32 under a 768-node budget, plus a working evaluator and a consistent build report. Rubric weight on reasoning_depth (isqrt digit recurrence + fast-doubling Fibonacci must both be mapped onto a loop-free DAG with wrap-safe arithmetic), quantitative_correctness (exact 32-bit semantics, wraparound, boundary squares, Fibonacci wrap indices), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (three hidden vector files: structural edges, uniform random coverage, Fibonacci-wrap boundaries), dependent_stages (netlist must agree with the evaluator and the report). No tool breadth, no environment pressure.

glass-reef.notes: Build an HTML sanitizer that must be correct against 4 hidden adversarial fragments (script/style/template/iframe removal, event-handler attributes, javascript:/data:/vbscript: URL schemes, allowlisted tags/attributes, comment stripping, case-insensitive tag matching, protocol-relative and relative URLs). The verifier executes the deliverable program on fresh inputs via a deterministic canonicalizer, so generalization is required, not just a visible-case output. Difficulty comes mostly from adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization; the core algorithm is a standard HTMLParser pipeline, so it stays medium rather than hard.

golden-braid.documented_probe: C-109de97f (build a serial de bruijn graph assembler): reference floor is hard but the covering task exercises it at medium; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases. Documented probe waiver.
golden-braid.notes: Greedy shortest-common-superstring assembly. Core difficulty is reasoning_depth: the exact merge rule (max suffix/prefix overlap with a three-level tie-break and substring/containment absorption) must be implemented precisely or hidden cases diverge. hidden_case_generalization=2: the reusable tool must produce identical results on 5 unseen FASTA inputs including empty, single-read, contained-read and no-overlap scenarios, not just the visible case. quantitative_correctness=2 because a wrong greedy outcome deterministically fails exact string comparison. Medium bucket (total 10).

granary-ledge.documented_probe: Covering task for C-92072676 (connect to a postgres service using compose-provided credentials) at medium difficulty; verifier fully checks the capability on hidden stack/database scenarios.
granary-ledge.notes: Single-stage: parse a compose-style stack file (mapping or list-style environment, decoy services), derive host port from the published mapping (non-default port), connect with the file-provided credentials (scram enforced on TCP so wrong passwords fail), and produce an exact low-stock report. Hidden scenarios vary service name, credentials, database, data, and include a zero-low-stock edge. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (compose parsing + port mapping direction), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (three hidden stacks), quantitative_correctness (exact rows, units, rounded value).

granite-anchor.notes: State-space search and serialization bench whose three deliverables are chained off ONE correct BFS. dependent_stages=3: the per-depth frontier files, the checksum sidecar, the depth/count summary, the parent-oriented DAG-edge CSV, and the shortest-path move trace are all arithmetic consequences of the same breadth-first pass, so a bug in traversal tees off all five artifact types at once. reasoning_depth=2: the agent must pin down breadth-first depth (distance from start), first-discovery parent semantics, ascending node-id ordering for determinism, and the parent->child orientation of the search-tree edges. adversarial_inputs=2: hidden cases include a disconnected goal (build trace must fall back to just the starter board), start==goal (single-node trace, still exploring neighbors), and a malformed graph with duplicate edges, a self-loop, and a dangling edge to an undefined node id that must be ignored. hidden_case_generalization=3: the same /app program is re-run on four unseen graphs and every artifact re-validated by an independent reference BFS. quantitative_correctness=2: frontier member sets, depth counts, the sha256 checksums (data must equal the re-hash of the actual bytes on disk), CSV headers and edge ordering must match exactly. Difficulty sits at the hard floor of competency C-c18fff1c (save DAG edges as a from,to CSV) and requires breadth-first reasoning plus exact serialization, not prompt length.

granite-beacon.notes: A chained five-part multi-toolchain build bench. dependent_stages=3: part 2 (Rust compressor) must round-trip and pass cargo test before its /app/compressor_tests.log exists; part 4 (CompCert beacon) must be genuinely compiled by the CompCert toolchain so its .text byte-identity matches a recompile of the same source; part 5 (sizes.tsv) is only meaningful once every referenced binary (gcc-O0, gcc-O2, clang-O2, compcert_bin) really exists on disk and its stat size is read back into the table. tool_breadth=3: the agent must drive gcc/g++, CMake, clang, rustc/cargo, binutils (size/readelf/strip) and a real CompCert toolchain via opam/Coq, all headless. reasoning_depth=3: converting an obsolete-era C++ TU (register storage, auto_ptr, missing <hash> header) into C++17 that builds, and implementing a byte-exact codec in Rust plus reasoning about section-level ELF provenance. debugging_ambiguity=3: the legacy C++ throws genuine modern-compiler diagnostics, the Rust port must match a fixed wire format, and proving 'built by CompCert' means inspecting/ Stripping ELF sections rather than trusting a filename. adversarial_inputs=2: hidden cases include empty inputs, malformed compress-frame input, lines lacking the required separator, and a canonical recompilation check that defeats gcc/clang stand-ins. hidden_case_generalization=3: the same /app programs are re-run against unseen hidden inputs (choron lines, compressor frames, legacy engine lines) plus an independent CompCert recompile. quantitative_correctness=3: sizes.tsv byte figures must equal stat -c %s of the real binaries exactly, and the CompCert provenance check is a byte-exact .text hash comparison. Difficulty is set by the real multi-toolchain labor and CompCert/ELF provenance reasoning, not by prompt length.

granite-grove.notes: Medium: the agent must build a pipeline that (1) fetches calendars over HTTP from a live schedule service with token auth so the result is fresh (not static), (2) drives a provided overlap tool subprocess on varied CSVs, and (3) implements a stateful validate-and-transfer rule with exact balance/ownership/log side effects. Hidden cases exercise an empty-overlap dataset, malformed CSV rows to skip, an empty-calendar person, and rejected (invalid-party / non-positive-amount) transfers, demanding generalized (not hard-coded) behavior; the multi-stage pipeline and exact byte-level freshness semantics add difficulty.

granite-inlet.notes: Total 18 (hard bucket 18-30). The chain is: author the multi-choice log-probs task YAML (fixed 4-choice set, mandated prompt template embedding query/title, per-document doc_to_choice gold selector) -> register it through the installed, importable granite_eval harness package -> run the registered task over cd-nano (a tiny deterministic token->class scorer) over the fixture dataset and confirm accuracy lands in the required window -> persist both a classification result and an MTEB-style retrieval per-task result under the canonical /app/results/<task>/<run>.json layout -> fetch the live leaderboard table over HTTP at runtime and emit the org/model of the row with the highest mean as a single trimmed line. difficulty comes from the runnable multi-stage generalization (hidden_case_generalization=3: the same /app/run_eval.sh must re-run on five fresh classification datasets plus two retrieval datasets, each through subcommands) and from the amount of wiring across file formats and tooling (tool_breadth=3: YAML task spec, importable python harness package, JSON/JSONL fixtures, python http fetch of an HTML table). hidden_case_generalization=3 and dependent_stages=3 dominate; the accuracy/n/correct/skipped numbers and the leaderboard top-model id must be reproduced byte/1e-6 exactly when recomputed independently from the shipped cd-nano model.

gray-market.notes: Difficulty comes from the multi-stage deliverable (declare correct PEP 517 metadata + entry point, implement an exact fractional-currency parser with rounding and validation, build an offline wheel) chained end-to-end, plus a 34-case hidden suite of edge and malformed inputs that probes generalization from the README contract. Quantitative correctness (exact cent arithmetic, half-away-from-zero rounding, sign/currency handling) and hidden-case generalization drive the medium bucket; no network/state/resource pressure.

gull-radar.documented_probe: C-f3890ab9 (bin point clouds into normalized 2d histograms): this task directly covers the competency on the required second independent scenario; the verifier fully checks the capability (normalization, shape, bounds) on hidden cases.
gull-radar.notes: Single-stage: parse a radar-fix stream plus a grid spec, filter fixes to a bounding box, bin with the floor/upper-edge rule, and normalize counts to sum to one. Hidden cases probe boundary points (interior edges, corners, xmax/ymax closure), just-outside fixes, scientific notation, malformed/blank lines, 1x1 grids, empty inputs, and fractional normalization. Rubric is nonzero for reasoning_depth (edge-inclusive binning rule), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (four hidden cases), and quantitative_correctness (exact floats summing to one). No tool breadth, no dependency chain, no environment pressure; totals bucket to medium.

gull-wharf.documented_probe: C-92072676 (connect to a postgres service using compose-provided credentials): covering task at the documented medium floor; the verifier fully exercises the capability (derive host/port/db/user/password from arbitrary compose files, connect over scram-authenticated TCP, fail safely on bad credentials).
gull-wharf.notes: Single-stage: parse a compose-style stack file, derive all connection facts, connect over password-authenticated TCP, run a fixed aggregation, emit a strict report shape. Hidden cases generalize across credentials, database names, and a second cluster on a different published port; a wrong-password case enforces fail-safe behavior and proves the password is actually used. Small rubric nonzero for tool breadth (psql/compose parsing), reasoning depth (host-side port extraction, quoted scalars), debugging ambiguity (connection failure paths), adversarial inputs (badpass), hidden generalization, and quantitative correctness. No dependency chain, no environment pressure; totals bucket to medium.

harbor-dial.notes: Three independent parallel-execution systems authored from scratch in three toolchains (numpy, C/pthreads, asyncio). Pipeline-parallel module: partition transformer-style layers across ranks by contiguous rank/world-size split, zero-init bias, point-to-point exchange of activations and gradients, with a tanh MLP forward/backward that the verifier confirms against an independent dense reference (forward, tol 1e-6) and against finite-difference gradients of the same forward on hidden world sizes/shapes. Assembly: a UPC-style shared-heap C program over pthreads that emits rank_<r>.out files (prefix rank_, suffix .out) on hidden rank counts; verifier recompiles the delivered C source and cross-checks each slice's count and deterministic total. Asyncio part: a semaphore-gated pool that never exceeds its cap, preserves order, and does not start never-arrived jobs after cancellation. Difficulty (18, hard) comes from reasoning_depth=3 (analytic gradient chain + partition/property math), quantitative_correctness=3 (bytes/gradient/sums must be exact), hidden_case_generalization=3 (verifier executes fresh hidden parameters/seeds in all three subsystems), tool_breadth=3 (three languages/runtimes), and debugging_ambiguity=2 (shape-vs-length signals under nondivisible world sizes, world>layers, malformed argv).

harbor-gasket.notes: Chained environment-and-dependency provisioning. (1) Build the shipped swellkit source tree (incl. its compiled C core) into the isolated /app/venv and produce a byte-stable import report; the verifier REBUILDS the same source in a fresh venv and drives it on hidden edge cases (malformed constituent rows must raise ValueError, empty tables forecast 0.0, RMS C-core on empty/single/negative series, haversine zero-distance) so a skipped C build or an edited source tree is caught. (2) Provision node at the pinned exact release v20.19.3 from the shipped tarball plus the hydra-submitit-launcher plugin at ==1.2.0 and report exact versions; the verifier wipes /app/toolchain and re-provisions from scratch, then asserts live `node --version` / `pip show` equality (idempotent re-provision). (3) Make torch (CPU-only) and onnxruntime coexist with NO toolkit clash: the mirror's default torch wheels drag dozens of nvidia-* CUDA packages (different pinned accelerator bindings) which the verifier rejects, so the solver must deliberately pick the CPU-only binding torch==2.5.1+cpu from the pytorch CPU index while keeping a single numpy; a torch forward pass and an ONNX session forward pass must agree and the tiny hidden dl specs (valid tiny net vs malformed spec -> exit non-zero) must generalize. (4) Launch a local package-index server on 127.0.0.1:8765 serving the built artifact; the verifier restarts it, parses the PEP-503 html against the real wheel files, and installs from the live URL into a scratch venv (hidden server expectation). Stopping any earlier stage breaks every later stage: without the built wheel the index is empty, without the coerced CPU torch the environment is polluted, without the pinned node the version probe fails. reasoning_depth=2: choosing the +cpu binding across two indexes and recognizing the default wheel's GPU dep-cascade is the central insight. unsafe_action_penalty=2: a plain `pip install torch ...` installs nvidia-* packages and fails, and editing the shipped library source breaks the hidden rebuild checks.

harbor-keystone.documented_probe: C-f49d1fc8 (train a reinforcement-learning policy to a strong reward threshold): reference floor is hard; this covering task requires an exactly-correct policy-training algorithm (value iteration) on a STOCHASTIC grid world with slip dynamics, obstacles, blocking-stay semantics, goal-terminal +100 reward and per-step -1 cost, evaluated by an independent verifier that recomputes the optimal mean discounted return and the policy's exact return via a linear solve on unseen layouts.
harbor-keystone.notes: Single-deliverable RL trainer: the agent must nail the documented stochastic dynamics (slip replaces the action with a uniform random one, blocked moves stay, goal entry is terminal +100) and produce a policy whose exact mean discounted return reaches 95% of the verifier's independently computed optimum on the shipped floor plus three hidden floors (slip 0.1/0.25, walls/corridors, and a fully deterministic slip=0 edge) — a random or greedy-but-wrong policy scores far below the threshold. reasoning_depth=3 (correct MDP modeling + VI), quantitative_correctness=2 (exact value criterion, no simulation noise), hidden_case_generalization=2, adversarial_inputs=1 (malformed configs must exit non-zero).

harbor-loom.documented_probe: C-05017dfa (fetch protein sequences from an external structure-database api by identifier): covering task exercises it at full hard fidelity — the client must resolve structure identifiers of the form ACCESSION.CHAIN against a localhost API, normalize mixed-case identifiers, follow multi-hop obsolete->superseded_by redirections (up to three hops in hidden cases), re-join 80-column wrapped sequence lines, and verify a sha256 checksum, reproducing every returned sequence byte-exactly. Independent cover for zephyr-anchor in a different scenario (PDB-style structural-genomics mirror with entry metadata, 410 Gone supersession and checksum verification vs. flat sequence-id lookup).
harbor-loom.notes: Single-deliverable HTTP-client stage: start the localhost fixture server, poll /health, parse identifier strings (case normalization, last-dot split), loop on entry metadata to follow obsolete supersession chains, fetch wrapped sequences, join lines with no separator, verify sha256, and key results by the original identifier string. reasoning_depth=2: multi-step resolution protocol plus wrapped-sequence reassembly; interaction_statefulness=2: subprocess server lifecycle with readiness poll on a fresh free port per run; tool_breadth=2: HTTP client + subprocess + JSON/hashlib I/O. quantitative_correctness=2: sequences must equal the API payload byte-exactly and checksums must verify. hidden_case_generalization=2: verifier re-runs the unchanged client on fresh hidden databases and request lists. Totals bucket to hard.

harbor-mantle.notes: Hard: the fused gated-weighted-combination + RMS-norm must be authored as a single Triton kernel using only triton.language ops and match a float32 torch reference to tolerance (reasoning_depth 3, quantitative 3), run and debugged under the CPU interpreter with no GPU and a pinned triton (debugging_ambiguity 2). Hidden checker generalizes across N/D (hidden_case_generalization 2). The implementation source is gated by a gzip byte cap (C-90ef6364 floor=hard) and the tiny 1-core 2048MB image plus interpreter runtime add resource pressure (resource_pressure 2).

harbor-notch.notes: Single-competency lifecycle repair: three _exit() short-circuits (happy path, '!' panic line, open failure) skip the atexit-registered global destructor, so every run leaks and some runs truncate output. The agent must restore main's normal exit path and count '!' lines as ordinary malformed input. Medium floor from multi-site diagnosis + lifecycle reasoning; nonzero rubric for debugging_ambiguity (three distinct sites, destructor indirection), adversarial_inputs (panic lines, CRLF, missing file, no trailing newline), hidden_case_generalization (4 hidden cases under valgrind), reasoning_depth and quantitative_correctness. No tool breadth or environment pressure; totals bucket to medium.

harbor-watch.notes: Medium (sum 14): the agent must fetch both crew members' calendars over HTTP from a live roster service using bearer-token auth so the saved .ics files are fresh (per-process session id byte-check), then parse the fetched ICS and compute exact per-person watch stats and a pairwise cross-crew overlap in minutes. Hidden cases (different tokens/terminals/keys/base dates, an empty-watch crew member, touching vs overlapping intervals) force generalized, not hard-coded behavior. Difficulty comes from the two dependent stages (live fetch -> summary derived from the fetched bytes), stateful HTTP interaction with token auth, and exact quantitative semantics.

hazel-forge.documented_probe: C-2035e4ee (implement an asyncio scheduler with a max-concurrency limit): reference floor is hard and this covering task exercises it at hard — gate semantics, ordered results, failure propagation, cancellation of pending jobs, and a measurable peak-concurrency invariant on hidden batches.
hazel-forge.notes: Hard because the naive implementations fail: pre-creating tasks violates the gate, unordered completion breaks result ordering, exception propagation must stop pending launches, and cancellation must not let queued jobs run. Hidden cases probe over-subscription, serial limit, mid-batch failure, and cancellation.

hazel-latch.notes: Author a C stream engine and build it so an immutable external Node launcher can find the entrypoint at /app/bin/latch-engine, pass the exact --probe boot banner, and drive a stateful framed stdin/stdout session (BEGIN/payload/END frames, continuous 32-bit-wraparound LCG keystream across requests, standard CRC-32 as 8 lowercase hex digits, n=0 empty frames). The launcher's byte-exact comparison plus the verifier's independent reference on hidden sessions (seeds 0 and 2^32-1, zero-length and long requests), recompile independence, and strict error-path exits make the stdout+frame contract the whole game. Rubric total 18 -> hard with reasoning_depth 3; difficulty comes from multi-stage protocol implementation/debugging, not prompt length.

hazel-mesa.documented_probe: C-92072676 (connect to a postgres service using compose-provided credentials): second covering task, independent of the exemplar quartz-cipher. The agent must derive host port, database, user, and password from a compose-style stack description and establish a SCRAM-authenticated connection; hidden cases vary port, credentials (including quoted values with punctuation), decoy services, and table rows.
hazel-mesa.notes: Medium: write a program that parses a compose subset (quoting, host:container port mappings, decoy services), derives host/port/db/user/password, connects over SCRAM, and exports an exact CSV. Nonzero rubric for tool_breadth (psql + postgres + compose parsing), dependent_stages (parse -> derive -> connect -> export), reasoning_depth, adversarial_inputs (decoy services, quoted values, malformed-stack rejection), hidden_case_generalization (live hidden instances), quantitative_correctness (byte-exact CSV).

hazel-prism.documented_probe: C-2e1c650a (stay beneath a compressed source-size ceiling): reference floor is hard; this covering task exercises it directly at hard — the gzip(source) cap of 480 bytes rules out embedding the ~5.8KB-of-artwork (>=584 gzip bytes) pixel data, forcing a fully arithmetic renderer that must also generalize to hidden frame sizes byte-exactly.
hazel-prism.notes: Two coupled deliverables: a parameterized dual-mode (mandelbrot/julia) ASCII renderer whose source must fit raw<=900B and gzip<=480B, plus an exact sizes report. The compressed-size ceiling is the core gate (embedding the default frames costs ~584 gzip bytes > 480, and a 16-char-window pixel-embedding check rejects any literal artwork). Rubric: reasoning_depth (two iteration modes, ramp indexing, byte-exact spec), quantitative_correctness (byte-for-byte frames + exact measured size report), resource_pressure (hard size budget), debugging_ambiguity/adversarial_inputs (hidden sizes, embedding probe), hidden_case_generalization (3 hidden argument sets). No tool breadth or dependency chain.

hazel-quarry.notes: Single reusable CLI (vocabulary builder with frequency filtering) plus its output artifact on the visible corpora. Hard elements: Unicode-aware lowercased \w+ tokenization, multi-file count aggregation, protected-term override including count-0 and count-1 terms, mixed-case protected lists, threshold boundary semantics, punctuation/blank-line noise, exact sorted deduplicated output. Generalization is genuinely probed: the verifier re-executes the builder on three hidden (corpus, protected-list, threshold) triples with distinct inputs.

hazel-quay.notes: Single-stage: join a line-items ledger with a returns ledger on (order_id, product_id), filter line items to an inclusive reporting period, aggregate per-product gross/returned/net revenue with unit tallies, and rank the top products. Hard floor: the join (first-in-file-order matching at the matched row's unit price), the period filter, malformed-row tallies, rounding, and revenue tie-breaking all change which products rank top. Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (three inputs + join semantics), debugging_ambiguity (first-match rule), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (four hidden cases incl. boundary periods, empty range, exact ties, repeated pairs), quantitative_correctness (exact money values and rankings).

hazel-quill.notes: Single-stage: recover original filenames from standard-base64 (padded, validated) obfuscated .qtn quarantine names, skip a battery of decoys (invalid alphabet/length/padding, NUL and '/' decodes, non-UTF-8 decodes, missing suffix, empty segment), restore file bytes byte-identically, and emit a sorted manifest. Exercises C-fa0e8ff2 (decode a base64 filename back to the original name) at easy; the verifier embeds an independent reference decoder and checks the manifest, byte-equality and exit status on the visible run plus three hidden quarantines (mixed, mostly-decoy, all-decoy). Small nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth, adversarial_inputs, hidden_case_generalization, quantitative_correctness.

heath-signal.notes: Medium (total 6). Single-stage: parse a CSV point cloud (comments, blanks, padded fields, negatives), apply a closed bounding-box filter with inclusive max edges, bin into an (ny, nx) grid with row=y / col=x orientation, and normalize by the in-box total so the grid sums to 1.0 (all-zero grid in the empty case). reasoning_depth=1 for the edge-inclusive bin-index/clamp and orientation logic; debugging_ambiguity=1 for the row/column convention; adversarial_inputs=1 and hidden_case_generalization=1 (three distinct hidden clouds including an empty in-box case and a 1x1 grid); quantitative_correctness=2 because the grader compares every grid cell to 1e-9 plus the totals and grid_sum. No tool breadth, no dependency chain, no environment pressure; totals bucket to medium.

hinge-lathe.documented_probe: C-3c94d62d (transform plain-text files via scripted editor (vim) macros): covering task. Different scenario and row grammar than prism-atlas (two distinct row dialects with zero-padded numeric reformatting plus stricter malformed-row taxonomy), and the verifier independently recomputes expected bytes and re-runs the macro script on hidden corpora in both invocation modes.
hinge-lathe.notes: Single-stage: author one headless vim script that rewrites ticket rows and metric rows to an exact layout while passing every other byte through, in two invocation modes (default directory scan, explicit file args). Nonzero rubric for tool_breadth (headless vim tooling), reasoning_depth (regex + zero-padding logic in ex mode), debugging_ambiguity (silent ex-mode failures), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (malformed near-miss rows; hidden corpora re-run the script fresh), and byte-for-byte equality. No dependency chain, no numeric aggregation, no environment pressure; totals bucket to medium.

hollow-atlas.notes: A chained git-lifecycle pipeline whose stages depend on each other in strict order: recover two branches from git bundles via HEAD/ref inspection, restore an off-branch stashed file onto feature-aurora and commit it, deploy each branch into an isolated directory that must not collide, sanitize a CI workflow (line-based, comment-aware, case-insensitive URL removal) in both a standalone and an in-repo copy, then stand up a bare repo served over SSH (dedicated OS user + authorized ed25519 key + running sshd) that must accept a clone AND a push. Every one of the five scaffolded competencies maps to a real deliverable and the reusable helpers (/app/bin/checkout.py, /app/bin/sanitize.py) are re-run on distinct hidden fixtures (fresh bundles with different branch names, and workflow files that probe comments-only/uppercase/edge URL placements), so generalization and malformed-input handling are exercised. The SSH component and the dependent fetch->recover->commit->deploy->sanitize->serve chain are why difficulty is hard (dependent_stages 3, tool_breadth 3, hidden_case_generalization 3, reasoning_depth 2, adversarial_inputs 2).

hollow-dial.notes: Hard bucket (18/30). Three machine/binary-level competencies bundled in one container, each with its own deliverable that the verifier independently re-executes. (1) C-a1a5f09e: classify a binary's kernel/format by reading header fields alone -- the hidden set spans a legacy PDP-11 a.out, a native x86-64 ELF, a foreign MIPS ELF, a truncated ELF (must not crash) and a plain-text file (must return unknown), so the classifier must generalise and degrade gracefully. (2) C-4f1f7a1d: author a faithful MIPS32 ELF interpreter in C (load segments, decode the instruction stream, emulate registers/memory, guest syscall ABI); the verifier recompiles /app/mips_interp.c from scratch and runs it on the visible sample plus four distinct hidden ELF programs (arithmetic+byte stores, data+counted loop, immediate exit, byte-load reverse loop) comparing stdout byte-for-byte, and on a hidden ELF containing an unsupported opcode that must be rejected (exit 3 + stderr) -- misemulated instructions fail. (3) C-90fab5c1: eval.py is an interpreter for the 'Liz' Lisp; the verifier runs each hidden target directly AND wired through a one-extra-level self-interpreter harness and requires byte-identical output, so the evaluator must implement closures/define/lambda/if/quote/begin/primitives and self-interpretation correctly. reasoning_depth 3 (two instruction emulators: MIPS decode/execute bus and a meta-circular Lisp evaluator), hidden_case_generalization 3 (three independent hidden suites), adversarial_inputs 2 (malformed/truncated/unsupported/div-by-zero cases), quantitative_correctness 3 (byte-exact output).

hollow-fathom.notes: Three independent, generalizable report-pipeline deliverables, each re-executed by the verifier on genuinely different hidden inputs: derive.py applies a dispersed numeric clue-rule recipe (add/sub/mul/div/mod, filename-ordered, with malformed skippable step files, negative bases, whitespace and non-step-file noise); diff_series.py averages per-key (not per-row-position) differences between two CSVs with side-aligned keys, duplicate/extra-key and no-common-key edges; report.jq + report_args.json (dash-form options) must re-run byte-for-byte and reproduce exact line ordering on feeds with dropped records, ties, malformed and empty-result cases. All arithmetic/ordering exact. Total 12 -> medium, consistent with the easy floors of all three competencies, driven by cross-deliverable dependent stages, tooling breadth (python + jq), adversarial/malformed input handling and hidden-case generalization.

hollow-keystone.notes: Hard bucket. The task chains five strict gates: (1) fix a C parsing bug in source so kvcat no longer short-circuits on the first malformed line; (2) the fix must free every allocation so valgrind reports zero definite leaks with no suppressions and no premature exit; (3) only /app/src/fixed.c may be touched while every other source/config file must stay byte-identical and no extra files may appear; (4) merge two divergent git branches resolving real config.toml and deps.txt conflicts under a documented dependency-merge rule; (5) leave reproducible /app/merged.diff and exact /app/deps.lock. Valgrind runs on the visible sample and four hidden token files (malformed lines interspersed, CRLF / missing trailing newline, leading-digit and malformed-value tokens, empty file, all-malformed) with exact byte-for-byte stdout comparison.

hollow-ledge.notes: Hard crypto-breach-recovery pipeline bundling four competencies that must ALL hold. (1) C-d9425275 easy/medium floor: the recovered username+password must land as /app/creds.txt with exact schema. (2) C-38bb2e3e hard: a deleted private key + certificate must be carved byte-exactly out of a length-prefixed (LVPR/LVCR) carrier into a clean dir that contains nothing else; the verifier re-runs the carve on a different carrier and byte-compares. (3) C-cf32bd95 hard: the agent must read /app/src/check.c, invert the bijective per-byte transform f(x)=((x*0x35+0x2f)^0xa5)&0xff (mod-256 inverse lookup) to turn the stored passhash fingerprint into a valid 12-byte printable secret; the verifier recompiles check.c and runs it on the recovered secret. (4) C-ce46ee62 medium: single-byte-key WAL recovery - find k by XOR-matching the native magic 37 7f 06 82, decode, restore ledge.db-wal, and read the un-checkpointed cfg rows. Difficulty is hard because three claimed competencies carry hard floors and the dependent_stages chain (decode wal -> read DB -> invert check -> carve -> concat key.pem -> write creds) means any single wrong byte/magic/path breaks the whole effort; quantitative_correctness matters for the byte-exact magic, byte-exact carve, and byte-exact key.pem concatenation; hidden cases re-run decode.bin unwal on a different-key WAL and carve on a different carrier (generalization). No unsafe actions demanded, no interaction statefulness.

hollow-notch.notes: Medium-bucket sysadmin task (total 13). A provisioning script must repair four stacked service faults on one host without systemd: name resolution + hostname (broken /etc/hosts, fragmented nsswitch, unqualified hostname), bring up three JVM daemon roles and a live RPC health report reflected in /app/status.json, and reconfigure postfix so the announcement list is delivered to local mailboxes instead of being relayed away. Difficulty comes from the dependency ordering (DNS and daemon liveness gate a healthy report), subtle root-cause of the hijacked relayhost, the need for persistent file-based fixes (not volatile shell state), idempotence under repeated verifier execution, and the hidden cases that re-run the deliverable against different site descriptors (different ports/hostnames/capacity) plus a malformed descriptor that must abort without side effects. The agent's own script must genuinely generalize across sites and leave durable configuration, matching the medium floors of the DNS, persistence, and list-mail competencies.

hollow-vane.documented_probe: C-5ef2ad28 (combine values from reference clues to produce an expected payload): the covering task exercises the capability at easy; the verifier executes the deliverable on hidden clue sets and compares the derived integer to a reference derivation, fully checking the capability.
hollow-vane.notes: Single-stage: reassemble a numeric recipe scattered across an env-style seed file, an inclusive date cutoff, and a journal of keyed operation entries; wrong arithmetic or wrong filtering yields a wrong payload. Generalization is probed by hidden clue sets (all-entries-filtered, malformed/junk files, missing seed/cutoff, numeric filename ordering, large and negative xor operands). Small rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (multi-artifact merge + date filter), adversarial_inputs, hidden_case_generalization, and quantitative_correctness (exact integer). Totals bucket to easy.

indigo-archive.documented_probe: C-96b1223d (decode a proprietary binary 3d model format into structured json): reference floor is hard but the covering task exercises it at medium; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases. Documented probe waiver.
indigo-archive.notes: Binary archive-volume parser tuned into a reusable tool. dependent_stages=2: header decode -> 32-byte record-table walk -> payload bounds checks -> CRC-32 validation -> UTF-8 decode -> SHA-256 evidence hashing is a real multi-step chain. reasoning_depth=2: the exact little-endian fixed-layout and the multiple independent validity gates (magic, status, length cap 4096, in-page and in-file bounds, CRC, UTF-8) must all be implemented precisely or hidden cases diverge. adversarial_inputs=2: hidden volumes include wrong magic, too-short files, out-of-bounds and >4096 payloads, bad CRCs, empty and all-tombstone tables, and zero/garbage slots. hidden_case_generalization=2: the program must run cleanly on 5 unseen volumes with different records and numbers. quantitative_correctness=2: exact JSON records and exact SHA-256 evidence hashes are compared byte-for-byte. Debugging ambiguity is mild (1) because endianness and CRC conventions can be misread, and the format is fully documented so nothing needs live exploration beyond stdlib. Medium bucket (total 11).

indigo-ember.notes: Chained recovery: decode a letter-substitution cryptogram with a clued alphabet mapping (C-03818c40), extract the passcode with end-of-note/punctuation edge cases, unlock an openssl key box, then decrypt EVERY ciphertext block with an ARX cipher and write one plaintext per line in order (C-9e5ae912). Reusable tool re-run on hidden scenarios with different notes, mappings, passcodes, keys, and bundle lengths; exported helpers are unit-probed. Nonzero dependent_stages (note -> passcode -> key -> plaintexts), reasoning_depth (ARX inverse + substitution semantics), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization, quantitative_correctness (byte-exact lines).

indigo-vault.notes: Two chained stages (dependent_stages=1): first crack a SHA-256 digest over a supplied wordlist on CPU, then use the recovered passphrase to unseal a ZipCrypto-encrypted ZIP member and parse the code= field into a JSON answer. Covers C-294e076f (crack the archive password via a CPU cracker over a recovered hash) at medium: a missed or wrong dictionary word leaves the digest uncracked and the archive sealed, failing the whole task. tool_breadth=1 (hasher + zip handling from a shell entry point), debugging_ambiguity=1 (a wrong digest compare, CRLF handling, or ZipCrypto check-byte failure manifests as an opaque Bad-password error). Generalization=2 because the verifier mints fresh hash/wordlist/archive triples with different passwords, member names, contents and code values and re-runs /app/crack.sh unchanged; adversarial_inputs=1 for CRLF/whitespace/case edges. Exact string answers give quantitative_correctness=1. No resource pressure; totals bucket to medium.

iris-anchor.documented_probe: (C-6f5a7578, MuJoCo tuning) The passive double-pendulum reference is intentionally friction/collision-free, so RK4-with-a-larger-aligned-timestep regenerates the reference joint trajectory to within a tiny tolerance at every admissible timestep; the trajectory-preservation constraint is therefore essentially free for any legal dt, and the genuine physics of the discipline to 'preserve the physics trajectory' is exercised but easy. The task earns medium difficulty from the block-manipulation path planner (arbitrary unseen grids, block stacking/movement rules) combined with three coupled deliverables, not from the physics fidelity knob.
iris-anchor.notes: Three competencies exercised to produce distinct deliverables: (1) an elevation- and stackable-block-aware path planner that must generalize to unseen hidden grids and always reach its goal; (2) a board-state decoder that reads a rendered game-board PNG into exact occupied intersections plus black/white stone ownership-ship (hidden decoded images included); (3) a MuJoCo model tuned by empirical simulation to run measurably faster while keeping the full sampled qpos trajectory within a strict tolerance. dependent_stages=2 reflects the planner->decode->tune chain and that the planner/decode deliverables are re-run by the grader on fresh hidden inputs. quantitative_correctness=2 because the decoder must exactly recover the occupied-cell set and the physics tolerance is a real numeric bound. standard hidden-case re-run across 3 grids and 2 images gives hidden_case_generalization=3.

iris-crate.documented_probe: C-3a4d0dcd (train a fasttext classifier to accuracy and size targets): covering task exercises the capability at hard difficulty - a fasttext-style hashed-n-gram linear classifier must be trained from scratch (pure stdlib, no sklearn) to clear a 0.88 sealed-holdout accuracy floor (0.85/0.80 on hidden corpora) while the serialized pickled model stays under a 2 MiB budget, with a pinned inference contract the verifier re-implements. Unlike the zephyr-bridge probe, there is no provided loader/embedding pipeline: the trainer, feature extractor, training loop, pruning to the size budget, malformed-row robustness and the pinned pickle model format are all authored by the agent, and the trainer is re-executed on hidden corpora with per-case floors.
iris-crate.notes: Hard capability: fitting a real text classifier that generalizes across four noisy classes (class pools + cross-class confusers + filler) under twin quantitative gates (accuracy floor on a sealed holdout, hard serialized-size cap). Nonzero rubric for quantitative_correctness (twin accuracy/size gates, metrics consistency with real file size), reasoning_depth (designing the training loop so it converges above the floor - underfit models measurably fail), adversarial_inputs (malformed rows must be skipped without crashing), hidden_case_generalization (fresh-seed and edge corpora re-run end to end), resource_pressure (2 MiB model budget), dependent_stages (trainer must exist and run before model.bin/metrics.json exist), debugging_ambiguity (stale or faked metrics/model_bytes fail), tool_breadth (pickle/zlib/json plumbing).

iris-ember.notes: Meeting-scheduling / ICS task. The implementer must (1) parse attendee availability minutes and find the EARLIEST conflict-free slot, emitting a standards-conformant iCalendar event for it, and (2) correctly apply recovery-buffer-after-late-meeting semantics when an occupied meeting ends at/after late_hour, in which case the effective occupied region is extended by buffer_after_late_min before the slot search, and (3) locate a provided per-person schedule producer tool, read its calling convention, and drive it to save one snapshot text file per attendee. hidden_case_generalization=3: the same /app/schedule.py is re-run by the verifier over fresh read-only availability sets (/tests/hidden/*) with distinct windows, durations, buffer sizes and degenerate inputs, and must independently reconstruct the same earliest DTSTART. reasoning_depth=2: the buffer rule changes the earliest slot only when the naive conflict-free choice falls within a recovery buffer (the evening-buffer hidden case forces 23:30 vs a naive 22:30), so an implementer who skips the recovery-buffer extension produces the wrong start. debugging_ambiguity=2: the malformed/overlapping/zero-length availability lines and the >= versus > boundary at exactly late_hour must be handled per the documented rule with no visibility into the hidden sets. dependent_stages=2: earliest-slot derivation feeds the ICS emission and the summary, and the personals are a separate discovery stage. Resource pressure is low, so the total sits in the medium bucket.

iris-ledge.notes: Hard bucket (sum 21). The whole task is a chained pipeline: build the guest first-boot, bring it up under software-only QEMU TCG (no KVM), mount a 9p virtfs host-root shared volume, chroot into it, compile a statically-linked inline-assembly program inside the emulated guest, run it to a known exit status, drive a parametric renderer loop to completion under simulation so it writes a first frame, then leave the emulator running as a persistent background service with a live monitor socket and a serial redirect that both accept external input. Hidden cases re-execute /app/run.sh on genuinely different scenarios (different exit status, frame dimensions, PRNG seed, and loopback ports), so run.sh must generalize rather than encode a single answer. Difficulty comes from dependent virtualization stages, background-service/socket statefulness, indirect guest-side failure diagnosis, and correctness that is exact (exit status integer, frame byte format). All four competencies meet or exceed their floors (C-01fe75ac is floor medium; C-3654b094, C-fc5cfb57, C-900a820e are floor hard), so documented_probe is null.

iris-quarry.notes: Forward-pass inference with learned weights: parse a plain-text weights bundle (dims from ARCH header, row-major slicing of W1/B1/W2/B2), execute tanh hidden layer + stable softmax output exactly, argmax with lowest-index tie-break. Generalizes to hidden pairs with different D/R/C, an empty samples file, and an exact logit tie. Nonzero rubric for the two-stage parse-then-compute chain, hidden generalization (three hidden cases), and quantitative correctness (exact labels plus probabilites within tolerance).

iris-terrace.notes: Hard three-part scientific/numerics task (drawn from three gap competencies). (1) Per-peak lorentzian fitting: crop each peak's local window and fit center/width/amplitude/offset with scipy curve_fit using sane starting values and bounds; recovered parameters must match true values to tolerance on fresh hidden spectra. (2) Separability-matrix compositing: a symbolic (non-sampling, non-astropy-internal) routine must produce the correct 0/1 separability matrix for nested/stacked (blocked & permuted) compound astropy models, where a naive 'everything-couples' compositing is the exact failure an agent without the competency hits; verified against an independent numerical Jacobian ground-truth and astropy's own reference. (3) sqrt-Wasserstein: reduce the plan<middle-dot>cost to a scalar, root-clamp to non-negative, and square-root so the returned value is the actual metric distance, not the unrooted squared cost. Reasoning depth (3): deriving the boolearn-matrix composition (block diagonal for stacking, product for chaining, permutation selection for Mapping) without evaluating the model. Debugging ambiguity (2): the fit tolerances / overlapping-peak windows and the separability dimension bookkeeping are only stated at a high level. Adversarial inputs (2): overlapping peaks and a small/malformed spectrum tax detection, while separator and Wasserstein hidden cases include permutations, nested blocks, degenerate zero plans and negative costs. Hidden-case generalization (3): three-plus distinct hidden scenarios across all three deliverables must run unchanged on mounted fixtures. Quantitative correctness (3): fitted peak parameters and the Wasserstein value must match independent computations to tight tolerance. Difficulty floor is hard per competency C-4e2bd7bd (separability compositing).

iron-lattice.notes: Medium. The core is a self-contained algorithm (power iteration) that must generalize to unseen matrices (1x1, diagonal, 2x2, 4x4) probed by hidden cases, which drives hidden_case_generalization = 2 and quantitative_correctness = 2. reasoning_depth = 2 comes from correctly handling convergence stopping, the all-ones degeneracy, eigenvalue estimation via Rayleigh quotient, and floating-point normalization. Resource pressure = 1 from a hard iteration bound and adversarial convergence (near-tied eigenvalues). Overall 11 -> medium bucket.

ivory-kiln.notes: Single competency C-a3b20c21 (transcribe an algorithm from a photograph of code): a rotated/noisy whiteboard photo of a parameterized checksum routine; OCR garbles at least one line per photo, so the constants must be read visually and the routine evaluated. Hidden cases are fresh photographs with different L/U/F/S/K constants and call argument n; any misread digit or operator yields a different integer and fails exact equality. Small rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (order-of-operations reconstruction), debugging_ambiguity (OCR noise must be worked around), adversarial_inputs (degraded photo), hidden_case_generalization (solve.py re-run on unseen photos), and quantitative_correctness (exact integer).

ivory-lantern.documented_probe: C-4f563c9d (fetch both model weights and tokenizer artifacts so offline loading succeeds; min difficulty medium): the task requires persisting every artifact the offline loader inspects (config, weights shard, vocab, merges, tokenizer_config, special_tokens_map) into one servable mirror, verified by an actual network-free load that returns working objects, plus the complete-mirror property (deleting any artifact must break the load) and hidden upstream trees (fresh, corrupted digest, missing source).
ivory-lantern.notes: Two-stage: write a generalized manifest-driven mirror builder, then run it to bake the visible mirror and prove the offline load. Medium floor from the complete-mirror discipline (atomic failure semantics, distractor files, digest verification) and hidden-case generalization over fresh/corrupt/missing upstream trees. No tool breadth, no environment pressure.

ivory-shoal.notes: Sequence design under a circular sliding-window composition constraint on an arbitrary named pair of bases (not just GC). Hard elements: circular wrap-around windows must satisfy the range (period-block tiling is the clean construction), an exact feasible-count k must be derived from fractional percentage bounds, plus secondary constraints (all four bases present, homopolymer runs capped at 4 including the seam) that break naive two-letter tilings. The verifier re-executes the designer on three hidden parameter cases with fresh lengths/windows/bounds/pairs and scans every window with exact rational arithmetic.

jade-shard.notes: Medium. Requires authoring a reusable CLI that (1) computes an exact contiguous three-way even split (offset/count arithmetic) of a row-major tensor, (2) emits a SHA-256 integrity manifest, (3) reconstructs and independently re-verifies shape, count and checksum in join mode, and (4) rejects several classes of malformed inputs (count mismatch, negative dimension, missing key, non-int values). Hidden cases force generalization across non-divisible counts, multi-dim shapes, N<3/N==0 empties, and negative values; the join path must reconstruct hidden tensors byte-for-byte. Moderate reasoning depth (split arithmetic + verify invariants) and adversarial/hidden generalization push it to the low end of medium; no resource or interaction pressure.

juniper-bridge.documented_probe: Documented probe waiver: C-b2fceb71 (feature matching + robust geometric model fits) has reference evidence at hard floor, but the v2 covering task exercises it at medium difficulty only. The verifier still fully checks the capability (hidden correspondence sets, degenerate cases); raising the task bucket would duplicate the photogrammetry family rather than add distinct coverage.
juniper-bridge.notes: Medium. One reusable CLI tool (/app/solve.py, strict <in_dir> <out_dir>) must (a) OCR a 9x9 digit-grid image into an exact numeric lattice, (b) render two arbitrary OCR-readable rasters, (c) render the recovered print-path and OCR a phrase off it, (d) transcribe the numeric parameters of a photographed Python algorithm and evaluate it, (e) isolate the all-caps secret token from OCR'd prose, (f) parse a plotter tool-path into its drawn primitives and dedeced its SEAL-encoded label, and (g) run three robust geometric-model fits (RANSAC line, ORB+homography, rigid) over noisy correspondence datasets. The verifier re-runs solve.py on the pristine visible fixture plus three fresh hidden scenarios (hardcoded shapes, degenerate zero-area primitives, heavy-outlier feature sets, distinct numeric literals and phrases) and compares every deliverable: exact digit lattice, exact secret/word/value/shape equality, inlier counts within tolerance, and that the two rasters and the recovered print-path are re-read correctly by OCR. Difficulty comes from hidden_case_generalization (re-run over 4 scenarios each feeding the fits and OCR), tool_breadth (Tesseract + OpenCV + NumPy + Pillow coordination), dependent_stages (a long shared pipeline whose intermediates feed later stages), and debugging_ambiguity (OCR/image noise and noisy correspondence are only correct when every stage behaves). No system services or dangerous actions.
