juniper-gasket.documented_probe: C-7210274e (meet a threshold accuracy on a held-out test set): second independent covering task. Fit a sklearn classifier on a training CSV so a strictly held-out test CSV classifies at or above the stated accuracy floor (0.85), persist a reloadable pickled model and metrics, and generalize to hidden cases with different seeds/sizes whose own floors are enforced by re-executing the deliverable. Easy: well-separated classes, single-stage fit, generous floor.
juniper-gasket.notes: Distinct from cedar-pier (hydra-configured logistic trainer with sign-constrained coefficients and pipeline hardening): here the contract is a minimal data-driven CLI fit + persist + threshold check. The verifier never trusts the reported metrics: it unpickles the model, recomputes holdout accuracy against the case floor, checks metric consistency, and re-runs the deliverable on hidden cases. Rubric is small: single-stage fit, one floor, hidden replays, quantitative correctness on the threshold comparison.

juniper-hollow.notes: Two-stage: build a triage program, then run it on the fixtures to emit alert.json and report.json. Reasoning: rule firing vs statistics (all rules reported, only firing ones alerted), dedup+sort of ips, deterministic event scan order. Adversarial: hidden rule sets probe missing/non-string patterns, invalid regexes, defaulted thresholds/severities, threshold 0 always firing, non-object rules, an invalid-JSON rules file yielding empty structures, and empty logs. Quantitative: exact match counts and schema keys.

juniper-latch.documented_probe: C-56dccd5f (keep the rest of the repository unmodified): this task is the covering exercise at medium difficulty; the verifier sha256-checks every file except the single sanctioned windowing.py against the release manifest and fails outright on any other byte change.
juniper-latch.notes: Single-sanctioned-file hotfix: repair the windowing math (zero-padding head bug, off-by-one window, wrong rounding decimals, tie-down quantization) while the checksum manifest pins every other package file, including the frozen constants that would be the tempting shortcut. Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth/debugging_ambiguity (multiple interacting defects, spec restated), adversarial_inputs (tamper temptation via constants.py), hidden_case_generalization (three distinct hidden telemetry files), quantitative_correctness (exact 4-decimal floats and rungs).

juniper-ledge.notes: Medium (sum 13). A multi-stage chained audit-and-exercise flow over a live in-container Flask service: read the vendored framework to locate both the concatenated-login-query SQL-injection sink (auth.py -> auth_login) and the from_string template-rendering sink (rendering.py -> render_user_copy); obtain a genuinely admin-privileged session (the admin password is withheld, so the authenticated token only comes from exercising the injection); present the token on admin-gated ledgers/retire routes (real DB mutation verified); then compute the documented rendezvous payload and POST it, verifying the returned final message survives hidden fresh ledger ids plus unknown/malformed-id negatives. Carried by dependent_stages, stateful HTTP sessions, hidden-case generalization, and reasoning about where each weakness lives; no heavy compute or resource pressure (single small Flask server). Max competency floor among the four claims is medium (C-19c9cfba, framework SSTI location), matching the difficulty bucket.

juniper-mesh.documented_probe: C-bb7cec38 (fit a parametric bayesian network over the discovered structure): covered at hard difficulty; the verifier independently recomputes the discovery rule and exact OLS fit and enforces KS tolerance (<=0.04) plus cross-column dependence checks on the resampled data.
juniper-mesh.notes: Three chained stages: deterministic structure discovery (thresholded correlation over a declared topological order), exact multiple-OLS parametric fit of every conditional (intercept, per-parent partial slopes, population residual std), and seeded ancestral sampling. The verifier re-runs the solver on three hidden data sets with different variables/orders/thresholds, recomputes edges and the OLS fit from the data, runs per-column two-sample KS tests against the true generating process, checks that discovered-edge correlations survive in the synthetic data, and requires byte-identical reruns. Rubric weights dependent_stages (sampling depends on fit depends on discovery), reasoning_depth (partial slopes vs pairwise, ddof=0), hidden_case_generalization, and quantitative_correctness; totals bucket to hard.

juniper-notch.notes: Medium messaging-queue-socket relay task (Juniper Notch). The agent is handed an unauthenticated loopback MQ bus (mosquitto on :31883), a relay worker (/app/relay/worker.py) that consumes retained 'rebalance' directives from topic juniper/jobs, and a raw-TCP survey gate (/app/relay/gate.py on :43979) speaking a MAP/SURVE text protocol. To succeed the agent must (1) discover the endpoints and protocol from /app/relay/station.toml and README.md, (2) craft /app/job.json matching the worker's exact schema and publish it retain=true via an MQTT client (paho) so the worker later consumes it (C-8dfb1620 queue injection, C-bc9fd958 unauthenticated-broker discovery/exploitation, C-5bf90775 protocol messaging), and (3) drive a structured socket request-response: connect, send MAP, read the JSON map, compute the nearest site by Manhattan distance with a documented tie-break, send SURVE <site>, and write the parsed site reply to /app/roundtrip.out (C-670b820b socket protocol + position parsing). The verifier re-executes the deliverable q.py on hidden inputs: a fresh unseen directive (generalized publish), a different unseen map (live re-survey proving roundtrip.out is computed, not hardcoded), and a malformed directive that must be rejected without crashing the worker. Difficulty comes from dependent_stages (bus + worker + gate + python tool must interoperate), interaction_statefulness (background broker/gate a live MQTT worker; multi-turn socket dialog), hidden_case_generalization (new directives and maps), and reasoning/quantitative correctness (schema crafting digits and the nearest-site computation incl. tie-breaks).

juniper-pier.notes: Hard (bucket 18+) because the highest competency floor (rstan/pystan posterior-sampling workflow, C-ed60d55a) is hard. The agent must (1) port an rstan sampling configuration faithfully to PyStan's num_warmup/num_samples/num_chains semantics (the classic warmup-vs-total misallocation bug would bias posterior means), (2) run a deterministic multi-chain NUTS sampler that compiles live via httpstan within the wall-clock budget and persists posterior means/draws that recover the data-generating parameters, and (3) select a lasso regularization penalty corroborated across cross-validation and a corrected (AICc) information criterion while keeping a distinct ridge variant. Quantitative correctness drives most of the score (posterior means must land inside tolerances on the default AND on hidden datasets; the chosen penalty must reproduce under an independent re-derivation on holdouts), plus hidden-case generalization because the verifier re-runs both the sampler and the penalty selector on unseen datasets and cross-checks the reported penalty against an independent computation.

juniper-quill.notes: Hard (19/30). Difficulty comes from a long multi-stage pipeline that must generalize: reverse a 4-byte repeating XOR whose key is detected from the SQLite WAL header magic, recover the intact rows, apply in-database cleaning (lowercase, cast digits-only value to integer, drop rows with neither contact field, dedup by id under a total order), export byte/semantic-exact JSON + 20 per-trial CSVs that must equal the cleaned table, reclaim an unlinked-but-open fd via /proc, and hit a measured query-performance gate that fails any correct-but-unindexed solution. Hidden cases vary the transform key (including a zero key and a single-byte key), row counts (down to a 35-row edge basket), duplicate ids, rows missing both contacts, and leading-zero values. A correct agent that skips the WAL, the dedup order, the CSV/db consistency, the fd, or the index all fail distinct verifier gates. Max competency floor (C-6ef56211) is hard, so no probe is needed.

juniper-upland.notes: Medium. One reusable CLI (/app/schedule.py) must scan attendee availability minutes for the earliest conflict-free UTC slot, honour a recovery buffer around any late-ending block (>= late_hour_utc, expanded both before and after), and emit a standards-conformant ICS while leaving inputs untouched; the same program is then re-run on four hidden scenario directories. Separately the agent must discover a provided per-member roster helper under /app/kit, learn its calling convention, and save each member's stdout byte-for-byte into /app/personals/<name>.txt. Difficulty comes from hidden_case_generalization (the verifier re-executes the program on four adversarial scenarios probing free-window/malformed blocks, a buffer-forcing late block, the inclusive clock-time <= boundary, and a missing attendee file), quantitative_correctness (exact UTC earliest start must match a brute-force ground truth, byte-equal snapshots), adversarial_inputs (malformed VEVENTs, absent per-member files, boundary minutes), and reasoning_depth (buffer expansion around late blocks and the wind-down-before/next-meeting semantics). No system services or unsafe actions.

juniper-wharf.documented_probe: The 'large' training set is delivered as a handful of modest parquet splits (a few KB each, ~2k combined rows in the visible fixture) rather than gigabytes. The competency exercised — reaching an S3-object endpoint over the loopback HTTP socket, enumerating a manifest, retrieving every split by key, SHA-256 verifying each object, validating the parquet schema, and assembling train/val/test locally — is preserved identically; only the byte volume is scaled down to fit the 4 GB storage / ~5-minute build limits of a single lean container.
juniper-wharf.notes: Hard. Four independent infrastructure artifacts each pull in a distinct toolchain (grpc_tools proto codegen + a live gRPC round-trip on the schema; cryptography/SAN + strict ISO-8601 expiry formatting for certcheck; anonymous S3-style object retrieval + SHA-256 integrity + parquet assembly for download; an HTTP Basic-auth default-credential mint probe that must produce honest response). Each stage depends on reading a live service the harness starts (dependent_stages 3): codegen, cert, object-store and control head. Debugging ambiguity is high (anonymous S3 access, exact ISO date formatting, gRPC stub generation/import, handling sealed endpoints). Hidden-case generalization is high: the same four binaries are re-run on 3 hidden scenarios with different buckets/columns/row counts, different certs (different CNs/lifespans), and different control-head credential pairs incl. a sealed (rotated) case that must be reported reachable=false. Quantitative-correctness covers SHA-256 equality, split row counts, and exact ISO dates. Adversarial_inputs captures the sealed control head and cert changelog. unsafe_action_penalty is 0 because the default-credential probe is an authorized benchmark scenario on a loopback-only fixture, not a real system.

juniper-yonder.notes: Hard. One reusable tool /app/attack.py must (a) run a chosen-plaintext differential/key-recovery attack against a hidden-key reduced-cipher oracle binary (/app/workspace/yonder_enc) and pin the two low-bit round keys k0,k1, (b) decrypt every ciphertext into one plaintext line each, (c) decode base64-obfuscated filenames, (d) decode a substitution cryptogram from the clued mapping to recover a passcode and an isolated secret word, (e) run the installed AES-256-CBC CLI (openssl) over every file in a source tree mirroring the tree to encsrc/, and (f) persist the secret with exact normalization (/app/name.txt). The verifier re-runs attack.py on the pristine visible workspace plus three fresh hidden scenarios (new keys, messages, source trees, dotfiles/empty files, uppercase secrets, symbol/digit ciphertext messages, varied base64 names) and checks: exact recovered key, exact per-line plaintexts, normalized secret, decoded name set, and that every source file encrypts and decrypts back byte-identical with the recovered passcode. It also imports /app/attack.py and confirms recover_key() recovers the key from an encrypt callback. Difficulty comes from dependent_stages (a long shared pipeline whose stages feed one another), hidden_case_generalization (three hidden re-runs), reasoning_depth (reverse-engineering the reduced cipher and implementing differential key recovery), tool_breadth (Python + openssl CLI + base64 + subprocess oracle), and quantitative_correctness (exact keys/plaintext/name). No system services or dangerous actions.

keel-bight.documented_probe: C-a4cb7c45 (emit plan records in the required schema): the covering task is authored at hard, matching the reference floor; the verifier strictly deserializes every emitted record (exact ordered key lists id/batch/shape and capacity/days/code/vessel, float-vs-int type checks, compact re-serialization) on the visible and all hidden inputs.
keel-bight.notes: Hard: a strict-schema record emitter. The downstream deserializer breaks on any wrong key, wrong key order, wrong JSON type (capacity must be a float, days an int), or non-compact structure, so the agent must implement the exact contract. Nonzero rubric: reasoning_depth (three-rule shape derivation plus a five-key aggregation summary), adversarial_inputs (boolean-as-number, float transit_days, uppercase priority, unparseable/truncated JSON, non-object JSON, duplicate keys, blank lines), hidden_case_generalization (three hidden files incl. empty and all-invalid), quantitative_correctness (exact counts, rounding, batch tallies), debugging_ambiguity (a long contract with several interlocking invalid-line rules), dependent_stages (program must be written, then run, to produce the two visible deliverables). No tool breadth, no resource pressure, no unsafe actions; totals bucket to hard.

kelp-fjord.notes: C-409f50fe (gpg-encrypt an archive and remove plaintext intermediates): build a reusable sealing script that snapshots a live export tree deterministically (sorted tar, fixed mtime, gzip -n) under /tmp only, seals it with gpg --symmetric --cipher-algo AES256 --s2k-digest-algo SHA512 using a passphrase file, records the strongest cipher discovered from `man gpg`, and removes every plaintext intermediate. The verifier decrypts with the live passphrase, confirms OpenPGP packet cipher 9 and byte-identical extraction, scans /app and /tmp for leftovers, then reruns the script on hidden mutations (changed/added files including a nested directory and two different passphrases).

kelp-notch.notes: Medium (sum 7). The mailing-list mapping must be declared in the canonical postfix virtual-alias file at the exact fixed path /etc/postfix/virtual, registered in main.cf (virtual_alias_maps/virtual_alias_domains), compiled with postmap, and summarized in a JSON manifest. Adversarial requirements: specs tolerate comments/blank lines/padded whitespace, the list domain is derived from the spec (hidden specs use different domains), and re-provisioning must replace the previous mapping so stale addresses no longer resolve (append-only or wrong-path configs fail). Delivered as an idempotent executable provisioning script the verifier re-runs on hidden specs.

kelp-quill.documented_probe: Documented probe waiver: C-2d0e9195 (generate and protect a 2048-bit rsa private key) reference floor is medium; this task exercises the capability directly at medium via policy-driven provisioning plus a reusable key-inspection tool, rather than plum-seal's certificate-centric scenario.
kelp-quill.notes: Medium security provisioning: generate a fresh 2048-bit unencrypted RSA key to a written policy (exact file/dir modes 0600/0700/0644), emit the matching SPKI public key, and author a reusable PEM key-inspection tool. Dependent stage: key must exist before the report can be produced. Hidden cases generalize the tool across RSA 1024/4096, an encrypted (passphrase-protected) key (algorithm/bits/fingerprint null), EC P-256, Ed25519, and an unparseable file (non-zero exit). Quantitative correctness: exact bit sizes, exact fingerprint hex, exact modes. Freshness guard ensures the deployed key is genuinely generated, not copied.

kestrel-bay.documented_probe: C-4b78df73 (run a multi-process distributed training function under the gloo backend): the program must spawn N rank-aware worker processes joined by a gloo CPU process group, move shards into float32 CPU tensors, all-reduce sufficient statistics, and emit per-rank markers plus an aggregated fit. The verifier re-runs the deliverable with hidden worker counts (including more workers than rows, so idle ranks must still join and write markers) and hidden datasets, checking backend identity, exact round-robin shard sizes, and agreement with an independent serial least-squares reference.
kestrel-bay.notes: Hard: process-group initialization, spawn guard, rendezvous hygiene, rank-aware sharding (round-robin, including zero-row ranks), explicit device/dtype movement, and collective reduction must all work simultaneously or the run hangs or produces wrong artifacts. Verifier executes the deliverable on three hidden datasets with 3/5/7 workers and checks fit.json against a serial reference plus per-rank marker fidelity.

kestrel-loop.documented_probe: C-04cd9bdd (run a speculative draft-and-verify loop against a target sequence): the covering task exercises the competency directly at medium difficulty; the verifier executes the delivered loop on five hidden cases (K=1, K-overrun with partial match, all-accepted draft-greedy target, tie-broken argmax rows, empty target) and compares result, all counters, and every block record.
kestrel-loop.notes: Single-stage: implement the draft-and-verify acceptance loop over a JSON dual-logits model (draft argmax without bias; target compared positionally up to first mismatch; corrected target token appended on rejection). The trap is off-by-one logic in acceptance/context updates, which the hidden cases expose via exact counters and per-block records. Small rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (loop invariants + tie-breaking), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (distinct models, K values, empty/overrun targets), and quantitative_correctness (exact integer counters and block lists). No tool breadth, no dependency chain, no environment pressure; totals bucket to medium.

kestrel-vault.notes: Interactive-process work: drive a pipe-based game through a text protocol (look/search/take/place/seal), capture the scenario-specific ending, and exit via the game's normal quit command so session state and events flush to SQLite. Killing, aborting, or EOFing the game writes nothing, so a clean exit path is mandatory. Rubric peaks on interaction_statefulness (spawned-process protocol, turn-by-turn state tracking) and unsafe_action_penalty (premature kill leaves the db unwritten); nonzero for dependent_stages, tool_breadth (subprocess pipes + sqlite inspection), reasoning_depth (generic parsing of scenario-specific containers/gems), debugging_ambiguity, and hidden_case_generalization (fresh scenarios with different shapes). Totals bucket to medium.

kiln-anchor.documented_probe: C-1a4b2841 (place the built binary on the shell PATH; min difficulty medium): the agent authors a C CLI against a strict parsing contract, compiles it to /app/dist/kilnstat, and must additionally install it so bare-name invocation works from any directory in a non-login shell (the verifier runs from /tmp via sh -c and checks command -v). A source deliverable is independently recompiled and re-run, and hidden logs probe the parser (clock bounds, exponent/negative/dot-fraction forms, junk tokens, zero-valid and missing-file cases).
kiln-anchor.notes: Medium: author + compile + PATH-install chain (three dependent stages), adversarial token grammar (strtod vs junk, strict clock bounds), hidden generalization through executed binaries, and quantitative correctness on the six-line summary compared to an independent recomputation. No resource pressure.

kiln-cipher.notes: Agent must build a reusable provisioning tool that generates an RSA key + matching self-signed certificate and emits a combined PEM bundle (key block first, certificate second) plus a DER-sha256 fingerprint, with correct file modes, then run it for the visible identity. Verifier executes /app/mkcert.py on hidden (cn, bits, out-dir) cases and validates every bundle with openssl: block order/count, standalone parse of each block, key/cert public-key match, CN match, key size, 0600 modes, fingerprint. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (PEM concatenation order + armor), tool_breadth (openssl subprocess plumbing), debugging_ambiguity (bundle parse pitfalls), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (unseen CNs, both key sizes, missing out-dir), quantitative_correctness (exact fingerprint digest, mode bits), dependent_stages (key -> cert -> bundle -> fingerprint).

kiln-journal.notes: Single-stage: restore a recovered SQLite WAL under the expected -wal name beside a writable copy of the database and let SQLite auto-replay the committed journal on open, yielding the full merged record set (baseline plus appended/updated/deleted rows). The verifier re-executes the solver on four hidden scenarios (appends-only, mixed update+delete+append, no-journal, many appends) and enforces the no-modify rule on inputs. Rubric nonzero for hidden_case_generalization (four distinct scenarios), reasoning_depth/debugging_ambiguity (WAL placement mechanics: journal must be renamed to <db>-wal, replay needs a writable scratch area, closing checkpoints), adversarial_inputs (no-modify hashing, missing-journal edge), quantitative_correctness (exact merged rows), dependent_stages (solve.py -> merged.db/merged.json).

kiln-vane.notes: Single deliverable function: fold a 2x2 tile into a 6x6 swatch via 3x3 tiling, a per-row horizontal circular shift (right by (r+1)%3) and a per-column vertical circular shift (up by (c+2)%3). Must be implemented generally; the verifier executes the module's CLI and its imported weave() on hidden tiles including uniform and sparse tiles, where wrong shift directions or offsets mismatch. Small rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (three ordered composable steps), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (multiple hidden tiles), and quantitative_correctness (exact integer grids). No tool breadth, no dependency chain, no environment pressure; totals bucket to easy.

kite-anchor.notes: hard bucket (sum 18). Multiple independent sub-problems bound by exact contracts: cross-compiling hop.c to a little-endian MIPS ELF that must reproduce native 32-bit-wraparound checksums when run under qemu-user-static; rewriting a g95-frontend Makefile to gfortran with the module-compiled-before-program invariant; a C/C++ polyglot proven under both toolchains; a C CLI whose particle positions/summary/stdout must match a Python reference byte-for-byte; an autoregressive arg-max sampler whose stdout must equal an external Python launcher's reference (32-bit wrap + non-negative modulo equality between C and Python); a release-key file that stays valid when the host recompiles the sampler from source (recompile independence, guarded against tampered binaries); and a metacircular Scheme-Lite evaluator (env chains, closures, eval/apply). hidden tails probe mips boards, fortran angles, launch (len,seed), extra seeds, cli counts, and two scheme programs.

kite-helix.notes: A five-component archive/filesystem pipeline in one Python program (solve.py) driven from a workspace dir and generalized over hidden inputs. (1) list-archive-members-to-surface-token: the manifest.zip holds several near-identical config.yaml members at different logical paths plus decoy tokens; only the exact path manifest/release/current/config.yaml carries the real app_token, so choosing the wrong member yields a different token and fails the content check. (2) exclude-path-patterns during packaging: out/release.zip must drop vendor/ and __pycache__ dirs, any *.pyc/.o/.tmp/.cache file, and restricted-permission files (mode 000), while precision probes like vendor.py / tool.o.txt (which only look like exclusions) must be kept. (3) deep.tar.gz must carry the relative symlink intact (not dereferenced) and must not truncate deeply nested or >100-char-long member names (PAX). (4) mirror tree: every *.dat.gz under mirror_src is decompressed into out/mirror/ under its original basename. (5) answer.json must contain the token and the exact per-file sha256 map of every file under data/hash, and the source tree must remain byte-for-byte unchanged (source-modification check fails on any mutation). hidden_case_generalization=3: three genuinely different fixtures (different tokens/names, spaces in names, deeper nesting, varied package/arbitrary member sets) are re-run through /app/solve.py. debugging_ambiguity=2: near-duplicate archive paths, decoy tokens, and exclusion-rule precision probes force reading member lists rather than guessing. Medium bucket (total 14).

kite-mesa.notes: Hard single-competency RL training task for C-f49d1fc8: implement a wall-aware gridworld with asymmetric transition semantics (boundary bounce -> -1, wall bump -> -5, inclusive euclidean dock disc -> +10), train a policy to a high mean-return threshold via finite-horizon value iteration, and expose a documented seeded evaluation interface. Hard because the policy must genuinely reach a near-optimal mean return (thresholds sit ~3-5% under the exact DP optimum computed per layout, far above any undirected behavior), the module must be both importable and CLI-runnable, and hidden layouts (different sizes, rack geometries, radii, horizons) re-exercise everything through the agent's own code with an independent reference simulation. Reasoning depth, hidden-case generalization and quantitative correctness dominate; a wall/resource-pressure rubric entry reflects the bump-penalty dynamics and the CPU train+evaluate budget. Totals bucket to hard.

kite-summit.notes: Total 20 (hard bucket). Three genuinely independent, must-pass deliverable groups. (1) A 32-bit arithmetic SSA circuit built by hand (subtraction-based integer sqrt plus fast-doubling Fibonacci, all reduced mod 2^32) that must evaluate exactly on randomized hidden 32-bit vectors AND fit inside a hard 600-node-line ceiling, so a solver that hashes a lookup table or over-unrolls fails the size cap; this alone is reasoning_depth>=2. (2) A from-scratch literal/back-reference encoder that must keep each output under a strict byte ceiling strictly below the all-literal 2-bytes-per-byte cost, using dynamic programming over LZ segmentation, with hidden blobs hitting long-distance matches, RLE/overlap runs, and mostly-incompressible regions - naive or over-conservative tokenization exceeds the ceiling and the decode-must-equal-original check fails. (3) a footprint discipline deliverable gated on an independent size measurement of the global site-packages tree (a heavy pip install like scipy/torch pushes current size past the parsed-limit bound and fails).

kite-yonder.notes: A five-component native C/C++ stack: (1) a plain-C JSON weight parser plus exact integer transformer forward pass doing arg-max autoregressive decoding and continue feeding output back (reasoning_depth=3; any transposition/off-by-one changes the continuation), (2) a C++11-strict constexpr template port of a post-C++11 header (debugging_ambiguity=2 - subtle relaxed-constexpr constructs), (3) a Makefile with serial + OpenMP (pgen) targets verified to actually thread and match checksums, (4) a CMake build that emits per-TU LLVM IR and links unified.bc exposing all symbols, and (5) a ctypes binding with a deliberately mismatched buffer length. dependent_stages=3: parse JSON -> build in-memory tensors -> forward pass -> argmax decode, plus the cmake/llvm-link pipeline. adversarial_inputs=2 and hidden_case_generalization=3: hidden weights with different dims/prompts/gen-length plus malformed JSON, ragged matrices, missing keys, out-of-range tokens, negative length, and hidden (N,x) C++11 cases must all behave exactly. quantitative_correctness=2: token sequences and constexpr sums are byte/int exact, sim checksums must match serial vs OMP. resource_pressure=1: OpenMP thread count plus a wide run-time speed band (single-core tolerant). Hard bucket (total 18).

larch-cipher.documented_probe: Two competencies are exercised lean but faithfully. C-07c78691 (evaluate a trained policy deterministically under a fixed-seed environment): instead of full RL tooling, the 'environment' is a fixed-seed reward-collection loop over the held-out pool whose mean reward must be byte-for-byte reproducible across re-runs; the trained classifier is the 'policy' and its seeded mean reward is the artifact, and the verifier re-runs the evaluation and asserts identical values. C-4c743935 (LoRA adapter loadable via from_pretrained): the transformers/peer HF stack is not installed by design; the adapter directory persists weights + config with a small self-contained loader that reconstructs the Net (sequence classifier) exactly as from_pretrained would, so the persisted-reloadable-adapter semantics are preserved while the HF entry point is replaced by an equivalent local one.
larch-cipher.notes: The chain is: (1) diagnose the stalled classifier from the recorded training signals + module inspection (frozen / zero-initialised output layer -> loss flat at ln2, head gradient norm 0, val acc stuck at chance) -> (2) apply the one fix (unfreeze + re-initialise the designated output layer) and fine-tune ONLY that head while freezing fc1/fc2 (exact-match against the base enforces 'only the head may differ') -> (3) LoRA adapter trained on the frozen fc2, saved as a reloadable adapter dir, merged into the base (verifier recomputes fc2 == base + BA*scale) -> (4) persist every model/array as state-dict pickle, npy and an sklearn pickle -> (5) deterministic fixed-seed reward collection. hidden_case_generalization=3: the same /app/finetune.py must run on 4 hidden fixtures (different dims/seed) and each must clear the accuracy/freeze/merge/exact-keys thresholds; quantitative_correctness=3: exact-key set equality, frozen-only-head exact-match, merged-fc2 exact equality to base+LoRA, and reproducibility exact-equality of the seeded re-eval. adversarial_inputs=2: the detection that the head is frozen (head gradient 0) is only discoverable by inspecting recorded signals+module and must not be hardcoded per case. difficulty is achieved through correctness/diagnosis, not prompt length or timeouts.

larch-dial.notes: Medium. The task is a multi-step downstream which must (a) follow a strict four-argument CLI with no hard-coded fixture paths, (b) reuse only the preinstalled packages (pure stdlib plus pytest), (c) keep the gzip-compressed source under a 2400-byte ceiling, (d) rewrite a subordinate include by swapping only permitted synonym tokens while keeping the frame and synonym list byte-identical and rendering a compiled inlined output, and (e) keep the emitted report sequence inside the cap.txt length ceiling (the 64-hex digest, not the raw expansion). A partial/naive solver fails: botching the substitution, the immutability, or the source-size/length caps, or any non-stdlib import, is caught by the verifier; the fresh hidden fixture sets generalize the edit and the numeric scoring paths. Difficulty derives from hidden_case_generalization (re-run on 3 fresh fixture trees), adversarial_inputs (punctuation-attached synonym tokens, malformed CSV rows, empty data), debugging_ambiguity (the pytest suite only goes green when the edit/rendering is correct), and reasoning_depth (co-ordinating substitution, rendering, scoring and the two caps into one reusable CLI tool). Low resource pressure, no flagrantly dangerous actions.

larch-ember.documented_probe: C-05d7fbec (exploit a misconfigured sudo rule to run a privileged command): covered here at medium; the verifier degrades the box into several hidden starting states and re-executes the deliverable, requiring the seals to be minted through the ops->sudo->sealctl path (journal proves sudo_user=ops) with idempotent convergence.
larch-ember.notes: Single-deliverable hardening script plus report. The sudo rule is intentionally narrow (one binary) and the vault is root-only, so the only viable elevation path is the configured rule. Rubric credits the multi-tool sysadmin work (sudo/runuser/sealctl), stateful convergence from degraded hidden states, adversarial stale/corrupt fixtures, and exact end-state correctness.

larch-fathom.notes: Medium. A multi-stage data-tier task: bring a Postgres service up from nothing without systemd (pg_createcluster/pg_ctlcluster), provision app role + database + grants, create a customers table to a prescribed schema, load messy CSVs, and then perform the data cleaning entirely through SQL (lowercase+trim email, digit-only phone, dedupe keeping earliest by (email,phone), delete rows missing both contact fields), persisting load.sql/clean.sql evidence. On top of that the solver must craft and EXERCISE a SQL-injection payload against a naive auth query to authenticate as the admin role, and generate importable grpc python bindings from an arbitrary proto. The verifier re-runs the same /app/solve.py on fresh hidden CSVs (edge/malformed contact rows, dedupe collapse) and fresh protos (renamed packages/services, stream RPCs, enum, oneofes) plus a malformed-proto case that must exit non-zero. Difficulty comes from dependent_stages (each later stage depends on the live DB/schema being correct), debugging_ambiguity (postgres bring-up, role/db grants, connection auth, generated-binding imports), hidden_case_generalization (re-run unchanged on fresh fixtures), and reasoning_depth (coordinating SQL cleaning, auth bypass and generic codegen in one undisciplined CLI tool). One container, no GPU/systemd/X; resource pressure is mild.

larch-hearth.documented_probe: Overall bucket is hard (sum 21) from the chained emulated-guest pipeline: author a tool ISO, inject a boot init that mounts the cdrom and the 9p host root, boot a real kernel under software-only QEMU TCG (no KVM), compile and run a statically-linked inline-assembly program inside the guest to an exact exit status, drive a no-password serial login, leave the emulator running as a background service, and generalize across genuinely different hidden scenarios. C-9e0d7397 (system-call/file-io emulation) has a 'hard' reference floor; here the guest reaches the host filesystem through the 9p shared host-root mount so host-fs syscall writes are more direct than a from-scratch syscall interpreter, so that one competency is intentionally easier than its floor while the other four meet or exceed their medium floors.
larch-hearth.notes: All five competencies are exercised for real in a live emulated guest. Difficulty comes from dependent emulation stages (ISO -> boot -> cdrom mount -> in-guest compile -> login), background-service/serial-interaction statefulness, headless-Guest failure diagnosis, and exact correctness (exit status integer, exact payload string in the ISO manifest echoed over the console). matches the hard bucket; documented_probe explains the single sub-floor competency.

larch-jetty.notes: Medium (total 11). The task consolidates five unrelated parsing/transformation slices into one /app/solve.py + answer.json contract. Difficulty is spread across hidden_case_generalization (2): the verifier runs the produced program against three distinct unseen datasets, so hardcoding the visible rows/files fails every hidden case. adversarial_inputs (2): edge inputs include >5 categories with a rank-5/rank-6 tie, unparseable amounts ('N/A', empty), invalid IPv4 (octet>255, leading zeros, IPv6), multiple dates per line (rightmost wins), ICS events missing DTEND (skipped), and exact-boundary overlap probes (half-open). quantitative_correctness (2): category ranking must sum absolute amounts and select exactly the top five in strict order. reasoning_depth (2) for binding the IP validity + last-date rule and the half-open interval semantics; debugging_ambiguity (1) and tool_breadth (2) for mixing csv/ics/regex/json in one pipeline. No resource pressure or statefulness: single self-contained script over small fixtures.

larch-terrace.notes: Cross-compiler toolchain lab. reasoning_depth=3: the arg-max autoregressive sampler must reproduce a documented deterministic integer transformer forward pass (embedding -> relu MLP -> logits -> first-max tie-break) fed back over a context, encoded modularly in plain C, and the polyglot requires constructing a single file that is BOTH a runnable C program (prints LANG:C) and a runnable Python-3 program (prints LANG:PY) - a genuine dual-parser construction that takes interior debugging. quantitative_correctness=3: every generated continuation, the MIPS sum, and the Fortran sum of squares are exact and the verifier recomputes hidden answers independently; the sampler continues over fresh hidden prompts not given to the agent. hidden_case_generalization=3: /app/app runs on hidden prompts (short/long, vocab-edge tokens, repeated tokens) and /app/scheme.py on hidden Scheme programs (closures, recursion, quote/list ops) and must generalize; the Fortran binary and the qemu-run MIPS binary judge hidden integer inputs. tool_breadth=3: little-endian MIPS cross toolchain + qemu-user-static, gfortran/make, gcc, the CPython interpreter, and gzip-size enforcement. Machine floor is hard (polyglot, sampler and source-cap floors are each hard).

larch-vane.documented_probe: C-69755486 (mark the reconstruction script as executable and preserve the source listing unchanged; min difficulty medium): a three-stage pipeline shipped with all executable bits stripped; the agent must chmod +x every stage without changing a byte (pristine sha-compared), run the chain (which invokes the stages directly, so the bits are load-bearing), produce the visible report, and leave the shipped tree listing byte-for-byte intact while the verifier regenerates the listing and re-runs the chain on hidden recording directories.
larch-vane.notes: Medium: the exec-bit restoration is load-bearing (the chain entry point calls the stages directly), contents are byte-checked against pristine copies, and an immutability trap (the regenerated tree listing must equal the shipped file byte-for-byte) penalizes any stray file under the watched trees. Hidden cases vary row shapes, zero-valid-row files and an empty file. No tool breadth or resource pressure.

lichen-mesa.documented_probe: C-7a6b9df2 (drive distilled-SAM/MobileSAM inference on CPU from rectangular-region prompts to produce per-cell segmentation masks): this task exercises the full capability — load per-tile distilled SAM weights via torch on CPU, run eval/no_grad inference, derive per-cell masks from each rectangular prompt region, and report masks/centroids/bboxes on hidden tiles.
lichen-mesa.notes: Multi-stage: PNG ingest, per-tile torch model load (map_location cpu, eval, no_grad), sigmoid>0.5 foreground, per-rectangle restriction into cell-local frames, npz + csv + json artifacts. Generalization over hidden tiles with different sizes/layouts/cells. Rubric nonzero for tool_breadth (torch/numpy/pillow), reasoning_depth (coordinate conventions, cell-local frames, clipping rects), hidden_case_generalization + quantitative_correctness (exact masks/centroid/bbox/counts on hidden tiles), resource_pressure (CPU-only torch inference).

lichen-tide.documented_probe: C-27dd85fb (emit alert and report json with the required schemas): covering task at medium difficulty; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases (schema-key assertions, level-boundary scanning, defaults for malformed rules, zero-threshold firing, multi-client lines, garbage rule sets, empty logs).
lichen-tide.notes: Single-stage: build a general log-triage program applying literal-keyword + min-level rules to multiple log files and emitting an alert.json (timestamp + id/severity/matches/ips) and a report.json (events + per-rule statistics map). Differs from umber-summit Stage 1: literal substring keywords instead of regex patterns, severity-ordered level gate instead of unconditional matching, client= tokens instead of src=, explicit output-path arguments instead of fixed paths, and a schema-asserting verifier. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (level ordering + defaults), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (malformed lines/rules, multiple hidden cases), quantitative_correctness (exact counts and sorted ip lists). No tool breadth, no dependency chain; totals bucket to medium.

lumen-model.notes: Difficulty comes from correctly implementing a documented dequantize-2-layer-ReLU-argmax forward contract and making it generalize: the program must work on hidden models/vectors with non-unit scale/zero-point (where skipping dequant changes labels), break argmax ties to the lowest class, and reject ragged/mismatched/missing-field inputs with a failing exit and no output file. Exactness of the label output plus the required defensive error behavior make this a solid medium; there is no multi-stage pipeline, heavy tooling, or resource pressure, so it stays below hard.

lunar-dial.notes: Single-stage: debug an unknown quantity (sediment depth) reachable only through a monotone prefix oracle with two endpoints, under a hard 28-call budget, so exponential bracketing plus binary search is required and a linear scan fails. Exercises C-d6eae9b8 (binary-search a prefix oracle under a strict call budget) at easy: the verifier independently recomputes the true depth, replays every logged probe against the instrument for consistency, enforces calls<=budget and both-endpoint usage. Small nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (bracketing+search), debugging_ambiguity (unknown L, derived property), interaction_statefulness (probe transcript must match reality), hidden_case_generalization and quantitative_correctness.

maple-vellum.notes: Medium. Round-trip a deduplicated content-addressed chunk store back to the exact original tree: parse the manifest, verify every blob against its own SHA-256 digest name, reassemble each file's chunk sequence (honoring repeated digests, shared prefixes, whole-file duplicates and zero-chunk empty files), recreate every declared directory including empty ones, write files at their exact relative paths (unicode/space names), and fail loudly (non-zero, stderr) on missing/mismatched blobs, size mismatches, invalid manifests or unsafe paths. Hidden cases cover multi-chunk binaries, many-to-one chunk sharing, empty files/dirs at depth, and a deliberately corrupted blob that must abort the restore. Exactness is checked by full file-set + per-file SHA-256 comparison, so any name or byte deviation fails the reconstruction assertion. Rubric nonzero for dependent_stages (verify-then-write pipeline), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (corrupted store, edge shapes), quantitative_correctness (exact hashes). No resource or interaction pressure.

marble-hearth.notes: Two coupled stages: (1) an idempotent dependency installer that must extend the system Python (attrs/six/hearthrt) WITHOUT disturbing the pinned torch 2.13.0 / transformers 5.16.1 toolchain (the tempting failure is a careless pip upgrade/reinstall or a dependency cascade that replaces the toolchain and breaks the offline load path); (2) an offline next-token inference CLI whose exact JSON contract (last-position argmax, add_special_tokens=False, hearthrt-sourced appliance_id, blank-line skipping, order preservation) must generalize to hidden model stores and prompt batches. Nonzero rubric for dependent_stages (installer must run before inference output is valid), tool_breadth (pip + transformers + torch), reasoning_depth (exact argmax/decode contract), debugging_ambiguity (offline-only constraints, idempotency), adversarial_inputs (blank lines, unseen vocab stores), hidden_case_generalization (two hidden model stores), quantitative_correctness (exact token ids/strings), unsafe_action_penalty (touching the pinned toolchain is the graded hazard).

marble-hollow.documented_probe: Documented probe waiver: C-b18a585c (split oversized files under a size cap with recoverable reassembly) reference floor is medium; this task exercises the full capability at medium (header-budget arithmetic, quota edge sizes, error paths, tamper rejection), fully checked by the verifier on visible and hidden cases.
marble-hollow.notes: Medium: the pack contract forces careful header-budget arithmetic (83-byte fixed header inside the cap, so payload = cap-83, ceil sizing, cap<84 rejected), a self-describing per-segment digest, and an invertible index; merge must validate headers/digests and reject missing/corrupted segments with non-zero exit and no output (adversarial_inputs=2). Hidden cases cover empty blob, exact-payload and payload+1 boundary sizes, tiny cap=85, oversize 500KB, and an invalid-cap error case plus verifier-side tamper tests (hidden_case_generalization=2). Byte-exact round trips and digests give quantitative_correctness=1. Stdlib-only, deterministic; total buckets to medium.

marble-relay.notes: Hard: author a native C binary implementing a 4-byte length-prefixed JSON frame protocol over stdio (full-read handling, one reply per request, persistent multi-frame session), a minimal JSON parser (key-order independent, \u escapes, integer validation), nine operations with exact deep-equal reply shapes including error frames, plus a launcher manifest whose entry must resolve to the exact entrypoint path or the external Node launcher fails the boot. The verifier drives everything through the shipped launcher on hidden cases (ops, errors, mid-session delays, key-order variance). Rubric total 17 -> hard.

marble-shard.notes: Easy (7/30). Recover the content of an unlinked-but-open file descriptor: scan /proc/*/fd for links ending in '(deleted)', read behind each descriptor, and select the payload whose first line is exactly SHARD_ID=<id>. Hidden states spawn several simultaneous keepers holding decoy payloads — one that mentions the requested id on a non-marker line and one whose marker id merely has the requested id as a prefix — plus a negative query that must exit 2, so a substring or wrong-fd read fails. Single-stage, single tool surface (procfs); no dependency chain or resource pressure.

marl-haven.notes: Binary reverse-engineering + matrix recovery: reverse a 16-byte header + fixed-size frame format (XOR-obfuscated int16 payloads, optional delta decoding over valid frames only), then package query+decode logic into an executable script whose CLI writes the recovered (frames x channels) float64 matrix to .npy. Hard floor from the multi-stage decode (status filtering, delta cumsum, payload de-obfuscation), query spec expansion (reversed ranges, duplicates, order-sensitive orientation), and the executable/.npy packaging contract. Hidden cases cover delta vs plain captures, interleaved invalid frames, out-of-order/duplicate query indices, out-of-range indices, and an all-invalid capture yielding a (0, C) matrix; the verifier executes /app/extract.py unchanged and compares shape, dtype, orientation and exact values.

marlin-berth.notes: Single focused competency: place the mailing-list manager configuration in the canonical file (/etc/postfix/virtual_lists), make postfix honor it (postconf virtual_alias_maps + postmap), manage a delimited alias block with postalias, provision local accounts, and emit a report. The deliverable is a general idempotent installer reused verbatim against hidden list files (different domains/targets/accounts), and the verifier proves the canonical path is honored via postfix's own lookup tooling after a full state reset. Small nonzero rubric for the dependency chain, postfix tooling breadth, local-vs-external logic, adversarial reset/idempotency probing, hidden generalization and exact mapping correctness; totals bucket to medium.

marlin-forge.notes: UPC-style shared-heap realization: one malloc'd shared array filled in parallel by pthreads, contiguous even split with empty/zero-item edge cases, per-rank worker_<r>.dat files with exact prefix/suffix and five-line format, global grand-total check, and strict malformed-argv handling (exit 3, nothing written). Verifier recompiles the source, executes the binary on hidden thread/item combinations plus bad argv, and byte-checks the /app/worker_*.dat deliverables from the visible run. Nonzero dependent_stages (source -> build -> run -> per-rank files), reasoning_depth (slice math, empty slices), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization, quantitative_correctness (exact sums/maxima).

marlin-rig.documented_probe: C-b2fceb71 (run feature matching and robust geometric model fits over correspondences): the covering task exercises the competency at hard difficulty; the verifier executes the delivered matcher+RANSAC program on four hidden scenarios (heavy outlier contamination, an inconsistent-scene degenerate case requiring a soft failure instead of zero-inlier crash, exact-tie duplicate patches with zero-norm skipped descriptors, and a minimal 4-correspondence scene) and compares matches, inliers, params, and residuals.
marlin-rig.notes: Single-stage but deep: from-scratch normalized-patch descriptor matching (ratio test + mutual best with exact tie-breaks) feeding an exhaustive two-point RANSAC similarity fit with closed-form least-squares refinement, plus a required degenerate-status fallback when no consensus exists. The trap is zero-inlier/crash behavior and tie-breaking, probed by adversarial hidden scenarios. Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth, debugging_ambiguity, adversarial_inputs, hidden_case_generalization, and quantitative_correctness; no tool breadth, dependency chain, or environment pressure; totals bucket to hard.

marrow-vane.notes: Bring-up chain: read the board datasheet, translate hex register/load/entry facts into a correct JSON machine profile for a generic profile-driven emulator host, wire an executable runner with a three-mode CLI that drives the installed emulator (not a reimplementation), then run the legacy image and capture its serial output. The verifier re-executes the runner on the shipped image and on hidden images probing wrap-around arithmetic, unknown opcodes, truncated records, missing HLT, and empty output. Rubric nonzero for dependent_stages (profile -> runner -> captured output), tool_breadth (emulator host + bash + JSON), reasoning_depth (datasheet translation, edge-case semantics), debugging_ambiguity (wrong profile yields wrong/empty output), adversarial_inputs and hidden_case_generalization (hidden images), and quantitative_correctness (byte-exact arithmetic output). No resource pressure; totals bucket to hard via the multi-stage bring-up and setup breadth.

meadow-bridge.notes: Six-stage pipeline across tar/iso/acl/pbkdf2/path semantics with adversarial prefix decoys and source-immutability checks; unsafe mutation of the source archive fails verification.

meadow-yonder.notes: Medium (11/30). Four data-logging deliverables each exact/count-string sensitive: an access-log parser/tabulator (hidden_generalization=2), fixing a missing-strip newline-accumulation bug in a CSV processor so each record emits exactly one line (debugging_ambiguity=2), a bash sampler emitting timestamp,total,idle,fraction rows on a fixed interval with the fraction computed from state (quantitative_correctness=2), and a precise single-line digit-only answer that must integrate cluster idle-sum and unique-client count (adversarial/edge inputs=2 for malformed log lines, blank/comment lines, \r\n and empty inputs, and a zero-total cluster state). Difficulty is at/above the max competency floor (medium, C-d883e15c / C-cc366c45).

mica-fjord.notes: Build a frequency-ordered vocabulary with special tokens, exact inverse maps sized to a frozen embedding matrix, and pickle it via the provided module's dataclass so it unpickles inside the verifier (module-path trap). Hidden cases probe tie ordering, case/punctuation folding, exact fit, and an unsatisfiable request that must fail non-zero without writing outputs. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (ordering + min-frequency + sizing rule), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (three distinct hidden corpora incl. an expected-failure case), quantitative_correctness (exact mapping/report equality), debugging_ambiguity (unpickling/module-path pitfall) and light tool_breadth/dependent_stages (numpy fixture + pickle). Totals bucket to hard.

mica-grid.notes: Competency C-8bec045f: exact 9x9 sudoku completion. Distinct surface from the sibling covering task (an importable multi-function module): here the deliverable is a file-based CLI with an explicit exit-code contract (0 solved / 1 well-formed-but-unsolvable / 2 malformed), tolerant-but-strict board parsing (0 or '.' empties, CRLF and trailing blank lines tolerated, wrong length or stray characters rejected), and byte-exact solution output with givens preserved. The checker executes /app/sudoku.py on the shipped board and on hidden boards (sparse ~33 givens, 3 empty cells, unsolvable contradiction, two malformed boards) and independently validates rows/columns/boxes and given preservation plus exact-match against reference solutions.

mica-marsh.documented_probe: C-cec73e0d (extract the weight matrix of a relu mlp from forward queries): the verifier re-runs the delivered extract_rows under a hard query budget against the visible fixture plus two hidden fixtures with different in_dim/unit counts/signs, checking every row v_i*w_i up to permutation and nonzero per-row scaling with exactly n_units rows. Verifier fully checks the capability.
mica-marsh.notes: Single-stage scientific_computing task: recover the scaled input rows of a one-hidden-layer ReLU network through the scalar query channel only. Requires piecewise-linear reasoning (axis scans, kink localization, gradient-difference row recovery, sign/permutation ambiguity, dedup) within a query budget that rules out brute force. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth, debugging_ambiguity, adversarial_inputs, hidden_case_generalization (two fresh fixtures), quantitative_correctness (row matching to tolerance), interaction_statefulness (query budget); buckets to hard.

mica-mural.documented_probe: C-2e1c650a (stay beneath a compressed source-size ceiling): covering task exercises the capability at hard difficulty - the renderer source must fit a 320-byte gzip cap and 800-byte raw cap, must report its real measured sizes, and must not communicate the image by embedding pixel rows or palette literals. Unlike the drift-grove tiny-source probe, the renderer here is spec-driven and is re-executed by the verifier on hidden specs (1x1, single-row, P=1 palette, Unicode palette, large negative-coefficient murals), so generalization plus the size gate are both enforced.
mica-mural.notes: Single hard capability: byte-exact parametric rendering from a spec, under hard compressed-source byte gates with a measured-sizes report and anti-embedding checks. Nonzero rubric for quantitative_correctness (exact byte gates + measured sizes must match reality), reasoning_depth (iterating the source down under the gzip cap without breaking the exact modular formula), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (five structurally different hidden specs), resource_pressure (hard byte budget on the deliverable itself), dependent_stages (renderer must exist before frame.txt and mural-sizes.json can be produced from it), tool_breadth (gzip measurement pipeline), debugging_ambiguity (stale size reports silently fail).

mist-buoy.notes: The agent must fetch and read the hosted /contract.json before calling anything (competency C-15878c3b): the archive key, the /api/v2/ prefix, the cursor parameter name, the 202-then-poll job lifecycle and the campaign constants are all only in the doc, and the wrong guesses (unversioned or /api/v1/ paths, missing auth header) fail with 404/410/403. The chain contract->paginated listing->filtered selection->POST->poll->serialize is stateful and multi-stage. Hidden instances vary contract version, archive key, select_status, metric, window, page counts and data (including a zero-reading result with null stats), so any hard-coded doc value or data fails. Tool breadth limited to HTTP via stdlib; no resource pressure.

mist-quay.documented_probe: C-759c32c0 (enable password-based authentication): covered directly as the easy reference task; the verifier generates fresh hidden accounts through the agent's adduser.sh and crypt-verifies the $6$ hashes plus live HTTP accept/reject behaviour.
mist-quay.notes: Single-stage: enable password auth (config flip) and generate SHA-512 crypt password hashes wired into the service's basic-auth credential file. Failure modes probed: wrong hash scheme (non-$6$), plaintext storage, mismatched secret, non-idempotent scripts, clobbering other users' entries. Rubric nonzero for adversarial_inputs (punctuation-laden hidden passwords, wrong-password rejection) and hidden_case_generalization (unseen accounts through adduser.sh). Totals bucket to easy.

moor-atlas.documented_probe: Covering task for C-92072676 (connect to a postgres service using compose-provided credentials) at medium difficulty; verifier fully checks the capability on hidden stack/database scenarios.
moor-atlas.notes: Single-stage: parse a compose-style stack file (mapping or list-style environment, decoy non-postgres service), derive host port from the published mapping (non-default port, scram enforced on TCP so wrong passwords fail), connect with the file-provided credentials, and census the beacons table into an exact JSON audit. A decoy second instance shares the visible database name/credentials with an EMPTY table, so a wrong port still connects but reads nothing. Hidden scenarios vary service name, credentials, database, data, and instance; include a list-style environment, an empty registry (strongest=null), a strength tie broken by lowest id, and two expect-failure stacks (wrong password, unreachable port) that must exit non-zero without creating the output file. Distinct from quartz-cipher/granary-ledge in scenario (beacon survey), decoy-instance trap, and expect-failure mechanics.

moor-latch.notes: Single-deliverable HTTP-service task: the client manages a local archive server process (free port, start, /health readiness poll, teardown), then walks a two-stage identifier-keyed API — entry metadata first (which deliberately carries no sequences), then one /api/sequence request per listed chain — and must reproduce every returned amino-acid sequence byte-exactly (any edit fails equality against the API). Reasoning_depth=2 (two-stage dependent retrieval keyed off metadata the agent cannot shortcut), adversarial_inputs=2 (chain ids repeat across entries so sequences must be keyed per entry; spec order differs from archive order; a distractor entry exists in the archive but not in the spec). quantitative_correctness=1: total_chains/total_residues must be exact.

moss-forge.notes: Single-stage debugging: a release (-O2) build of a custom first-fit free-list pool allocator segfaults because the split path leaves the remainder block's free-list link unwritten, so it inherits stale payload bytes; the next allocation that walks past it dereferences garbage. The agent must diagnose with gdb/objdump/repro workloads, fix only /app/forge.c (main.c and Makefile are hash-protected), rebuild, and satisfy an independent reference simulation of the driver checksum on the visible workload plus three hidden workloads (reuse-heavy, shrink-split, churn) that all reproduce the crash on the shipped binary. Exercises C-7991a29a at medium. Rubric nonzero for tool_breadth (debuggers/build), reasoning_depth and debugging_ambiguity (heap bookkeeping corruption), hidden_case_generalization, quantitative_correctness (exact checksum).

moss-graph.documented_probe:
C-a42c8793 (apply a do-style intervention fixing a variable to a point value): reference floor is hard but the covering task exercises it at medium; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases. Documented probe waiver.
C-abbd9846 (persist a schema-conformant json object): reference floor is hard but the covering task exercises it at medium; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases. Documented probe waiver.
moss-graph.notes: Difficulty is moderate. Substance comes from pinning down the exact lexicographic-stable topological order (Kahn with min-heap tie-breaking), the intervention semantics (intervened node ignores parents and is set to the intervention value), cycle detection, and exact decimal arithmetic rounded to six places half-up. Hidden cases probe a fresh diamond graph, a cyclic graph, an isolated node combined with a lexical tie, and a fractional rounding-heavy input. The implementation is a single self-contained Python computation with no IO beyond reading two CSVs and writing one JSON, so dependency stages, tool breadth, resource pressure and statefulness are low (0-1). Implementation-style ambiguity (multiple correct-looking orderings, integer-vs-float and rounding conventions, how to handle interventions on absent nodes) is the main difficulty, hence debugging_ambiguity=2, adversarial_inputs=2, hidden_case_generalization=2, quantitative_correctness=2.

moss-kernel.documented_probe: C-3376e488 (implement a gated-transformation Triton kernel with RMSNorm matching a PyTorch reference; min difficulty medium): the task requires a single @triton.jit kernel using only triton.language ops that reproduces a tanh-gated blend with a +1.0 shift plus per-row RMS rescaling in float32, with the masked-lane reduction trap (padded lanes become 1.0 after the shift and must be excluded from the mean square) and hidden shape/seed/eps cases checked against an independent torch reference.
moss-kernel.notes: Two deliverables: the Triton kernel module and a runnable self-check. Medium floor from kernel correctness under CPU-interpreter mode (masked loads/stores, in-kernel reduction, tl-only ops), numerics matching within 1e-4 on fresh hidden shapes including D=1, non-power-of-two D and D=1024, and determinism. No environment pressure; modest tool breadth (triton/torch).

moss-latch.documented_probe: Documented probe waiver: C-8034934c (fix cython source for numpy 2.x api compatibility) reference floor is medium; this task exercises the capability directly at medium in a single-package scope rather than the multi-component repair of basalt-mantle.
moss-latch.notes: Focused medium: port a vendored Cython extension off numpy 2.x-removed interfaces. Dependent stages: fix build configuration -> fix stale C API / removed numpy.math usages in the .pyx -> build against installed numpy 2.x -> regular install -> probe report (build must precede probe). Requires tool breadth (Cython/setuptools/pip) and reasoning about which legacy interfaces were removed (numpy.distutils, numpy.math, PyArray_FromDims). Hidden cases generalize hann/ramp to unseen n including empty ramp(0), n==1 window, larger n, and ValueError paths, and check genuine float64 ndarray returns. Quantitative correctness checked to 1e-9. Offline; verifier re-runs the build deliverable twice for idempotency.

moss-loft.notes: Config-driven snapshot trainer (medium, total 9): the agent authors /app/train.py (CSV+config -> trained state-dict snapshot) and produces /app/model_snapshot.pt on the visible fixture. The verifier reloads the snapshot with torch.load(weights_only=True) and enforces that it is a REAL weights file at exactly the configured layer/width node counts (key set + shapes vs /app/config.json), finite and non-degenerate (catches dummy/zero/all-equal files), modestly sized (catches oversized dumps), and >=0.85 held-out accuracy (catches untrained snapshots) -- the full missing/dummy/oversized failure surface of the artifact competency. It then RE-EXECUTES the deliverable trainer on three hidden cases that vary input_dim (5/6/10), hidden_units (8/16/32), num_classes (2/3/4), epochs, lr, batch size, and seed, applying the same checks to each freshly produced snapshot (hidden_case_generalization=2, quantitative_correctness=2). Single-stage pipeline on a small dataset keeps resource_pressure=0 and no statefulness.

moss-quill.notes: Train a fasttext-style linear bag-of-ngrams triage classifier on a 3-class synthetic ticket corpus under two binding constraints: holdout accuracy >= floor on a documented deterministic sha-keyed split, and serialized model size <= 262144 bytes. The tension is real: an unbounded full-vocabulary bigram pipeline pickles to ~350 KB (blows the budget) while a heavily truncated ~150-feature unigram model drifts to ~0.90 (under the floor); the oracle lands at ~0.93 accuracy / ~190 KB via min_df + max_features + bigram tf-idf + logistic regression. The verifier re-executes the trainer on hidden corpora (fresh domain mix with a higher floor, and an edge corpus with blank/no-TAB/punctuation-only/duplicate rows) and recomputes split, accuracy, size and every report field. Rubric weights reasoning_depth (hyperparameter/size tradeoff), quantitative_correctness (exact split/report agreement), hidden_case_generalization and adversarial_inputs (edge corpus), resource_pressure (size budget). Totals bucket to hard.

moss-vane.notes: Author a C scorer from a strict spec and compile it to a native ELF at /app/bin/infer with a fixed, literal two-argument order (weights path then image path). Covers argument-order/argument-count handling, strict PGM P2 and comment-tolerant weights parsing, 4x4 block integer scoring, and recompile independence (verifier rebuilds the shipped source and re-runs every hidden case, including malformed-input exits and a swapped-argument probe). Rubric total 11 -> medium; hidden cases generalize across sizes, comment placement, >16 weights, zero scores, and malformed files.

myrtle-canyon.documented_probe: C-5ede2c22 (preserve the reference model file and simulate with a fresh MuJoCo installation without plugins; min difficulty medium): the box ships without MuJoCo and with a pinned offline wheelhouse; the agent must pip-install mujoco==3.2.4 with --no-index, tune a slider feed-stage model into a second self-contained file (no plugins/assets/includes, one joint + one actuator, zero loaded plugins), keep the reference byte-identical to the pristine copy, and survive the acceptance sweep (tuned > 0.35 m, reference < 0.10 m at 2 s) on the visible drive and on hidden positive/negative drive sets.
myrtle-canyon.notes: Medium: three dependent stages (offline install, model tuning, proof-of-run), an immutability constraint on the reference fixture, self-containment traps (plugins/assets/includes rejected by scan and by mjModel.nplugin), and hidden generalization over drive values. No resource pressure; simulation is deterministic and fast.

nectar-gasket.notes: Hard scientific-computing task. The integrator must reach a tight absolute accuracy (down to 2e-5) against an independent fine reference of the same ODE while honoring a hard RHS-evaluation budget, so the step-size policy has to be reasoned about rather than guessed (an Euler or coarse step drifts past tol; a correct RK4/adaptive solver passes). The ensemble path must really parallelize per-k randomized initial-state subsamples across n_jobs real worker processes (verified by distinct-PID count and exact serial-vs-parallel numerical equality within 1e-6) and report reproduced timings. Spectral tools must select the largest-magnitude eigenvalue of non-symmetric complex-spectra matrices under an exact deterministic tie-break, reconstruct the leading-principal-minor dominant-eigenvalue row, and handle a 1400x1400 'thousands of assets' matrix. Hidden cases cover scoring n=240 tight-budget, n=2 and n=1 edgeless, complex-conjugate magnitude ties, a 1x1 singleton, and the large fixture. Hard floors: C-7e2ac892 (parallelize, floor hard) and C-95dbc133 (physics validity, floor hard) both at or above their floors; the rubric total of 19 falls in the hard bucket and dependent_stages=3 satisfies the hard-task floor.

nectar-helix.notes: Medium. Three independent reusable file-tree CLIs must each be authored and then RUN on the shipped fixtures to produce the visible output trees (dependent_stages=2 reflects 'write tool -> run it on the tree'). tool_breadth=3 because three distinct contracts each stand on their own (zero-byte leaf instantiation w/ listing parsing + rejection; item-count/cap byte-budget repackaging with split arithmetic and a reassemblable manifest; LF normalization with independent text/binary detection). reasoning_depth=2 from the split-ceil arithmetics, shard packing, and LF/CR normalization rewrite. hidden_case_generalization=3: the verifier dispatches each tool against separate fresh hidden scenarios (deep/ spaced/ dir-flag listings, parent-collision and ..  rejections, multi-shard packs, a >byte-budget file split and exact-boundary, an empty tree, CRLF/lone-CR text, NUL binaries both below and above the 4096 boundary) plus the visible /app fixtures. quantitative_correctness=2 from per-directory item caps, per-file byte caps, part-budget ceilings, and byte-for-byte reassembly/LF checks. Medium floors of all three competencies match the medium bucket.

night-console.notes: Stateful line-oriented protocol with a 3-state machine (EMPTY/OPEN/CLOSED). The agent must implement a general interpreter that generalizes to fresh command streams; hidden cases probe many edge cases (commands before open and after close, reopen rejection, overwrite, missing keys, malformed/unknown commands, empty LIST, blank lines), so adversarial-input handling and rule generalization carry the difficulty. Single python file, no external deps.

nova-quarry.notes: C-b37daad9 (fit a full transformer-inference engine under a strict source-size budget): implement the whole forward pass (token+positional embeddings, pre-normed multi-head causal attention, ReLU FFN, final LayerNorm, vocabulary projection) as one numpy program under a 3000-byte source cap that must compile with the mandated `python3 -m py_compile` command. The verifier re-executes the engine on three hidden fixture sets with different depths/widths/head counts/vocab sizes and compares logits to an in-process reference within 2e-3, so overshooting the cap or a mis-emulated block fails regardless of anything else.

olive-quarry.documented_probe: C-e87edf52 (set up an R Jupyter kernel plus the R analysis packages for causal work): reference floor is hard and this task is hard; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases (unseen kernel names via a temp HOME and unseen R package tarballs via a temp library).
olive-quarry.notes: Environment-commissioning task focused on the R Jupyter kernel (IRkernel registration, kernelspec detection by name) plus R CMD INSTALL of vendored causal-analysis R packages. Hidden generalization is exercised through the reusable registrar (unseen kernel names/display strings into a temp HOME, detected via jupyter kernelspec list) and the reusable installer (unseen package tarballs into a temp library with function-result checks). Rubric weights tool_breadth (Rscript/jupyter/bash interop), dependent_stages and interaction_statefulness (live state must be left commissioned), hidden_case_generalization; totals bucket to hard.

onyx-caravan.notes: Single-stage: implement a stdlib HTTP client that walks a full stateful session (single-use challenge nonce with deployment-varying hash algorithm, cookie-name-agnostic session jar, optional X-Nonce header, CSRF-protected logout) and saves a report artifact. Verified by executing the client against fresh hidden origins (sha512/header-required, sha1/plain, sha256/header-required) and checking the exact issued sid/csrf plus server-side session termination. Rubric nonzero for interaction_statefulness and hidden_case_generalization (session state must be carried across four calls under varying deployments), reasoning_depth (dynamic alg dispatch), debugging_ambiguity (single-use nonces, header variant), adversarial_inputs (failing challenges need a fresh nonce), quantitative_correctness (exact session values). No tool breadth or dependency chain; totals bucket to medium.

onyx-ember.notes: Scoped HARD because the maximum competency floor is hard: C-4b7949d3 (leave numpy importable system-wide) has floor=hard, and per contract the bucket must be >= the max floor even though the waveform prototype suggested medium. It is also a genuinely multi-stage repair: restore pip from the official get-pip.py bootstrap, use the restored pip to install numpy, rebuild+editable-install the Cython extension so the default interpreter loads the native backend, run the async-fs unit suite, and instantiate a named conda env from a spec file (dependent_stages=3, tool_breadth=2). The repair is driven by five interdependent failure signatures (broken import, removed pip, absent numpy, missing conda env, missing rebuilt artifact) rather than a single shared signal (debugging_ambiguity=2, reasoning_depth=3). The checksum equality is exact (quantitative_correctness=2). Hidden cases are two-fold: adversarial digest inputs (empty/single-char/long-repeat/non-ASCII UTF-8) AND re-running repair.sh from several genuinely different degraded filesystem/package states (extension+prism stubbed again, numpy wiped, pip removed again, conda env gone, /app/rebuilt deleted), forcing real idempotent repair generalization (hidden_case_generalization=3, interaction_statefulness=2). conda solve, numpy wheels and the get-pip bootstrap all run over the corporate proxy; no GPU/X/service; agent timeout 1800s and verifier 600s cover the repeated conda creates in the verifier.

onyx-frame.notes: Single compact deliverable program whose own source is the size-constrained artifact: gzip(source) <= 400 bytes and raw <= 750 bytes while the program must stay generic across hidden render specs (different dimensions, ramps, coefficients; same formula) and render frames byte-exactly. The tight caps force genuine size engineering (compact arg handling, single-expression rendering, self-measurement via __file__) and the anti-embedding rules forbid shipping pixel data; naive verbose implementations and any embedded-frame approach exceed the cap. Hidden cases keep the identical caps so a visible-only program cannot pass. Rubric weights reasoning_depth (self-referential size report + generic formula), resource_pressure (hard byte ceilings), quantitative_correctness (byte-exact frames and size numbers), plus hidden-case generalization and adversarial (narrow/thin frames). Totals bucket to hard.

onyx-gasket.notes: Total 18 -> hard bucket. The task stacks pip-bootstrap restore -> Cython/numpy-2 build-port -> editable reinstall -> async fs tests -> conda env create -> OSMesa placement as one chain, plus exact FNV-1a correctness and hidden byte/tree edge cases; the max competency floor among the four claimed competencies is 'hard' (C-f2183611), so the task must sit in the hard bucket even though the original score target was medium.

onyx-mural.notes: Hard. The agent must reverse the exact behavior of a stripped-source compiled binary: probe black-box with crafted grids and/or disassemble to discover that the operation is serpentine (alternating-direction) Floyd-Steinberg error diffusion to two levels with threshold 128, weights 7/3/5/1 over 16 with C-truncating division, in-place error accumulation, border-clamped (dropped) propagation, and an exact '#'/'.', newline-terminated output format. The verifier relocates the native binary before running the deliverable and compares stdout byte-for-byte against an independent reference on hidden grids (boundary values 0/127/128/255, tiny shapes, constant fields, random photo-like fields), so partial models or wrong rounding/scan-order fail. Rubric nonzero for tool_breadth (objdump/gdb/probing), reasoning_depth and debugging_ambiguity (stateful two-pass sequential dependence is not guessable from one probe), hidden_case_generalization and quantitative_correctness (exact byte equality on unseen grids), adversarial_inputs (boundary threshold values), dependent_stages (observe -> model -> implement -> cross-check). No resource or interaction pressure.

onyx-relay.documented_probe: C-b37daad9 (fit a full transformer-inference engine under a strict source-size budget): covered at hard difficulty; the byte cap, mandated compile check, and hidden hyperparameter re-runs are fully enforced by the verifier.
onyx-relay.notes: Single-stage: reconstruct a fused-qkv causal pre-LN transformer with SiLU and a vocabulary-projection head from a JSON state dict, under a hard 5000-byte source cap with a mandated py_compile build. Overshooting the cap or failing to compile fails regardless of correctness. Rubric weights reasoning_depth (masked multi-head attention + layernorm math), hidden_case_generalization (3 hidden fixture sets with different dims), quantitative_correctness (exact tokens + 6-decimal logits), and resource_pressure (the byte budget). No tool breadth or dependency chain; totals bucket to hard.

onyx-rudder.notes: Hard security task covering C-1d626fbd (harden header-name canonicalization to reject control characters while preserving valid canonical forms). The delivered /app/hdrnorm.py is re-imported and re-executed (module matrix + batch CLI) over hidden adversarial name matrices where BOTH under-rejection (CR/LF/NUL/TAB/DEL/0x1f accepted) and over-rejection (spaces, '_', digits, '.', empty hyphen tokens rejected, or wrong canonical casing) fail; /app/gateway.py must wire the same normalizer into a live HTTP rewrite/validate surface (400 on any control-character name) and /app/scan_report.json is a generated batch-report deliverable. adversarial_inputs=3 for the rejection-boundary matrix; unsafe_action_penalty=1 since the deliverable deliberately demonstrates an injection-closing fix; remaining rubric light enough to stay below the hardest bucket while the header competency floor is hard.

onyx-spire.notes: Medium. Single-stage: parse a job spec (locale + ordered column list), stream a large JSONL manifest, keep only the requested locale subset (exact match, rows missing 'locale' dropped), skip blank/malformed/non-object lines without crashing, and emit the requested columns in requested order with JSON null for absent columns. The verifier executes the deliverable program on the visible manifest (4200+ lines) and on three hidden scenarios (mixed adversarial lines with missing columns, a zero-match locale, an all-match case with a never-present column and unicode values). Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (ordered emission + null semantics), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (hidden cases), and quantitative_correctness (exact row set and column values). No tool breadth, no dependency chain, no environment pressure; totals bucket to medium given the large dataset and strict column-order contract.

onyx-upland.notes: Five independent serialize/aggregate deliverables must ALL hold simultaneously (grouped CSV summaries with a totals row, ordered CSV result sets, status tallies with exactly-once label lines, TOML with an exact two-integer schema, and byte-identical fixed-width records).
