No dependency chain or resource pressure; totals bucket to medium.

saffron-rune.documented_probe: C-57f213ee (featurize SMILES strings into model-input arrays; min difficulty hard): the task demands a byte-exact reproduction of a published multi-stage tokenization + rolling-hash featurization (bracket spans, two-letter tokens, invalid-character and unclosed-bracket zero vectors, positional binning) exercised on three hidden SMILES lists plus a catalog-derived features.npz. The covering task exercises the capability fully on hidden cases.
saffron-rune.notes: Single-stage: implement the exact deterministic featurizer and run it on the visible catalog. Hard floor from adversarial inputs (unclosed brackets, whitespace, non-ASCII, tabs, foreign tokens), hidden_case_generalization (three hidden lists) and quantitative_correctness (byte-exact float32 comparison). No tool breadth, no dependency chain, no environment pressure.

saffron-vine.documented_probe: C-4c743935 (LoRA adapter train/save/merge lifecycle): second independent covering task. A corrupted (zeroed) fc2 weight must be recovered by training a rank-constrained LoRA adapter to a holdout accuracy target, persisting a self-sufficient reloadable adapter directory (weights/config/tokenizer feature spec), and merging the adapter into the base weight per an exact equation that the verifier checks numerically. Hard: multi-stage lifecycle, exact merge-equation + freeze constraints, hidden-fixture generalization.
saffron-vine.notes: Distinct from larch-cipher (stalled-head scenario): here the base model's fc2.weight is zeroed by a failed checkpoint restore and the agent must run the full LoRA lifecycle. The verifier executes /app/restore.py on the visible case and three hidden fixtures with different vocab/embed/hidden/seq-len/seed, validates the adapter directory reloads onto the base and reproduces merged outputs, checks the merge equation tensor-exactly, enforces that non-fc2 tensors are untouched, and enforces the >=0.86 holdout accuracy bar. Rubric: dependent stages (train->save->merge->eval), reasoning depth (LoRA math + freeze discipline), hidden generalization + quantitative correctness (accuracy bar and exact merge), moderate resource pressure (CPU torch training).

sage-canyon.notes: Hard (total 18). A staged exploit chain, each stage gated by the previous one (dependent_stages=3): (1) craft a working SQL-injection payload to authenticate as a target account; (2) craft an exact byte-level overflow payload that flips an adjacent gating field inside a fixed struct to a specific magic constant, unlocking the protected branch that prints the lone deployment secret; (3) run the Flask service's authorize_deployment() with that secret so its body actually executes and writes a side-effect grants file; (4) harden /app/app.py so any unknown /lookup/<id> returns HTTP 404 with a JSON error body and no HTML or stack trace. Reasoning is threefold (reasoning_depth=3): deriving the SQL tautology (easy) and C struct offset/magic-constant layout so the 20-byte payload lands exactly on the gate (quantitative=3, exact bytes and exact value), and the 404 hardening. The overflow symptom is ambiguous: an underrun or wrong-length payload prints only locked, so the agent must infer the buffer/field layout from source alone (debugging_ambiguity=2). generalization=3 because the verifier replays the payload against several target accounts, re-runs the deployment check against a fresh hash verification, and hits a battery of malformed/special-case not-found IDs (adversarial=2, ids with spaces, dots, SQL-ish text, long strings) that must not 500. Hard floors: C-1f4f846b requires actually running the app to emit the side-effect file (hard); C-1aefef55 and C-9c9c34df are medium. Correctness is numeric/exact (magic constant 0x9E1C, sha256 digest match, exact 20-byte payload).

sage-keystone.notes: Hard bucket (total 19). Three independent extraction sub-tasks the verifier re-runs on fresh fixtures: (1) a pypdf form-field enumerator re-run on three hidden forms (with-label, one with NO /TU label, and one with zero controls); (2) a rdflib SPARQL walk from Recruit->firm running on two hidden graphs with decoy triples (un-named recruit, un-typed seconded entity, firm with no name, duplicate secondments requiring DISTINCT), asserting exact result-variable binding; (3) a byte-faithful skinned-mesh decoder compared against an independent struct/numpy reference read of the same binary across three valid layouts and one torn/malformed file that must fail cleanly. reasoning_depth + dependent_stages of three chained independent competencies drive the hard bucket; generalized hidden inputs in every gate require runnable deliverables, not one-shot answers.

sage-wharf.notes: Hard (total 18). The crux is the range coder (C-e41d6ebb, floor hard): the agent must implement the exact 32-bit arithmetic-coded decoder AND an encoder that inverts the decoder's reads bit-for-bit (the renorm high/low update order is the classic off-by-one trap), confirmed by an encode->decode round-trip on unseen bytes. reasoning_depth 3 and debugging_ambiguity 3 come from the renorm boundary conditions and the greedy interval-split selection; hidden_case_generalization 3 from fresh blobs, round-trips, layers, WAL transforms and digest inputs; quantitative_correctness 3 from byte-exact decode and exact digest. Adversarial 2 via empty/0x00/0xFF-run blobs, noise and short WALs, empty pay/command. resource_pressure 0 (small fixtures, stdlib only).

sedge-vault.documented_probe: C-92072676 (connect to a postgres service using compose-provided credentials): the second covering task; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases (different db names, roles, passwords, and stack-file formatting against a live password-authenticated instance).
sedge-vault.notes: Medium: derive host/published-port/db/user/password from a compose-style stack file (nonstandard port 5541, scram-authenticated TCP), connect to the live Postgres, and export the specimens table as JSON. Hidden cases re-execute the deliverable on other stack files (other database, other role+password, noisy multi-service formatting), so hard-coding any connection parameter fails. Rubric nonzero for dependent stages (parse -> connect -> export), tool breadth (psql/postgres client), reasoning depth, debugging ambiguity, hidden-case generalization, quantitative correctness (exact rows/types), and interaction statefulness (live DB).

silt-barrow.documented_probe: C-4a3a4fa1 (selectively stream a single archive member without expanding the whole archive): reference floor is easy and the covering task exercises it at easy; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases. Documented probe waiver.
silt-barrow.notes: Single-stage: stream one named member (crash.mkd) out of a gzip tar to an output file while a sensitive member (hostkeys.pem) must never touch disk and a coexisting live recorder.log (plus a same-named archive member) must not be clobbered by full extraction. The verifier re-executes the deliverable script on hidden bundles and fails if any non-wanted member is materialized, the archive or live log changed, or the member bytes differ. Small rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (member targeting without extraction), tool_breadth (tar streaming), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (distinct hidden bundles), quantitative_correctness (byte-exact member), and unsafe_action_penalty (sensitive-member materialization).

skiff-berth.documented_probe: C-759c32c0 (enable password-based authentication): the covering task is authored at easy, matching the reference floor; the verifier fully checks the capability (hash generation on hidden secrets, crypt verification of the wired credentials, idempotent re-provisioning, and live HTTP probes of the gateway).
skiff-berth.notes: Easy: generate a sha512-crypt hash and wire it into the gateway's credential file so the configured secret is accepted. The wrong-scheme/mismatch failure mode is covered: the verifier crypt-verifies every hash (visible plus two hidden secrets run through the agent's generator), rejects locked/malformed entries and plaintext leakage, and probes the live server for 401/403/200 behavior. Nonzero rubric: dependent_stages (hash generator must be written, then provisioning run, then credentials consumed by the server), reasoning_depth (correct crypt scheme and idempotent provisioning), adversarial_inputs (hidden secrets, wrong-password/unknown-user probes), hidden_case_generalization (fresh secrets and a re-run). No tool breadth, quantitative, resource, or unsafe-action pressure; totals bucket to easy.

slate-anchor.notes: Configure the legacy plotsmith build so the non-graphical engine compiles while the X11-based frontend and its library linking are excluded entirely (./configure --without-x + make, exact deliverable name plotsmith). Medium: requires discovering the shipped configure/Makefile knobs (docs hint), understanding the two build modes, satisfying the no-X11-linkage check (dynamic section + symbols), and running the engine on jobs. Hidden generalization covers clipping edges, dense overlaps, malformed job lines, and mid-job clear, byte-compared against an independent reference.

slate-fjord.notes: Hard floor (C-a9d4f82b). The agent must make interactive password SSH usable by scripts: automate the password prompt for git clone/push, pin the server host key port-aware into a known-hosts file while keeping strict checking enabled, and make the sync script fully self-contained (graded under a pristine HOME, stdin at EOF). Depends on a chain: parse URL form/port -> pin host key -> non-interactive auth -> clone (including an empty repo with an unborn branch) -> commit -> push back to whatever branch the clone checked out. Hidden probes generalize across an empty repo, a master-branch remote with a stale manifest and byte-preservation requirements, and an ssh:// port-2222 endpoint. Server integrity (password-only sshd, untouched /srv/git) is enforced; weakening host-key checking is penalized. Differs from umber-yonder (forensics/secret purging): here the competency is exercised purely as unattended clone+push automation.

slate-hollow.notes: Covering task for C-4e83076b (inject an init script that enables serial login under an authenticated name): author an injected guest init that mounts the pseudo-filesystems (proc/sysfs/devtmpfs), registers a getty on ttyS0, and provisions a passwordless (unauthenticated) account, then repack the initramfs and drive the serial console. Rubric: dependent_stages (init authored -> repacked -> booted -> login driven -> captured), interaction_statefulness (live serial login session with an emulator), tool_breadth (QEMU TCG, cpio/gzip repacking, busybox userland, programmatic console driving), debugging_ambiguity (getty controlling-tty/setsid, empty-password semantics, prompt timing), hidden_case_generalization (verifier rebuilds the appliance for unseen usernames and independently boots + logs in, checking mounts, uid 1000 and the exact name).

slate-quarry.documented_probe: C-05d7fbec (exploit a misconfigured sudo rule to run a privileged command): the covering task executes the delivered script AS the unprivileged operator, so elevation through the configured sudo rule is the only path to the required end-state; hidden cases re-run it over wiped/stale/idempotency states. Verifier fully checks the capability.
slate-quarry.notes: Single-stage system_administration task: author an idempotent rotation script that mints a seal via the sudo-allowed snapshotctl and destroys a protected ledger via the sudo-allowed shred rule, then writes a labeled report. The verifier executes the deliverable as dana (no root powers), enforces pristine hashes of the sudoers rule and tool, and probes three hidden degraded states. Nonzero rubric for tool_breadth, reasoning_depth (privilege model), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (degraded states), interaction_statefulness (idempotency); buckets to medium.

slate-ratchet.documented_probe: C-aded17a5 (keep the answer independent of a recompiled binary): this task is the covering exercise at hard difficulty; the verifier recompiles the checksum-verified source at -O0/-O2/-Os and grades the answer against every fresh build plus negative controls, so a value that only works against a tampered binary fails.
slate-ratchet.notes: Single deliverable: recover the activation codes by reversing the obfuscated validation logic in the provided C source. The verifier enforces the no-tamper rule via sha256 on the source, rebuilds three fresh binaries, requires ACCEPT on every enabled profile under every build, and requires REJECT on hidden probe codes. Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (deobfuscation + reimplementation of the per-profile chain), adversarial_inputs (tamper/negative probes), hidden_case_generalization (multiple profiles + multiple build levels), quantitative_correctness (exact code strings).

sorrel-hasp.documented_probe: None. This is the second independent covering task for C-2d0e9195 (generate and protect a 2048-bit rsa private key); the reference task plum-seal touches key generation only as a sub-step of X.509 certificate issuance, while this task centers the full key-generation contract: exact bit-length policy, unencrypted PEM, explicit 0600 mode under any umask, overwrite semantics, and precise exit codes.
sorrel-hasp.notes: Two-stage: build a reusable validating generator (policy gate on bit size with exit code 2, umask-independent chmod 0600, overwrite semantics) and then actually run it to leave the 2048-bit /app/deploy_key.pem. Hidden cases execute the script on accepted sizes (2048/3072/4096, incl. umask 000), rejected sizes/inputs (1024, 0, negative, non-numeric, 16384) that must exit 2 and create nothing, and an overwrite case. Medium: adversarial_inputs and unsafe_action_penalty (permissions are the core), quantitative_correctness (exact bit length and exit codes), one dependent stage (script then key), tool_breadth (openssl + shell + stat).

sorrel-marsh.notes: Single-stage: group JSON sync records by (user, field), decide conflicts by value divergence, apply a two-level tie-break (recency then device priority then input order) for the winner, and emit a structured report whose total_conflicts must equal len(conflicts). Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (tie-break cascade), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (hidden tie/duplicate/empty cases), and quantitative_correctness (exact counts and winner identity verified structurally).

sorrel-quay.documented_probe: C-e37bcb4d (configure a single-node cluster to listen on a designated port via site/core config files with complementary namenode/datanode functions): covered at easy with Hadoop-style core-site.xml/hdfs-site.xml placeholders and a designated rpc endpoint; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases (textual checks plus live daemons and probes). Documented probe waiver.
sorrel-quay.notes: Single-stage: fill seven designated property values across two Hadoop-style site files; miswritten strings fail the textual check and starve the shipped daemons, which then fail the live bind and hidden probes. Small rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (fs.defaultFS URI encodes the rpc port) and adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (three independent live probes re-read the agent's files). No tool breadth, no dependency chain, no environment pressure; totals bucket to easy.

sorrel-tide.notes: Format-constrained enumeration probe: honor a compact duty-roster gate (never brute-force the full serial space), apply the exact well-formed-keycard predicate (exact length, required prefix/suffix fragments, uppercase+digits only) to every rostered emission — including near-miss decoys (off-by-one length, lowercase prefix/body, dash separator) and valid tokens riddled with the confusable characters O/0/I/1 that punish over-tightening — write EVERY retained candidate to the result file in ascending serial order, and only then select the unique SHA-256 residue match as the vault keycard. The solver is reusable: the verifier re-runs it unchanged on hidden generator modules with different serial ranges, lengths, fragments, alphabets and pins, and re-derives the expected candidate list and selection independently. Hard: the failure mode is precisely dropping the matching candidate by tightening the format (or guessing the final value instead of enumerating), and the hidden modules break any hard-coded format constant.

spume-ferry.documented_probe: C-9316fd7f (call an http endpoint carrying a computed payload): reference floor is easy and this covering task is authored at easy; the verifier re-runs the deliverable script against the live in-container service on hidden dock ids (open, closed, non-integer) and checks the printed final message against the documented formula.
spume-ferry.notes: Single flow: start a shipped local kiosk service, discover the claim route and receipt list, compute a sha256-based rendezvous payload for a dock id, POST it, and deliver the returned pier-pass string plus receipt JSON. Hidden cases re-execute the script with unseen open ids (catches hard-coded outputs), a closed id (409 -> non-zero exit, no pierpass on stdout), and a non-integer arg. Easy: no multi-step auth, no auditing, straightforward documented formula.

tarn-mesa.notes: Reverse-engineer a specified binary container (magic/version/flags header, variable header length with junk padding, optional 2-byte repeating XOR mask over the payload, either float32 endianness, row- vs column-major storage, 4-byte CRC trailer that must not be read as data) and ship a runnable extractor that numpy.saves the recovered matrix. Hard floor: the deliverable must be a general executable (/app/extract.py) plus the persisted /app/recovered.npy, verified by executing it on hidden containers that flip every flag combination (big/little endian, C/Fortran order, masked/unmasked, padded/unpadded headers) and checking exact values, shape, dtype, and orientation. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (multi-field header + mask + order/endianness interplay), adversarial_inputs (trailer trap, junk padding), hidden_case_generalization (flag-flipped hidden containers), quantitative_correctness (exact float matrix equality), and small tool/dependency credit for the two-stage write-then-run flow.

tarn-quay.notes: Medium. Single-stage: merge three snapshot export formats (CSV with RFC quoting, JSONL, JSON array), normalize types (zero-padded id/value strings -> int, whitespace-padded names stripped), skip malformed rows, resolve duplicate ids by min (value, name), and serialize one complete JSON array sorted ascending by id. Adversarial_inputs=2 (quoted/comma names, malformed rows, zero-padding, negatives, empty dir); hidden_case_generalization=2 (four distinct hidden snapshot sets incl. empty dir and reverse-ordered sources); quantitative_correctness=1 (exact content/order match); tool_breadth=1 (csv/json parsing); reasoning_depth=1 and debugging_ambiguity=1 (dedup tie-breaking). No dependency chain, environment pressure, or statefulness; totals bucket to medium. Covers C-5df6a315 (JSON list export sorted by primary key) via distinct asserts on types, order, duplicates, and completeness.

teal-assembler.notes: Core is a two-pass assembler over a fixed 5-mnemonic instruction set: pass 1 must collect labels (including forward references and label-only lines) while computing byte addresses, pass 2 emits byte-exact machine code with packed ADD registers, big-endian 16-bit JMP addresses, and load immediate range checks. Difficulty comes from the sequential label-then-encode dependency (dependent_stages=2), exact byte-encoding correctness (quantitative_correctness=2), and generalizing one program to arbitrary inputs (hidden_case_generalization=2): hidden cases cover forward/backward jumps, r15, hex and 0/255 boundary immediates, and six documented error classes (duplicate label, unknown mnemonic, wrong operand count, register out of range, immediate out of range, jump to undefined label), each required to abort nonzero with a line-numbered diagnostic and no output file.

teal-macro.notes: Single-stage: record a Vim macro register set whose combined getreg length stays at or under a fixed 40-keystroke ceiling while performing a field-reordering rewrite (WORD,NUMBER,WORD -> WORD3 WORD1 (NUMBER)) that must generalize to hidden source files with different values and field widths. The verifier sources /app/macros.vim in a clean headless Vim, checks the buffer was not modified by sourcing, measures the budget via getreg over registers a-z, applies :%g/^/normal @a itself, and compares byte-for-byte against the expected target; a static scan forbids functions/autocmds/maps/interpreter bridges so the work is genuinely done by the recorded keystrokes. Rubric nonzero for quantitative_correctness (exact output bytes and hard budget), hidden_case_generalization (three distinct hidden sources), reasoning_depth (very-magic regex economy), interaction_statefulness and tool_breadth (headless vim sourcing mechanics), adversarial_inputs (no buffer edits at source time, no-modify on source.txt).

tern-delta.notes: Focused single-competency task: produce a probability array over a fixed vocabulary meeting both forward- and reverse-KL budgets, via the documented mixing-with-uniform halving method. The verifier re-runs the deliverable on seven hidden priors/budget pairs (zero budgets returning the exact normalized prior, length-1, huge budgets, a very tight pair needing many halvings, numpy/list input polymorphism) and validates the visible /app/calibrated.json against the agent's own function. Shape/value failures (wrong length, non-finite, non-positive, unnormalized) are all probed.

tide-ember.notes: Hard. The agent must combine lookup (instruments gain table, unit factor table), parsing (multi-file JSON catalogs with many malformed-record shapes that must be skipped without crashing), descriptor normalization (value * unit_factor * gain, rounded to 6 dp), inclusive-tolerance filtering against a target, and proximity ranking (score = 1 - distance/tolerance, ascending distance with obs_id tie-break), plus a mandatory normalization-reporting string per record. The verifier executes the deliverable program on the visible fixture and on three hidden scenarios: an inclusive boundary case (distance exactly at tolerance kept, just outside dropped), an adversarial mix (unknown units/instruments, non-string ids, booleans, non-object records, a distance tie broken by obs_id, mixed unit conversions), and a zero-match case yielding []. Rubric nonzero for adversarial_inputs, quantitative_correctness (exact rounded floats, exact sort, exact reporting strings), reasoning_depth (multi-stage normalization math), and hidden_case_generalization. No resource or interaction pressure.

tide-grove.notes: Single pipeline stage with coupled artifacts: a config-driven, deterministic trainer that must save a REAL trained state_dict at <ckpt_root>/iter-<N>/model.pt where N (and hidden width, lr, seed) come from the config file and the feature dimension from the CSV header — hidden cases vary all four plus the dims (10/24/6), so any hard-coded count/shape/path fails. The verifier executes the deliverable on visible + 3 hidden cases and checks: snapshot existence at the configured iteration node, loadability with weights_only=True, exactly the four tensors of the two Linear layers by shape, finiteness/non-degeneracy/size bounds (no dummy or oversized weights), meta.json consistency, holdout + train accuracy >= 0.85, printed final_accuracy, and tensor-for-tensor determinism across two fresh runs plus equality with the delivered visible snapshot. Nonzero rubric for dependent_stages (train -> save -> reload), reasoning_depth (shape-driven state-dict contract, seeded full-batch SGD), debugging_ambiguity (determinism + exact iteration count), adversarial_inputs (unseen configs/dims), hidden_case_generalization, quantitative_correctness (accuracy thresholds).

topaz-marsh.notes: Exact weighted Max-SAT over DIMACS-style WCNF with hard/soft clauses. Hard elements: a complete (branch-and-bound or MILP) encoding is mandatory since brute force is impossible at n=48 and heuristics give suboptimal totals; correct handling of tautological clauses, unit hard pins that permanently forfeit soft weight, jointly contradictory hard clauses (HARD_UNSAT), and comment/noise tolerance. Quantitative correctness is exact-match on the optimum; verifier re-executes the solver on three hidden instances with distinct structures (large satisfiable, hard-unsat, pinned).

topaz-quarry.notes: Produce a real trained-model snapshot: config-driven architecture (input_dim/classes/max_epochs read from config.json), capped-epoch training on CPU, torch.save of exactly the two-tensor state_dict. The verifier reloads each snapshot strict=True (catching dummy, oversized, or wrong-shaped weights), checks finiteness and non-constancy, and requires >=0.90 held-out accuracy on the visible eval set and on hidden runs with different dims/class counts. Nonzero rubric for the train-then-snapshot chain, torch usage, config reasoning, adversarial dummy-snapshot traps, hidden generalization (two hidden runs), and quantitative accuracy.

topaz-vane.notes: Single-stage: keyword-token rule matching across multiple logs, per-rule match counts and sorted deduped from= IPs, threshold firing, and emission of two exact-schema JSON artifacts (alert.json with timestamp+alerts, report.json with events+statistics). Rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (schema assembly + event ordering), adversarial_inputs (malformed rules files, missing fields, empty logs), hidden_case_generalization (three hidden cases), and quantitative_correctness (counts recomputed independently by the verifier).

tundra-bridge.notes: Bringing up and operating an nginx static site end-to-end drives the hard bucket (19). Many dependent stages must compose before anything works: generate a self-signed cert named by domain, write an nginx server config (non-default HTTP port, TLS:443, named log format, per-IP rate limit, custom 404 page), install it under /etc/nginx/conf.d while deactivating the distro default site, run a syntax-clean nginx that is actually listening, and leave a resolvable /etc/hosts + nsswitch setup so localhost and the site domain (and arbitrary hidden aliases via a parameterised network_fix helper) resolve. debugging_ambiguity is high because a leftover default site, a cert/key mismatch, a rate-limit pitfall and a silent access-log failure each look 'working' from partial views. Tool breadth spans nginx config + TLS/openssl + curl + hosts/nsswitch editing + a statistics-producing self-check program. Hidden cases probe generalization (generic register/apply resolution helper, varied HTTP status paths incl. deep 404s, malformed/blank host lines) and exact output formats for the access log and the self-check (per-test CHK lines plus numeric MEAN/STD). Quantitative difficulty is modest because the stats have to be numeric but not precise.

tundra-cipher.notes: Hard via four interdependent sub-problems (9x9 constraint grid, exact big-integer packing count, multi-person+lunch/weekday business-hours slot scan, rotation-invariant neighbour enumeration) unified into a single CLI engine that must generalise to unseen instance directories. The packing instances use 28-32 items (brute-force 2^n infeasible), forcing a no-miss/no-duplicate DP; the unique 9x9 solution, the large exact integer answer, and the exact 9-line grid serialisation all demand quantitative correctness. Hidden cases include edge/malformed instances: capacity 0, a person with a zero-length availability that blocks an entire day, a 1-person and focus-absent round, a lunch break falling before the first usable slot, and a weekend day explicitly in the schedulable list, so the engine must apply every rule simultaneously rather than memorise one visible layout data-dependence. reasoning_depth 3 and dependent_stages 3 (each output depends on a separately specified sub-rule and the whole must be one coherent CLI that generalises).

tundra-engine.notes: One general CLI solver must handle five sub-problems (optimal sliding-tile search with A*, parity-based solvability, canonical zero-padded serialization, seven-pairs/thirteen-orphans win detection, four-in-a-row threat blocking, and shortest-turn maze routing under a budget). Difficulty comes from the optimal-move-search core (A*/BFS optimality over 3x3..4x4 boards), the exact-matching turn-budget/ground-truth requirements, and a broad set of adversarial/malformed inputs the hidden cases probe; all of this lands the total in the medium bucket.

tundra-jetty.notes: Hard bucket (rubric total 18). Seven competencies chained in one pipeline: author a reusable R solver (structure recovery via coupling heuristics: fixed-edge-count max-|corr| spanning tree, root-constraint orientation, child-analogy ambiguity rule; parametric network fit; ATE with the confounder adjustment set), then a hierarchical beta-binomial Stan model with a Jeffreys-type hyperprior, sample it with rstan, and publish an R Markdown document plus a legacy nbformat R-kernel notebook that load the data and DAG spec. The verifier re-runs /app/solver.R on 3 hidden topologies (chain-like, ladder, star) with different group counts and effect sizes, requiring exact directed edge sets, ATE within 0.12, and network slopes within 0.12. Difficulty derives from the multi-stage dependent pipeline (install-free but runtime C++ model compilation), the reasoning needed to design the recovery+adjustment-set logic that generalizes, and the tight quantitative tolerances; every competency carries a hard floor (one medium), so difficulty >= max floor.

tundra-keystone.notes: Three-independent gapped competencies rolled into one workload. dependent_stages=3: the pipeline's gradient-exchange correctness depends on the partition being sound and the per-rank layer assignment contiguous+zero-bias; the async scheduler's cancellation contract depends on a correct started/queued split; the mp entry depends on guarded spawn. adversarial_inputs=3: hidden probes cover world_size > num_layers (empty stages), zero-layer pipelines, cancel-all and run-all triggers, a negative (malformed) trigger, and a conversation with cap larger than the job set. hidden_case_generalization=3: the verifier re-invokes pipeline_parallel.py over fresh (world,layers,d,batch) tuples, re-invokes async_pool.py over fresh (jobs,cap,trigger), and re-executes mp_entry.py with a different pool size; all must be rerunnable from the deliverable scripts. quantitative_correctness=3: the forward must be recomputed from the archived per-layer weights and match the archived output to <1e-4, and the layer coverage of the partition must be exact. reasoning_depth is held at 2 because no single stage is conceptually deep on its own; the difficulty is the breadth of getting all three contracts independently right.

tundra-ledge.notes: Hard ML-systems task bundling three independent strands that must all hold: (1) recover a one-hidden-layer ReLU MLP's input rows from forward queries alone (kink detection + full-gradient diffs; sign/permutation ambiguity must be handled), (2) low-rank matrix completion from sparse (row,col,val) observations that must return an explicitly low-rank reconstruction within a relative-Frobenius budget, and (3) a bit-level conversion of a compressed chess .cnet file into a PyTorch state dict that must load and run. Difficulty is hard because every claimed competency carries a hard floor; difficulty comes from dependent multi-stage reasoning plus strict quantitative tolerances and hidden-case generalization (the verifier re-runs the solver's routines on different-size MLPs, rank-deficient/low-sampling matrices, and a different chess architecture).

tundra-orchid.notes: Five independent parsing/reporting artifacts, each re-checked on new hidden input by a built-in ground-truth rule. Medium comes from: (a) diagnosing the newline-accumulation bug in the CSV pipeline (debugging_ambiguity=2), (b) exact-format guarantees (quantitative_correctness=2: {3f} acceptance rate, bare ISO-500 timestamp, exact fixed report lines, one CSV output line per input record), (c) hidden generalization of every script against the setup's own ground-truth parser, and (d) a dependent re-run/verify step on the CSV pipeline. All competency floors are easy/medium, so medium is the correct bucket.

tundra-quill.notes: Single pure-JS module with an exact export interface (plain function step on a cell-state object, module.exports = { step: step }, no imports/classes). Logic: 4-direction neighbour eligibility (bounds, blocked flag, object checks), min-cost selection with a fixed directional tie-break order, battery-exhaustion hold rule, and layered malformed-state fallbacks. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (tie-break + cost rules), debugging_ambiguity (order-of-checks subtleties), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (empty grid, out-of-bounds, null cells, missing fields, battery edge). No tool breadth, dependency chain, or resource pressure; totals bucket to medium.

tundra-terrace.notes: Hard ML-artifact task. The agent must (a) reconstruct a complete causal-transformer forward pass purely from a state dict and a hyperparameter file, (b) reproduce, to a tight tolerance, oracle-computed scores for every sample, (c) persist a low-rank factorization of every linear weight matrix whose significant-singular-value count respects the configured rank, and (d) keep the whole engine under a strict 6000-byte source budget. Reasoning depth (3): deriving the exact norm/MHA/GELU arithmetic from the weight layout and matching float-level outputs. Quantitative correctness (3): hidden cases compare scores within 2e-3 and enforce low-rank singular-value bounds. Hidden-case generalization (3): four hidden cases vary d/layers/vocab/ctx/heads/rank, so the engine must be architecture-parametric, not fixture-hardcoded. Resource pressure (2): hard source byte budget plus tightly bounded runtime.

umber-anchor.notes: Medium: a four-stage environment-provisioning chain. Dependent stages 3: author a pinned dependency manifest (numpy/pandas + plotting/scientific lib), resolve a pairwise numpy-vs-scipy version conflict in the environment spec, and install/configure a zsh framework (theme + exact plugin set); a fourth deliverable is a generalized version-constraint checker. Reasoning depth 2: diagnosing which side of the numpy-scipy conflict to re-pin requires reasoning about the library upper-bound requirement (`ResolutionImpossible`). Debugging ambiguity 2: pip error messages for the conflict are noisy and the fix has multiple valid directions. Adversarial 2: hidden manifest cases include a missing package, an installed-version breach of an upper bound, combined comma specs, and comment/include-only edge files. Resource pressure 1: the verifier pip-installs three isolated venvs inside the time budget. Task difficulty (14) >= competency floor (medium).

umber-engine.notes: Total 18 (hard). Four competencies, each verified on hidden inputs. The sequence must be implemented identically under two independent runtimes (Python + safe Rust), where the Rust source is additionally statically scanned for zero unsafe/FFI/ABI constructs, so small off-by-one or recurrence errors show up as cross-runtime disagreement (quantitative_correctness=3, hidden_case_generalization=3). The wasm deliverable must satisfy an exact ABI: boot() fills 256 bytes of linear memory from a documented formula, producer() returns a dynamic offset in [0,239], consumer() reads exactly 16 bytes at that offset and returns their sum; the verifier reads the same 16 bytes host-side and compares byte-for-byte and against the integer (dependent_stages=2, reasoning_depth=2, quantitative=3) — wrong length/offset silently break the sum on hidden seeds. The grpc toolchain must be importable system-wide and its code generator must produce importable bindings from an unseen hidden proto (hidden_case_generalization). Difficulty is genuinely distributed across tools (system apt installs, pip toolchain, clang wasm32, rustc, wasmtime host ABI, grpc_tools.protoc) and the exact-output byte/integer checks, not from length alone. The two hard-floor competencies (sequence-in-two-runtimes, safe Rust with zero unsafe) are met head-on; no probe is documented.

umber-flotilla.notes: Medium web task covering C-84b8017c (inputs scaling to thousands of assets): the verifier replays a 6,000-asset hidden portfolio plus a 1,500-asset visible fixture against the delivered Flask service, requiring linear-time ingest, exact per-file-order float aggregation, deterministic top-10 tie-breaking, zero-total and empty-portfolio edge cases, strict 400/404 validation (bools and non-finite numbers rejected), and a generated /app/summary.json deliverable. resource_pressure=2 for the scale dimension; remaining rubric is intentionally light so the total buckets to medium.

umber-gasket.notes: Hand-built computation-engine task rated hard (rubric total 19). (a) /app/eval.py is a Scheme-like evaluator that MUST read the first stdin line as the path to an M program and relay later stdin to that program, while its prints go to stdout; the hidden verifier feeds meta-programs (a self-interpreter written in M) and a stdin-reading program, and demands the exact printed value of a subject expression through one extra interpreter level (self-interpretation). A loop-only or feature-thin evaluator cannot run the meta kernel (needs lists, quote, closures, apply, recursion) and fails. (b) /app/moves.fen.rules is an ordered list of [pattern,replacement] regex-rewrite pairs that apply to a starting FEN to enumerate legal next knight positions, one per output line, without a runtime move loop; hidden FENs include corners, edges and a knight-less board (empty output). (c) /app/gate_net.txt is a combinational logic-gate network computing fib(floor(sqrt(n))) for 7-bit n, verified against a reference simulator on squares/neighbours/edges; /app/simulate.py must evaluate it. reasoning_depth=3: the metacircular evaluator, the regex rewrite pipeline, combinational SOP synthesis. debugging_ambiguity=2: exact-line outputs, FEN set parity, stray-bit off-by-ones. adversarial_inputs=3: hidden subjects differ per meta program, hidden FEN/cell spread includes edges and a knight-less board, hidden n values are squares+neighbors+edges. hidden_case_generalization=3: every deliverable is re-run on hidden inputs. dependent_stages=3: gate network computed from the sqrt→fib mapping and simulate.py must agree with the reference; the evaluator must host a self-interpreter and relay stdin. No competency is faked.

umber-larch.documented_probe: C-500da2a9 (estimate an average treatment effect to high accuracy): this task exercises the full capability — derive the backdoor adjustment set from a supplied DAG (excluding the instrument, mediator and collider), fit an outcome model flexible enough for a nonlinear/interactive DGP, compute the ATE by g-computation, and land within ±0.06 of the true effect on hidden studies.
umber-larch.notes: Failure modes probed directly: adjusting for the mediator/collider or failing to exclude the instrument dilutes or biases the estimate (far outside tolerance); an additive-linear outcome model misses the squared terms and treatment interactions (bias > tolerance); wrong number formatting/scale is rejected by the strict 6-decimal single-number format check. Hidden studies vary n, sigma, effect signs/strengths, column names and DAG topology (instrument-only-parent, confounder chain, binary/continuous confounder mixes), so hard-coding the visible estimate fails.

umber-mantle.notes: Seven slice competencies bundled. The make-or-break skill is reassembling a hexdump that carries an offset column and an ascii annotation (must strip both via token filtering) into a compressed streamed tar member -- reasoning_depth=3. dependent_stages=3 because out.bin requires (a) streaming exactly one archive member without expanding, then (b) reassembling that hexdump; exclusions require auditing every entry (caches, vendored deps, build objects, version metadata, 0600 creds). hidden_case_generalization is required by 3 distinct hidden trees (plaintext printer, a __pycache__-less tree, different names/bytes). Bucket total = 19 -> hard. task.toml difficulty is set to hard because the spec max competency floor (reassemble-hexdump) is hard, exceeding the nominal easy target.

umber-prism.notes: Full descriptor-screening chain: implement a recursive formula parser (nesting, hydrate multipliers via U+00B7 and ASCII dot, leading part multipliers), a descriptor lookup+arithmetic stage (molar mass from a JSON mass table), tolerance filtering with a rounding-defined inclusive boundary, normalized proximity scoring (dnorm/score with a tolerance==0 special case), deterministic ranking (distance then id tie-break), plus a counts/echo report, and deliver the program + artifacts produced by running it on the visible fixtures. Hidden cases vary mass tables, cover nested/hydrate formulas, unknown elements, unbalanced parens, lowercase starts, whitespace, bare multipliers, missing/non-string formulas, a non-JSON line, an exact-hit d=0 row, an exact inclusive-boundary row, a distance tie, and an empty dataset. Rubric nonzero for dependent_stages (parser -> descriptor -> filter -> rank -> report -> artifacts), reasoning_depth (recursive grammar + rounding contract), debugging_ambiguity (boundary/tie semantics), adversarial_inputs and hidden_case_generalization (4 hidden cases), quantitative_correctness (exact floats, sort order, counts). No tool breadth, resource pressure, or statefulness; totals bucket to hard.

umber-quill.notes: Medium (sum 11): five distinct log-processing competencies bundled into two runnable programs (jsonl group-sort + equal-thirds round partitioning; stack-trace-to-frames parsing with prefix/:: stripping; IP-presence-gated last-date regex extraction; and an incident tool with IPv4 validation + cross-log dedup). The agent must specify exact deterministic formats (raw-line preservation for rounds, line-number row keys, JSON schemas, exit codes) that the verifier then revalidates by re-running /app/logproc.py and /app/respond.py on fresh hidden inputs, including malformed JSON lines, duplicate microsecond timestamps, invalid-octet IPs, empty-report targets, and invalid-IP rejection (non-zero exit + marker). Reasoning depth and quantitative correctness come from the aggregate-thirds round partition and dedup/sort semantics; hidden_case_generalization captures the runnable-on-new-inputs contract across four hidden scenarios.

umber-ridge.notes: Bucket sum 14 -> medium. The task chains three medium-floor competencies: (1) union three differently-formatted sources (json/csv/parquet) into one canonical schema and persist as a numpy structured array; (2) cross-check per-region summed balances against reported grand totals to pin the single inconsistent figure; (3) push reconciled values into a sheet grid through an API at exact cell addresses. Hidden generality is high (the deliverable must be re-runnable on three distinct source sets incl. empty source, numeric-as-string, stray non-canonical region), and per-cell / per-field quantitative correctness must be exact (cent-exact float sums, fixed address mapping). Matches the medium floor of every claimed competency.

umber-summit.notes: Four chained security operations builds: (1) a rule engine that applies a JSON rule set to log files — counting matches and unique source IPs per rule and emitting alert.json/report.json with exact schemas, which must survive hidden rule/log sets including empty logs, missing rule keys, and regexes that raise re.error; (2) deterministic tar.gz snapshot sealed with gpg --symmetric --cipher-algo AES256 discovered from man gpg, with no plaintext archive left anywhere; (3) recovering an unknown 8-byte key from the cipher oracle via chosen zero-plaintext within a strict 25s wall-clock budget; (4) a pickle __reduce__ gadget whose load runs os.system and produces /app/pwn-proof.txt. reasoning_depth=3 from implementing the gpg option discovery (strongest of AES-128/192/256), the chosen-plaintext key fold, and robust defaulting for malformed rules; adversarial_inputs=2 from hidden edge/malformed rule+log sets and the oracle hidden re-key; hidden_case_generalization=3 because /app/detect.sh must run on brand-new rule/log sets and oracle.py must recover a fresh hidden key; resource_pressure=2 from the hard-time oracle budget.

umber-terrace.notes: Hard: four independent numeric-solver deliverables (MPS MIP solver, LP corner enumeration, composite quartic+quadratic+coupling minimization, entropic Sinkhorn OT), each of which must run on unseen hidden inputs. Reasoning depth 3: correct convex/nonconvex stationary-point termination and exact vertex enumeration from square subsystems. Debugging ambiguity 2: a premature/divergent optimizer or wrong coupling scaling yields wrong numbers with no obvious error. Adversarial 3: hidden MPS includes an integer MIP (offset ambiguity, dedicated dense columns), a degenerate corner LP with duplicate corners, large-scale (n=120) quartic and (45x65) OT. Quantitative 3: objective / MIP value / transport cost must match independent reference within tight tolerances. Resource pressure 2: all four runs must stay inside the time budget. Task difficulty (22) >= competency floor (hard).

umber-vault.notes: Chained reproducible-CPU-training pipeline: (1) split.py must emit fixed, seed-deterministic, non-overlapping train/val/test CSVs that the verifier re-derives byte-for-byte with the documented algorithm on fresh and tiny hidden datasets; (2) train.py must define the solver (SGD/CPU/iteration caps) and the documented 48->64->2 network and train /app/model_snapshot.pt that re-fits to train accuracy >= 0.90; (3) finetune.py reuses the base snapshot and must adapt to a previously-unseen hidden fold, yielding a new loadable checkpoint scoring >= 0.90 on that fold; (4) predict.py emits exactly one digit per row to stdout AND a result file, and the verifier cross-checks both against a reload of the model snapshot on hidden holdout rows; (5) the bag scorer must stream per-patch scores with bounded RAM and near-linear time — the verifier feeds a generated 1.2M-patch bag under a hard RSS cap and wall-clock deadline and verifies the per-bag majority labels against an independent snapshot recompute. dependent_stages=3 because split -> trained snapshot -> fine-tune -> predict -> bag scoring is one chain where each stage feeds the next and a failure anywhere cascades. hidden_case_generalization=3 because split, prediction, fine-tuning and the large-bag iterator all run on fresh hidden inputs the agent never sees. resource_pressure=3 from the strict memory bound plus deadline on the bag path; an agent that materializes the whole bag (numpy/torch full-tensor or eager pandas read) exceeds the RSS cap. quantitative_correctness=2: partition CSVs must be byte-identical to a reference rebuild and bag labels must match an independent snapshot recompute exactly (tie handled deterministically). The problem has zero interaction/unsafe surface, so those dimensions stay 0; adversarial_inputs=2 covers tiny-split rounding, ragged bag sizes and empty-bag/edge shapes.

umber-yonder.notes: Hard 19/30. Multi-stage git forensics: automate a password-SSH clone, then design a reusable scrubber that recovers a committed-then-deleted credential, rewrites all reachable history (trees, blobs, commit messages) with typed placeholders while leaving every unrelated file byte-identical, and prunes dangling objects so a byte-level scan of the object store finds no trace. Hidden fixtures place secrets in working files, commit messages, and dangling-only objects, include case variants and a benign lookalike, and a malformed non-repository input. Requires the scrubber to generalize (hidden_case_generalization=3) and exact byte/placeholder correctness (quantitative_correctness=3). Difficulty is at/above the max competency floor (hard, C-a9d4f82b / C-162592ad).

umbral-mesh.notes: Hard: recover a directed acyclic graph from raw observational samples by implementing a precisely-specified multi-step heuristic (Pearson max-|r| spanning tree with a strict tie-break, BFS orientation away from a declared root, and domain-hint flips that override BFS orientation). The ambiguity-resolution stage is where set equality breaks: a hint that conflicts must flip the BFS direction, while a hint referencing a non-skeleton pair or a non-network column must be ignored; distractor columns outside spec['columns'] must be excluded. The deliverable solver is re-executed on four hidden fixtures with different column counts (3-8), roots that are not the generative source, distractor columns, and mixed hint semantics, so a hard-coded or partially-implemented heuristic fails set equality. Rubric weights reasoning_depth (multi-stage ordering-sensitive algorithm), debugging_ambiguity (hint-conflict vs ignore), adversarial_inputs (distractors, non-source roots), hidden_case_generalization, and quantitative_correctness (exact edge-set equality).

vane-marsh.documented_probe: C-92072676 (connect to a postgres service using compose-provided credentials): the covering task derives host/port/db/user/password from a compose-style file and establishes a live connection; wrong credentials or the wrong published port make the store unreachable and the report empty. Verifier executes the deliverable on hidden compose/database pairs with different credentials, ports and quoting.
vane-marsh.notes: Medium: two-stage (parse compose -> live connect -> structured export). The visible instance uses a non-default published port (5433) and scram auth, so a wrong password genuinely fails to connect. Hidden cases vary database name, user, password, quoting and row population (empty, single, duplicate/fractional rows). Small rubric nonzero for the parse->connect->export dependency chain, psql tooling, live-service statefulness, hidden generalization, and quantitative exactness of the JSON report.

vanta-mesa.notes: Single fetch + parse: GET / on a local origin, scope parsing to <section id="offers"> while ignoring same-markup decoy articles in #care-guides, unescape entities, handle missing price/stock spans (null), Sold out (0), sub-unit and integral prices, messy whitespace, and an empty offers section. Dependent stage: the agent must start the origin before running the client to save answer.json. Hidden scenarios rerun the client unchanged on fresh origin configs. Small rubric nonzero for reasoning_depth (scoped section parsing), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (three hidden scenarios), and quantitative_correctness (typed null/int/float fields). No tool breadth or environment pressure; totals bucket to easy.

vellum-notch.notes: Single-stage selective streaming: extract exactly one member of a gzipped tar to stdout without materializing the archive, knowing that full extraction would clobber the coexisting live audit log (same-named stale member) and scatter restricted credential payloads on disk. The verifier re-executes the deliverable script on hidden archives with different member names/nesting, requires byte-exact stdout, an untouched sentinel log, an unmodified archive and zero new files in the scratch dir, and rejects any extracted leftovers under /app. Nonzero rubric for tar streaming tooling, unsafe-action penalty (sensitive leakage/clobber) and hidden generalization; totals bucket to easy.

velvet-atlas.notes: Targeted account deactivation over a REST API: issue DELETEs for exactly the cancelled attendee IDs while every survivor remains queryable and still authenticates at the badge endpoint. The verifier executes the deliverable client against fresh emulator instances with different rosters and different target sets (over-deletion or under-deletion fails), and checks the append-only audit trail to confirm the work went through the API. Small rubric nonzero for tool_breadth (HTTP client, process management), adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (hidden rosters/targets), and interaction_statefulness (live service state). Totals bucket to easy.

velvet-ember.notes: Hard: patch header-name normalization so CR/LF/NUL (and all non-token) characters are rejected while benign token names keep their exact canonical title forms; the documented failure mode is over-broad validation that mangles or rejects valid headers. Also wire it into a WSGI relay with structured 400s (invalid_header/duplicate_header/bad_request) and a CLI mapping deliverable. adversarial_inputs=2 and hidden_case_generalization=2 (control-char matrix plus benign edge families: empty tokens, digits, dots, unicode, non-strings), debugging_ambiguity=1 (precise token-set boundary), interaction_statefulness=1 (live gateway sequence with duplicate-collision detection), dependent_stages=1 (canonical_map.json derived from running the CLI).

velvet-quay.notes: Temporal-validity probe: every fact in the ledger is qualified by dates, and all classification is evaluated against a fixed reference date read from the audit file. The agent must (1) replay amendments onto base fields with latest-effective_on<=as_of wins (later-list-position tie-break), value-null clears the field, non-amendable/malformed amendments ignored; (2) classify charters with mixed inclusive/exclusive boundary semantics (end_on inclusive, terminated_on exclusive, start_on as-of-amended, signed_on existence check) into active/pending/excluded; (3) count malformed lines; (4) emit exactly-sorted ids and vessel aggregates. Hard: the amendment replay plus asymmetric boundary rules is easy to get subtly wrong, and the verifier re-runs the deliverable on hidden ledgers with different as-of dates, amendment patterns (retro-active, future, clearing, double amendments) and junk lines, so an incomplete date predicate keeps outdated facts in the results and fails.

vesper-broker.notes: Two chained stages (dependent_stages=1): author a pickle deserialization gadget (__reduce__ -> os.system) via /app/gadget.py, then deliver the crafted message through the stock consumer so the escape marker is produced by pickle.load itself. Covers C-3c7bf71e (malicious serialized object whose load executes a command) at medium: the marker must be produced by deserialization inside the unmodified worker, re-verified in fresh processes. generalization=2 because the verifier mints fresh mission tokens (never the visible one) and re-runs /app/gadget.py unchanged, so a hard-coded payload fails; adversarial_inputs=1 (marker deleted before every consumer run, exact content match). quantitative_correctness=1 for the exact marker bytes; debugging_ambiguity=1 (a pickle that dispatch.py refuses to load, or a gadget that writes the marker itself, both surface as a missing marker). No tool breadth or resource pressure; totals bucket to medium.

vine-delta.notes: Bundle of five pure-python computational competencies under the puzzle-algorithmics family: (1) periodic-scheduling maximum-gap via explicit least-common-multiple scan, (2) weighted-return dot product with strict tolerance and unequal-length rejection, (3) exact 9x9 sudoku completion via constraint-propagation backtracking, (4) a turn-based lane strategy that must emit exactly one legal in-bounds move per turn (a hold marker -1 when no open cell remains, and ERR for malformed descriptors so an invalid descriptor can never stall or crash the run), and (5) a strategy entrypoint `play(sock)` exposing the exact one-socket-parameter signature. Difficulty is medium: the flattest competency floor that can be honestly claimed for the resulting set (medium), with hidden-case generalization and quantitative correctness at 2 (multiple independent hidden gap / dot-product / sudoku / game scenarios including malformed and edge inputs), adversarial_inputs at 2 (malformed lanes, non-9x9 grids, unequal vector lengths, non-positive cycles), and interaction_statefulness at 2 (the multi-turn lane strategy must reply once-and-once per turn without pausing or double-moving across distinct boards). No external tools beyond the Python 3.12 stdlib are required (tool_breadth 0); pure numerical/algorithmic work, so resource_pressure and unsafe-action penalty are 0. The two spec slice-competencies with hard reference floors (C-fef928b0 chess-as-regex; C-f49d1fc8 RL policy threshold) are explicitly dropped rather than forced into this lean stdlib-only numerical family.

vine-forge.documented_probe: C-c3adcbc5 (achieve memory-efficient near-linear scaling on large bags): reference floor is medium; this covering task requires streaming a fixed-scorer forward over a ~2M-patch multi-bag CSV under a hard 450 MB peak-RSS cap and a 240 s deadline, with exact per-bag positive counts on the visible and hidden bags and error/empty-file edges.
vine-forge.notes: Streaming inference over huge bags: the deliverable must chunk-read the CSV (a full float64 materialization of the stress bag needs > 500 MB and busts the 450 MB VmHWM cap), apply the fixed 32->16->1 scorer, and emit first-occurrence-ordered per-bag positive counts. resource_pressure=3 (measured peak RSS + deadline on the stress bag), quantitative_correctness=2 (exact counts on visible/hidden bags, small tolerance only for fp tie noise on the stress bag), adversarial_inputs=2 (non-numeric feature, missing columns, header-only file), hidden_case_generalization=2 (unseen bag sizes/ids including a bag far larger than any single chunk).

vine-helix.notes: Bundled system-administration repair task (total 20 = hard; two bundled competencies floor at hard: C-58dbebf6 running-task cleanup-on-cancellation and C-90cc2aa9 verbatim terminal capture, so the bucket must be >= hard). The agent authors an idempotent /app/configure.sh that must fix ALL of: password-based login for account juna (crypt-verified, unlocks the shadow entry), the shared /app/shared area (group petal, mode-750 so group members read while non-members broka are denied), restored execute+read on the group's shell scripts, cProfile profiling of four python workloads with recorded stats plus a band.txt that reads slow/fast totals and confirms faster_ok, authoring the node trial-checker solution and running the bundled node runner to write/read results.json until all PASS, purging two config+PID lifecycle files, fixing the cleanup worker forever so cancellation still completes in-flight cleanup (run_tester.sh gate), and capturing finish.sh's banner byte-for-byte into dump.txt. The verifier independently re-runs configure.sh (idempotent), diffs dump.txt against a fresh banner run, and re-runs the fixperms deliverable against hidden permission trees (scripts mode 000, read-only 0400, execute-only 0111, nested subdirs, an empty tree, and a nonexistent target) with a per-file expected manifest. dependent_stages=3, tool_breadth=3 (chpasswd/usermod, sshd_config, crypt, find/chmod, cProfile/pstats, node runner, su, signal-handling python); reasoning_depth=2, debugging_ambiguity=2, quantitative_correctness=2 (auth verify, numeric turn counts, time bands, exact modes), adversarial_inputs + hidden_case_generalization=2 through the hidden permission trees (incl. malformed 000/exec-only/empty/nonexistent). interaction_statefulness=2 via the cancellation/customer expectation that the in-flight bundle still completes cleanup before exit. Only moderate resource pressure (blocked runs), local-only unsafe-action surface.

vine-inlet.documented_probe: C-8c2c83d5 (respect declared dependency constraints) has a hard reference floor in the global inventory, but here it is exercised at an intentionally easy level: the constraint is simply 'install exactly the two pinned top-level packages and only lower the react-family versions in an already-closed manifest, adding/removing nothing'. It is a comprehension/respect of an explicit manifest contract rather than the full 'implement functionality with a single allowed crate' scenario, which does not fit an environment/dependency-management task. The task as a whole stays easy per its reference target.
vine-inlet.notes: A repair-and-lock environment task. dependent_stages=1: the upgraded lotusfields is what makes /app/tools/probe.py (which requires the dtype_backend= keyword) run at all, and pinned.txt must agree with the venv as finally installed. tool_breadth=2: venv pip repair (ensurepip), offline pip version upgrade from a local flat index, and a JSON manifest edit. debugging_ambiguity=1: the venv ships with pip removed and an outdated lotusfields, so the agent must diagnose which of several broken facts blocks the probe. hidden_case_generalization=1: the fixed probe harness must keep working over fresh hidden tables plus documented malformed/empty edge cases with exact error contracts. quantitative_correctness=1: the probe's total_flux sum/round is recomputed independently by the verifier. Totals to 5 -> easy.

vine-ledge.notes: Environment-provisioning task (medium, total 13): the agent authors an idempotent /app/provision.sh that must create two named venvs, install a gRPC toolchain and a Jupyter notebook server SYSTEM-WIDE at exact pinned versions, install the chain-query package + Flask + requests into a serve venv, and launch two persistent background services -- all WITHOUT disturbing the platform-pinned torch/transformers baseline (offline_load.py + an exact-version check fail if it is altered). Exact-version pinning throughout gives quantitative_correctness=2 and tool_breadth=2 (venvs, grpc tools, jupyter, flask, pip freeze lock); dependent_stages=2 because every subsystem must be consistent and the provisioner must be idempotent/re-runnable; the verifier re-runs provision.sh and pushes 4 hidden /height cases (valid, mixed-case+whitespace normalization, bad-length, non-hex) against the live service so hidden_case_generalization=2 and adversarial_inputs=2; debugging_ambiguity=2 because failures surface as missing ports, broken imports, or version drift. No multi-stage recurrence beyond one idempotent re-run, no statefulness-beyond-daemon, no unsafe-action pressure.

vine-mantle.notes: Hard red/purple-team recovery pipeline. Multiple dependent stages: (1) enumerate strictly-formatted passphrase candidates on CPU, derive a SHA-1 structural count filter from the documented subkey-seed constraint (units digit equals count of a-f letters in the 40-hex digest), probe the encrypted header with p7zip to isolate the vault key, decrypt and extract the member, parse out the credentials. (2) Sanitize a git repo by replacing only the byte-contaminated tracked files (mixed letter-case leaks), proving absence case-insensitively. (3) Patch a vulnerable Java jar-upload filename resolver so only the base name survives separators, percent-encoded separators and traversal/mask components, then rebuild the runtime jar. (4) generate and place a self-signed cert+key pair in a conventions directory with domain-named filenames. Difficulty comes from adversarial jar inputs (traversal/`%2F`/`%5C`/mask), the SHA-1 subkey constraint requiring genuine enumeration+filter+probe reasoning, strict multi-step dependences, and generalized re-running of the solver on a second encrypted archive. max competency floor = hard (java jar-upload rebuild).

vine-pier.notes: Total 18 = hard (bucketing: max competency floor in spec is hard, C-ce192866 read a network checkpoint + BPE vocabulary from C, so the bucket must be >= hard). A self-contained local-inference lifecycle pipeline on a bespoke VINER1 checkpoint: (1) author a dependency-free pure-C reader (ckpt_reader.c) that parses the little-endian tensor format and the tab-separated byte-pair vocabulary and prints an exact digest (FNV-1a-64 over each raw tensor + dims/nelems + id->token map); the verifier compiles it and diffs stdout byte-for-byte against an independent reference on BOTH the shipped and a hidden checkpoint (different vocab_size/max_gen/revision/dims). (2) greedy target-sequence generation (generate.py): deterministic argmax next-token loop over the target tensor with ties broken to the lowest index; re-run on fresh hidden prompts token-for-token. (3) speculative draft-and-verify (speculative.py): draft a K-token block from the draft tensor, compare each proposed token to the target sequence up to first mismatch, accept the matching prefix, append the verified true target token on the first mismatch, extend the context, and record n_drafted / n_accepted / block verdicts -- hidden K/target combos (wholly-accepted draft-greedy target, short target, K=1) drive off-by-one checks. (4) retrieval at a pinned revision (retrieve.py): L2-normalized mean-of-token-embeddings + cosine, rank desc with ties to lower doc index, return selected + 5th; revision must match the checkpoint. (5) persist the fitted model to pickle; (6) emit params.json in an exact two-peak (W/B) layout. six competencies chained on one container; byte/token/cosine/count correctness plus fresh-input generalization carry the difficulty; no GPU, no network.

vine-terrace.documented_probe: The reference floors for the primer-design (hard), causal-adjustment (hard) and jaxley-biophysics (hard) competencies are intentionally exercised in a compact, self-contained form: a single small primer parts table (3-4 parts) with known flanks, a hand-sized causal DAG (<=6 nodes) with a declared effect and optional forbid list, and one small SWC morphology + params JSON ported into three jaxley channel classes. Each is real (correct primer overhang/anneal/Tm bounds, genuine minimal back-door adjustment sets, genuine ODE kinetics), so the competencies are honestly exercised, but the data scale keeps the overall task at the medium bucket rather than hard. Nothing is dropped or faked.
vine-terrace.notes: Five slice competencies bundled into one /app/analyze.py whose public API is re-run on hidden inputs per competency: a size-configurable normalized 2D histogram with inclusive max edges; a ';'-delimited/','-decimal spectrum parser returning clean x/y; all inclusion-minimal back-door adjustment sets for a named effect (d-separation + descendants/forbid exclusions); golden-gate primer design with Wallace Tm and exact reference TSV serialization; and a NEURON MOD -> jaxley channel port driven to a voltage trace compared to a reference within tolerance. Difficulty comes from reasoning_depth (causal/back-door + Tm selection), dependent_stages (program authors + runs + verifier re-runs functions on visible and hidden inputs), hidden_case_generalization (all five have fresh hidden fixtures), tool_breadth (numpy, networkx/d-separation, jaxley), quantitative_correctness (exact TSV/JSON and trace tolerance). Rubric total 13 -> medium (10-17).

vine-yonder.notes: Medium band (total 15). Six linked deliverables push dependent_stages (2): a broken-proxy egress fetch, a Spark standalone cluster (master+worker launched by hand, then local[*] and spark:// submits), a chained three-stage pipeline, and a 60s monitor. Debugging_ambiguity (2) is the proxy-override diagnosis plus the missing-helper/missing-dir pipeline faults; reasoning_depth (2) spans choosing the correct config/split from a manifest, wiring a live JSON RPC, and neutralising the egress fault. Quantitative_correctness (2) needs a byte-for-byte fetch match, exact reserved-split totals, accurate status/block/tx/account fields, machine-readable runtimes, and a monitor that spans ~60s at ~10s intervals. hidden_case_generalization (2) re-runs load-dataset.py on an alternate hub repo (with non-numeric/blank cells, matching the documented skip rules) and chain-query.py against a second dev-mode node. Each rubric floor among the claimed competencies is <= medium, so no documented_probe is required.

white-bell.documented_probe: C-e9521e76 (construct multi-hop SPARQL joins across several related resource types): reference floor is hard but the covering task exercises it at medium; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases. Documented probe waiver.
white-bell.notes: Conjunctive graph-pattern (SPARQL-like) join over a triple list. The main difficulty is correct join / consistency semantics: handling variables in arbitrary positions (subject/predicate/object), self-joins (chains), single empty binding for all-constant patterns, empty result vs empty-domain handling, and deterministic ordering (join_order first-occurrence, bindings sorted by variable names alphabetically). All this must generalize to hidden inputs the program is re-run on, so the solver must model variable-value domains and cross-product enumeration rather than match the one provided query. stdlib only, no network attached.

wick-lantern.notes: Single-deliverable Jupyter Server config (C-9feab250, floor easy). The verifier both checks the documented assignment lines textually (both ServerApp and NotebookApp aliases) and genuinely executes the config: jupyter server is launched under five hidden port scenarios (two explicit LANTERN_PORT values, unset, non-integer, out-of-range) and must bind the expected port, answer a tokenless /api/status with 200, and be reachable via the container's non-loopback address (all-interfaces bind plus allow_remote_access). interaction_statefulness=1 for the server start/poll/stop lifecycle; reasoning_depth=1 for the env-var integer-range fallback; quantitative_correctness=1 for exact bind/HTTP results. Small totals bucket to easy.

willow-bridge.notes: Total 12 (medium). The jupyter-server competency (C-9feab250, floor easy) is achieved by an executable config file the verifier genuinely launches with `jupyter server --config=...` and validates by actual loopback bind + tokenless HTTP 200, so the config must load, bind the env-sourced port, and switch auth off. reasoning_depth=2 comes from weighting the octet restriction into one self-contained strict IPv4 ERE (varial-digit 0..255 with no leading zeros, four groups, full-string anchors) so leading-zero and out-of-range octets are rejected; adversarial_inputs=2 and hidden_case_generalization=2 from the hidden per-line corpora (mixed legal/illegal, leading-zero/out-of-range stress, surrounding-alphanumeric-and-whitespace corpus incl. empty lines) plus four distinct Jupyter port scenarios (explicit ports, unset, non-integer fallback). quantitative_correctness=2: every label and every bind/200 result must match the independent ground truth exactly. interaction_statefulness=1: the verifier must start/stop long-lived Jupyter server processes and poll bind readiness. resource_pressure=0 (small collection, stdlib/gawk only).

willow-hearth.notes: Hard. One C program /app/decode.c must implement the 'vigil' 16-bit 4-round SPN from the documented spec, mount linear-cryptanalysis bias statistics and exact verification over the compact 16-bit seed space to recover the round subkey from known plaintext/ciphertext pairs, expose it via uint32_t recover_round_key(const char*) (the required calling convention), and decrypt a block ciphertext; plus crack an encrypted zip's dictionary password, build a combined key+cert PEM, and write creds.txt. The verifier compiles decode.c and re-runs it on 4 hidden scenarios (different keys/pair counts/targets) checking recovered 32-bit key and plaintext, plus the visible key/record, the PEM parse/matching-key, and the passphrase that unlocks the archive. Hard: reasoning_depth (reverse-engineering the cipher and implementing the attack in C), dependent_stages (crack->decode->decrypt->creds->PEM pipeline), hidden_case_generalization (4 re-runs), quantitative_correctness (exact key/record), ad subtle adversarial_inputs (all-caps hex, large keys). No system services or dangerous actions.

willow-quill.notes: Reproduce higher-order semantics exactly: a self-observing stateful ledger closure (deposit/withdraw/log/undo edge cases, unknown commands raise), currying with reusable triples, variadic left-to-right composition (0/1/many functions, identity base), a mutually recursive bracket scanner (balanced + max depth with ValueError semantics), and a variadic probe closure recording its own call count and previous arguments. Medium: five interacting higher-order contracts, adversarial edge cases (empty-log undo, ([)], empty string), hidden-case generalization via import-time probing against an independent reference.

willow-upland.notes: Hard bucket (rubric total 18). One scenario bundles seven distinct competencies the agent must satisfy simultaneously: an idempotent, LF-only, allowlist-constrained bash script that recreates the /app/out/{records,summary} tree, scans /app/logs/*.log into a TOKEN=n severity table whose counts must match `grep -iw` word-boundary ground truth exactly (mixed-case tokens count, but overlapping words such as INFO inside information or WARN inside WARNING must NOT), cleans /app/stage back to the allowed {*.proof, MANIFEST} plus-preserved scratch subtree, regenerates its own output cleanly on every invocation, and a Makefile that compiles both serial and pgen executables from src/*.c into /app/bin (including rebuild-from-clean and -j2). reasoning_depth=3: the allowlist contract (no command substitution, no backticks, only a whitelist of utilities such as mkdir/grep/wc/printf) conflicts with the requirement to emit exact severity totals without eval or command substitution, so the correct solution must count lines via pipelines. debugging_ambiguity=2: word-boundary semantics of mixed-case/overlapping/filename-token cases are easy to get subtly wrong (WARNING vs WARN, INFORMATION vs INFO, INFORMATIONx). adversarial_inputs=3: hidden empty-logs dir (glob with no matches must yield all-zero counts), mixed/overlap log sets, an unrelated cleanup file set, and a pre-existing tree + sentinel that must survive two runs. hidden_case_generalization=3: test.sh seeds each hidden fixture into /app and re-runs bash /app/fix.sh, and re-runs make across clean/parallel states; a solver overfit to the visible fixtures fails. dependent_staging=2: both the idempotent fix run and the make build must land and interlock.

willow-wharf.notes: Medium (total 15). One scenario spanning four toolchains, each with an independently re-verified deliverable and its own strict contract: (1) a Coq file on the image that is deliberately left admitting, which the consultant must complete by structural induction (base reflexivity, step rewrites the IH and uses plus-commutativity via lia), terminating in Qed with no Admitted/admit/Oops tokens; coqc must compile it to a .vo and two hidden dependent .v files must link against the compiled module via Require Import proof and derive corollaries, so incomplete or admitted proofs fail. (2) a sympy script that integrates hidden expressions over [0,1] and prints exact simplified closed forms (string-identical to a freshly computed sp.simplify(sp.expand(...)) result, so numerics/unsimplified forms fail), with an unparseable input that must exit 2. (3) an R script whose two entry-point names are regex-matched verbatim and whose willow_sample(n,a) must land within tolerance of 1/(a+1) on hidden (n,a) incl. n=1, with willow_selftest() re-run requiring exit 0 + 'PASS'. (4) a LaTeX memo rebuilt fresh by pdflatex that must have zero 'Overfull \hbox' warnings, must not contain the over-wide unbreakable token and must contain no \texttt-verbatim token longer than 24 chars (synonym substitution), with the shipped pdflatex.log/prof also warning-free. Tool breadth (Coq+R+sympy+LaTeX) and the independent audit of every artifact drive the difficulty; the induction itself is easy-per-competency, and this task meets/exceeds the medium floor of the R naming competency.

wren-cipher.documented_probe: C-409f50fe (gpg-encrypt an archive and remove plaintext intermediates): covered at medium difficulty; the verifier independently decrypts, checks OpenPGP cipher 9 / S2K hash 10, requires wrong-passphrase rejection on a hidden case, and sweeps /app and /tmp for surviving plaintext archives.
wren-cipher.notes: Single multi-tool stage: build a transient tar snapshot strictly under /tmp, symmetric-seal it with gpg (--cipher-algo AES256, --s2k-digest-algo SHA512, batch/loopback passphrase-file), remove every plaintext intermediate, and record the cipher name. The verifier re-runs the deliverable with hidden source dirs/passphrases in both invocation styles, diffs decrypted trees byte-for-byte, inspects packets, and enforces wrong-passphrase rejection and the no-intermediates sweep. Rubric weights tool_breadth (tar/gzip/gpg/mktemp), unsafe_action_penalty (leaving cleartext snapshots), and adversarial/generalization checks; totals bucket to medium.

wren-forge.notes: Focused Stan-authoring probe (R/rstan surface): write a hierarchical Bayesian beta-binomial program (per-group binomial likelihood k ~ binomial(n, theta), shared beta group prior theta ~ beta(alpha,beta), and the exact Jeffreys-type hyper-prior target += -0.5*log(alpha)-0.5*log(beta)-0.5*log(alpha+beta)), plus a reusable deterministic R driver that validates the trial table, embeds the exact program, samples with a fixed seed and publishes posterior draws and a summary. The verifier re-runs the driver on visible and hidden tables (different group counts/sizes/rates), byte-checks the emitted program against the deliverable, independently compiles the deliverable Stan source and samples it against empirical germination rates (semantic proof that likelihood and prior structure are right), and checks invalid-input rejection. Hard: Stan syntax/semantics must survive an actual toolchain compile (failure mode: syntax or semantic error fails the model parse), plus quantitative posterior-vs-rate tolerances and multi-dataset generalization.

wren-link.notes: Focused single-competency task: drive llvm-link over separately emitted IR modules into one combined bitcode module resolving cross-file references, then link it with a C harness into a native executable. Failure modes probed: undefined symbols from a missed module (plugin.bc must have no undefined cross-module declares) and duplicate symbols from double-linking; link.sh must be generic for two hidden module sets with distinct call chains. Depends on a staged toolchain flow (link -> nm check -> compile+link -> run).

wren-loom.documented_probe: C-ac4a9918 (declare the mailing-list configuration in the canonical file): the second covering task; the verifier fully checks the capability — the canonical config path, its documented semantics, and the live daemon honoring it after an idempotent provision script runs on visible and hidden specs.
wren-loom.notes: Medium: write an idempotent provisioner that renders a spec CSV into the canonical /etc/loopd/lists.conf (documented INI-like semantics: last-section-wins, enabled only on exact 'true', members in config order), signal the already-running daemon (SIGHUP via pidfile, no restart), and emit a live-state report. Hidden cases re-execute the provisioner on other specs (reordered lists, tagged member addresses, disabled lists, an empty spec), so hard-coded lists fail. Rubric nonzero for dependent stages (config -> reload -> verify), tool breadth (signals/sockets), reasoning depth, debugging ambiguity (canonical path + reload semantics), adversarial inputs (empty spec, disabled lists, verbatim tagged addresses), hidden-case generalization, and interaction statefulness (live daemon).
