wren-quarry.notes: Medium: the agent must start a local stdlib HTTP defect-service, pull the defect report (line numbers, kinds, intended semantics) from GET /defects, and apply five single-line repairs exclusively through POST /fix. Every request burns one attempt and the grader enforces a ceiling of 6 attempts for 5 defects (service hard-locks at 8), so careless trial-and-error fails the run even if the file ends up correct. Repairs are diagnosed from the intent hints (accumulator clobber, off-by-one window loop, swapped clamp bounds, chunk stride, missing descending sort). The verifier rebuilds the file from the pristine copy plus the recorded fix chain (catching out-of-band edits), audits that every defect line was repaired within budget, and executes the repaired module on hidden behavioural cases (empty inputs, full-window boundaries, k<=0, short tails, ValueError paths, floats/negatives).

wren-spire.documented_probe: Covering task for C-ac4a9918 (declare the mailing-list configuration in the canonical file) at medium difficulty; verifier fully checks the capability (fresh-state provisioning + live daemon routing on hidden mail batches).
wren-spire.notes: Single-stage: discover the canonical config path of the installed listd daemon, author the INI list declarations at /etc/listd/lists.conf via an idempotent provisioning script, and reload the running daemon. The verifier strips the canonical file and restarts the daemon first, so config written anywhere else (or a daemon never reloaded) fails; hidden cases replay distinct mail batches (uppercase addressing, direct-to-subscriber mail, unknown addresses, empty-subscriber list) through the daemon. Nonzero rubric for tool_breadth (ctl script usage), reasoning_depth, debugging_ambiguity (canonical-path discovery), hidden_case_generalization, interaction_statefulness (running daemon must be reloaded).

wren-vane.notes: Covering task for C-b9c4c8e7 (implement an integer mathematical function as a finite logic-gate network): compile y = F(isqrt(x)) mod 2^32 into a straight-line 32-bit operator network (isqrt by 16 restoring subtraction steps, Fibonacci by 32 unconditional fast-doubling steps with SEL/MUX on bits), plus a general evaluator for the documented format. Rubric: reasoning_depth/quantitative_correctness high (loop unrolling to a DAG, exact modular arithmetic, edge cases 0/2^32-1/perfect squares), hidden_case_generalization (3 hidden vector files checked both by an independent format evaluator and by the agent's evaluator), dependent_stages (netlist must be authored then simulated then probe output produced), debugging_ambiguity moderate (off-by-one in isqrt steps or fib bit order fails specific vectors), adversarial_inputs (format rules enforced: node ordering, arity, shift ranges, constant ranges, 1200-node cap).

zephyr-anchor.notes: A compact bioinformatics batch that must satisfy six distinct deliverables exercised end-to-end. window.py must construct a DNA string whose GC fraction stays inside a stated range in EVERY fixed-length sliding window (an invariant that must hold at exact integer counts, probed by re-running on hidden lengths/windows/GC ranges). fasta.py must emit exactly two records with forward-first orientation and template-derived headers and no stray whitespace, and must reverse-complement correctly on hidden templates (multi-line, mixed case, GC-rich). smiles.py converts SMILES to RDKit Mol objects and returns None for invalid or empty/whitespace input without ever raising (hidden catalogs include unresolvable elements, unbalanced/open rings, and blank entries; RDKit returns an empty Mol for the empty string, which the agent must detect). api_client.py starts the localhost fixture spectra/sequence server (no outbound net), selects a donor by its emission and an acceptor by its excitation against disjoint wavelength windows that are exactly-one on every hidden database, fetches amino-acid sequences by identifier and reproduces them exactly, and joins every project member to the employee row in the project's department. tool_breadth=3: RDKit, an HTTP client plus an in-process fixture server, subprocess lifecycle management, JSON I/O, and FASTA parsing. reasoning_depth=3: the window-balancing construction, the spectral donor/acceptor disambiguation, and the same-department referential join. interaction_statefulness=2: each api_client run brings up and tears down the local server with a readiness poll on a fresh free port. quantitative_correctness=3: exact per-window GC counts, exact reverse-complement equality, exact atom counts, and byte-exact API sequence equality are all required. hidden_case_generalization=3: every deliverable is re-run against hidden inputs it has never seen. The task rates hard because all six claimed competencies carry a hard reference floor; each is exercised here at full fidelity (nothing is faked or simplified).

zephyr-bridge.notes: Total 18 = hard. The pipeline is a long chain of dependent stages that must stay mutually consistent: learn a BPE tokenizer (vocab + merge rules in the loader's exact formats), train a 300-dim word2vec-style embedding matrix whose rows exactly equal the vocab and are distributionally meaningful (verified by within-class vs cross-class cosine separation on frequently co-occurring anchors), build a fasttext-style linear classifier over mean-pooled word embeddings that clears a holdout-accuracy floor while its serialized model stays under a size budget, emit a per-model metrics table (model, correlation, error, penalty, dof) with internally consistent values, and serialize a Vocab dataclass whose word<->index maps are exact inverses sized to the embedding rows. Difficulty comes from coordinating tokenizer/embedding/classifier/metadata so every invariant holds simultaneously, generalising the whole runner to fresh and malformed synthetic corpora (blank, punctuation-only, digit-only, short, duplicate, and missing-TAB rows), and respecting the accuracy-vs-size budget and verifier time budget. Leaning implementation: a gensim+scikit-learn rapid pipeline stands in for the classic C++ fasttext binary (no compiled-toolchain step), but every competency is genuinely exercised for real.

zephyr-cipher.notes: Five medium-floor DSP competencies chained in one pipeline: exact-parameter scipy STFT magnitude export, wavelength->wavenumber conversion, localized-decimal spectrum parsing, RMS-normalized 16-bit multitone wav synthesis, and vosk mp3->text transcription. Quantitative rigor dominates: STFT magnitudes must equal a scipy gold to 1e-4, wavenumber peak centers to 1 cm^-1, wav RMS inside a band, all requested tones present in the spectrum. Hidden cases vary STFT window/nperseg/nfft/boundary settings, sample rates, spectrum peak counts/wavelengths, tone frequencies/RMS levels, and spoken phrases, so generalization to fresh scenarios is required. Transcription is exercised for real (preinstalled vosk model + ffmpeg decode of mp3), keeping the speech competency honest rather than faked. Sum 13 => medium, matching the medium floor of every competency.

zephyr-engine.notes: End-to-end recovery pipeline: enumerate candidate flare passphrases under the compact commissioned-seed gate (the naive full 24-char alphanumeric token space is hopeless; you must honor the subkey/seed gate and the exact 24-char ZEPH...CORE uppercase-digit format and write every well-formed candidate); select the active vault passphrase via a sha1 hex letter-count structural beacon (K=17); run a password-hash probe of the AES-256 7z to confirm it is a protected/crackable target; crack and extract the member with the recovered password; then a parallel defensive leg sanitizing the leaked credential out of a repo with a reusable scrubber and patching a jar-upload filename filter against traversal and dangerous-extension masks. True to 'hard': two hard-floor competencies (format-constrained enumeration, subkey-seed search-space shrink) require reasoning to avoid an infeasible brute force; the long dependent_stages chain means one wrong password/format/fingerprint propagates to a failed extraction; debugging_ambiguity and adversarial mask/traversal inputs plus hidden scrub dirs drive generalization; quantitative_correctness matters for the exact digest count, exact answer.json keys, and exact decrypted creds bytes. No unsafe actions are demanded and no interaction statefulness is required.

zephyr-forge.notes: Hard (total 19). Six distinct competencies must each be genuinely solved: (1) provision a real MIP solver that reads standard .mps and returns the exact integer optimum (hidden models carry an integrality gap, so an LP-relax-only solver fails); (2) exact weighted MAX-SAT optimum over 2^n assignments with a hard-UNSAT case that must be reported specifically; (3) formulate and minimize a convex quartic + per-vector quadratic penalty + global coupling objective numerically to a near-stationary optimum matching a reference minimizer; (4) enumerate every distinct basic-feasible corner of nonnegative LPs with exact rational arithmetic (duplicate columns, m>n and negative-rhs edge cases); (5) classify solver verdict text using a documented token rule incl. empty-file and case-mixed edges; (6) choose a literal-vs-back-reference segmentation (fixed self-delimiting format) that decodes byte-exact and stays strictly under a byte ceiling that a naive all-literal encoding always exceeds. tool_breadth 3 (HiGHS/CBC MIP, scipy numeric optimizer, exact Fraction linear solve, text classification, custom LZ packing); reasoning_depth 3 (the generalisation contract, the exactness of the optima/counts, and the DP over coding costs in F); hidden_case_generalization 3 (three hidden case dirs probe HARD_UNSAT, empty/to-be-over-255 verdicts, m>n and singular/duplicate corners, tight ceilings, and a fresh MIP with a general-integer variable).

zephyr-gasket.notes: Difficulty total 12 -> medium (matches task.toml 'medium', >= the max competency floor 'medium'). The maze side is a navigation-constrained, feedback-only unknown-maze explorer: the agent may only peek the cell it stands in and move a single cell through open passages, so it must run a real DFS with backtracking over cycles and dead ends within a move budget and reconstruct the full wall map plus a legal path to the far exit. This exercises explore/infer layout, per-id instance targeting, and navigation with constraints. The reference-maze selfcheck (offline known fixture) forces the same flood logic to generalize before it is trusted on the live unknown instances. The game side is mate-in-1 search over a precisely-specified chess subset (K,Q,R,B,N, no pawns/castling): the agent must generate legal moves, filter self-check, verify check, and prove the opponent has no reply, writing all winning moves in src-dest square notation. Every result is equality-checked against an independently re-deriving engine, and hidden cases vary maze size/layout/cycles and game piece/game configurations including zero-mate and missing-opponent-king edge positions (adversarial=2, hidden_generalization=3, quantitative=3). reasoning_depth=2 from the search + legality proofs; a single shared exploration core generalizes across all instances (hidden uncertainty). No heavy resource or interaction pressure beyond the single-file CLI contract.

zephyr-grove.notes: A single reusable scheduling engine must jointly solve three independent deterministic problems from one config: an exact subset-sum counting objective (one-use-only + allowed-number semantics, duplicates handled as distinct elements, negative/zero target gates), a 9x9 Latin-square arrangement serialized to strict two-digit zero-padded row-major tiles, and an availability overlap finder that enforces the weekday business-hours window with a lunch exclusion across every person simultaneously and emits only windows that reach the required duration. Reasoning depth (hard): designing the exact-count DP so duplicates and off-by-one sum handling are right, plus interval semantics (lunch slice, inverted/ignored intervals, exact-boundary inclusion) are easy to get subtly wrong. Adversarial_inputs: hidden cases force a zero-count answer, an all-busy empty plans list, a lunch-gap split at the exact == duration boundary, and malformed busy/multipce entries plus duplicate and non-positive numbers (all of which our daemon must tolerate). Debugging_ambiguity: three outputs must all be correct at once; a wrong assumption in any sub-problem fails an independent gold. Hidden generalization: the grader re-runs the executable on four fresh configs and compares to independent recomputation. Sum 18 => hard, meeting and exceeding the max floor (medium) among the five competencies.

zephyr-helix.documented_probe: C-01d6c7ae is intentionally exercised only through the integrator's discretization choice (atol/rtol/method) required to stay inside the state/right-hand-side budget for randomized initial states; it is not an autonomous full-physics simulation of its own, so that dimension is subsumed by C-5149cd00 rather than graded twice.
zephyr-helix.notes: Hard (18/30). Two independent scientific kernels must be authored from a bare contract and generalize to unseen inputs. integrate.py must numerically solve a linear first-order system under a hard ceiling on RHS-evaluation calls while every grid state stays within a max-absolute-error tolerance of the exact matrix-exponential solution and stays finite; tuning atol/rtol/method to fit the budget is genuine quantitative reasoning. eig.py must select the largest-magnitude eigenvalue (magnitude, not real-part ordering, so complex-conjugate and negative-real spectra are traps) and emit per-index leading principal-minor spectra ordered by magnitude. Both CLIs must reject malformed cases with a clean ERR exit. Hidden-case generalization and exact-output correctness dominate; moderate build/steps make it run cleanly CPU-only.

zephyr-notch.notes: Three chained stages: (1) author a reusable secure eraser that overwrites each file in place before unlinking and finally removes the whole directory tree, then run it on /app/vault to produce /app/erased_ok.txt; (2) consult `man openssl-enc` to identify the exact -aes-256-ctr option and decrypt /app/handoff/msg.enc, documenting the option in capability_notes.md; (3) persist the exact recovered plaintext to /app/results.txt. dependent_stages=3 because the marker emission depends on the eraser succeeding, the decryption depends on the man-page-derived option, and the results file depends on that decryption. tool_breadth=2 for shred/find (erase), man + openssl enc -K/-iv (crypto), bash scripting. adversarial_inputs=2 because the hidden erase trees include dot-files, names with spaces, a read-only file, an empty tree, a broken symlink, and a missing target, and hidden crypto re-runs the documented option on fresh ciphertexts including an empty plaintext. hidden_case_generalization=2 because both deliverable programs are re-executed on unseen hidden material. quantitative_correctness=2 because the final message and the cipher option must match byte-for-byte. unsafe_action_penalty=2: the eraser must never walk out of its target (blast-radius checks fail a wildcard rm), matching the secure-erasure competency's requirement to destroy only the designated tree. Medium floor from competency C-51021b37.

zephyr-orchid.notes: A three-stage media+ASR pipeline is gated stage-by-stage (download must yield a real mp4 before trimming; the ASR model must be unpacked before transcription), spans three tools (curl, ffmpeg/ffprobe, python3/vosk over a local HTTP mirror) and requires numeric content agreement (trailer PSNR>=30dB, transcript strings must normalize-exactly against independent expected text). Hidden cases replay the downloader on unseen fixtures (different durations/resolutions, query-string URLs) and push voice recognition over fresh audio at odd sample rates (44.1kHz) - real generalization rather than output-file guessing. Rubric sum 13 lands in the medium bucket (10-17) and is at least the max competency floor (medium) for C-a13c3ba1, C-361f3946 and C-494accea.

zephyr-summit.notes: Rubric total 20 -> hard bucket, matching task.toml 'hard' and >= the max competency floor (hard, from the formal-proofs competency C-047ea557). The task is a staged toolchain build-out (dependent_stages=3): a clean-room C compiler (zcc, authored for the task, at /app/cc-src) is installed as /app/vendor/bin/cc, /app/sections.txt is derived by compiling a probe with that very compiler and dumping its ELF sections and symbol tables with readelf, the Coq proof module is completed and compiled to a .vo proof object, the Scala 2.11 project is packaged into a standalone assembly JAR (bundle scala-library so java -jar works), and a symbolic execution engine with the z3 constraint solver is implemented and installed on PATH. tool_breadth=3 covers the compiler install/build pipeline (python front-end + as/ld via binutils), coqc, scalac+jar, readelf, z3, and the LLVM-16 toolchain. reasoning_depth=3: completing the formal proofs requires real tactic work (induction; the gauss identity needs polynomial arithmetic that plain lia cannot close, forcing nia/ring), and writing a correct symbolic executor over an IR with ITE path conditions. hidden_case_generalization=3: the engine is re-run byte-for-byte on hidden IRs (including a NO_SOLUTION case), the compiler is re-run on hidden C programs, and sections.txt is byte-compared to a rebuilt readelf dump. debugging_ambiguity=2 from compiler/codegen and proof tactic failures; adversarial_inputs=1 (the NO_SOLUTION engine case and scala arg variants); resource_pressure=2 from the multi-toolchain install/build budget and 1-cpu build. quantitative_correctness=2 for exact numeric outputs (solver models, jar arithmetic, compiled program stdout).

zephyr-vault.notes: Total 15 = medium, at/above the max competency floor (medium). The task chains three distinct competencies: reading the legacy auth source and recognising that the login query is spliced with + (string concatenation of user input) for the audit; authoring the hardened /app/app.py render path so the running server keeps its Flask/version identity while binding every supplied payload class as data (never evaluating {{...}}/<%= %>/${}/<?php?>/{% %} via any engine) and tolerating malformed bodies; and driving the provided spreadsheet REST mock to create a nested named spreadsheet+worksheet, record the returned ids, and stay idempotent on re-run. Difficulty comes from interlocking those stages (source audit -> fixed app -> regression harness -> verified resources), from designing a regression checker that both proves non-evaluation across payload classes and preserves the framework banner, and from generalising to hidden payload classes, unicode/special-char spreadsheet names and malformed creates handled cleanly.

zinc-meridian.documented_probe: C-92a2624a (filter and rank candidates by proximity to a target property value): reference floor is hard and this covering task is hard; the verifier fully checks the capability on hidden cases.
zinc-meridian.notes: Single pipeline of dependent stages: recursive formula parsing (nested parens, hydrate dots with multipliers), atomic-mass lookup, descriptor computation, inclusive-tolerance filter, deterministic ranking with id tie-break, plus a normalization report of parsed/rejected rows. Hard via the recursive-descent formula grammar and exact rounding/tie-break semantics. Hidden cases cover boundary-inclusive candidates, distance ties, unknown elements against a reduced masses table, malformed formulas, hydrates, zero matches and an empty compounds array. Rubric nonzero for dependent_stages (parse -> lookup -> compute -> filter -> rank -> report), reasoning_depth, adversarial_inputs/hidden_case_generalization (5 hidden cases), quantitative_correctness (exact floats and sort order). No tool breadth, no environment pressure.

cedar-summit.documented_probe: C-6f29d769 (complete an authenticated interactive conversation with each person's phone tool): the agent must bring up four Flask microservices, obtain the planning phrase from the coordinator desk as the registered planner, then hold phrase-authenticated multi-turn conversations with three colleague phone services via interactive bash dialers (read + respond), gathering availability, preferences and constraints, and aggregate them into the unique optimal plan written to /app/offsite_plan.json. Hidden probes re-validate the plan against the group's hidden state, read the services' call journal to confirm every authenticated conversation actually happened (phrase issued, all three questions asked per colleague, calls completed), and confirm a wrong phrase still ends a call with no data. A stale/missing phrase ends the call early and no data is gathered — the documented failure mode.
cedar-summit.notes: Medium-to-hard interactive task: stack bring-up, multi-service HTTP conversation protocol, authentication phrase flow (coordinator issues, colleagues require), and preference/constraint aggregation with a unique optimum. High interaction_statefulness (server-side session state across turns), dependent_stages (up -> phrase -> calls -> aggregate -> plan), adversarial_inputs (wrong-phrase hang-up, feasible-but-suboptimal plans), unsafe_action_penalty (weakening the services' auth or editing /opt/offsite is detected). Kept in the medium bucket: the protocol is fully documented and the decision space is small.

flint-gate.documented_probe: C-2e082c47 (shape-robust kernel across both gate modes) + C-c34cf87e (kernel bodies restricted to triton.language ops with explicit reductions): one task covers both. The agent implements an optionally gated LayerNorm as a @triton.jit kernel under TRITON_INTERPRET=1; hidden probes execute it against a pure-torch reference on a matrix of shapes (B=1, S=1, D=1, odd non-power-of-two D) in both the gated and no-gate branches, at rtol=1e-4/atol=1e-6, and an AST/text inspection fails the task if tl.sum / .sum( / the built-in sum or any torch/numpy/math call appears inside the kernel bodies.
flint-gate.notes: Medium: author a shape-robust Triton kernel in CPU interpreter mode with two reduction passes (mean, variance) expressed without the tl.sum helper, an optional-gate branch, and masked handling of non-power-of-two D. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (reduction without the sum helper; padding/masking), debugging_ambiguity (interpreter-mode semantics differ from GPU Triton), adversarial_inputs (edge shapes and the None-gate branch), hidden_case_generalization (hidden shape/mode matrix), quantitative_correctness (tight float32 tolerance).

tb3-agate-latch.documented_probe: Hardware authoring + simulation with Icarus Verilog: the agent writes a parametrized synchronous FIFO (sync_fifo) with registered count, combinational show-ahead dout, and read-before-write head visibility, documented cycle-by-cycle and validated against the visible sanity testbench. The hidden testbenches each embed an independent golden array/pointer/counter model and compare dout/full/empty/count after every rising edge over fixed-seed randomized and scripted sequences (LFSR-driven, no $urandom), covering write-when-full, read-when-empty, simultaneous read+write at full, empty, and count==1, deep wrap-around across the pointer boundary, mid-sequence synchronous resets, and non-default parameters (DATA_WIDTH=12, DEPTH=64 via parameter override). The verifier compiles and simulates the agent's RTL against each hidden testbench and requires its PASS sentinel.
tb3-agate-latch.notes: Medium: author clean synthesizable RTL to an exact protocol. Nonzero rubric for tool_breadth (iverilog/vvp compile-simulate-debug loop), reasoning_depth (registered vs combinational outputs, full/empty legality on pre-edge state, read-before-write visibility at count==1, circular pointer arithmetic with parameterized depths), debugging_ambiguity (observable timing is subtle; the visible fixture only nudges, the hidden goldens are strict), adversarial_inputs (simultaneous ops at the full/empty boundaries and mid-stream reset pulses), hidden_case_generalization (three independent hidden TBs plus non-default geometry via parameter override, so hardcoded or default-geometry stubs fail), quantitative_correctness (count/full/empty/dout exact every cycle).

tb3-birch-lemma.documented_probe: tb3-birch-lemma exercises the Science/Linguistics competency of historical/computational linguistics: implementing a strictly ordered sound-change derivation engine with exact positional matching semantics. The verifier executes /app/derive.py on the visible pair and on five hidden (rules.json, lexicon.txt) pairs covering feeding chains (rule 1 creates rule 2's environment), bleeding chains (rule 1 destroys rule 2's environment), pre-pass single-pass matching traps (adjacent matches on one rule), initial/final/medial insertion rules, edge-conditioned changes at both word edges, a fully deleted word, words where nothing applies, and interior spacing preservation in the input column; each output is compared byte-for-byte against the verifier's own independent recomputation, so hardcoding the visible output fails.
tb3-birch-lemma.notes: Medium: the semantics are fully documented (single pre-pass match pass per rule, rightmost-first application, edge and empty-context matching, deletion/insertion position shifts), so the programming task is mechanical once the spec is read, but the hidden cases make any shortcut fail: ordering traps (feeding and bleeding) distinguish implementations that respect list order from naive ones, and five orthogonal hidden rule sets (deletion chains, insertion rules, dual-edge-conditioned changes, inert lexicons) force true generalization rather than visible-shape matching. Reasoning depth comes from getting the pre-pass semantics and boundary insertion indices exactly right; byte-exact TSV comparison (including a zero-length derived field and preserved interior whitespace) removes grading ambiguity. No tool breadth, resource pressure, or interaction state beyond a single CLI invocation.

tb3-brass-caliper.documented_probe: Parametric mechanical-part geometry engine (bolt-circle spacer/flange): the agent authors an importable pure-Python cadmodel module (bolt-hole centers, edge clearances, annular area, volume, mass, validate_spec, build_report) and a rounded JSON report for a visible spec. The verifier imports /app/cadmodel.py and re-runs every function on hidden specs (bolt counts 1/2/12/24, tiny margins, planted multi-code violations, boundary-touch cases, malformed values, float-vs-int bolt counts, missing keys) under three limits variants, plus an independent recompute of /app/spacer_report.json.
tb3-brass-caliper.notes: Medium: quantitative_correctness 2 because every reported number must match an independent recompute to 4 decimals under exact documented conventions (angles, overlap handling, rounding, sort order); hidden_case_generalization 2 because hidden specs span edge shapes and limits variants so hardcoding the visible report fails; adversarial_inputs 2 from malformed-field specs (strings, bools, negative/zero values, float bolt count, missing keys); dependent_stages 2 because the module and the JSON report must agree with each other and with the verifier. No tool breadth or resource pressure: pure stdlib math, single-digit-second runtime.

tb3-harbor-ledger.documented_probe: Claims-adjudication engine: the agent implements /app/adjudicate.py (a stdlib CLI) plus the visible report /app/adjudication.json. The verifier first executes the CLI on the visible fixtures, then runs an independent recomputation inside /tests/hidden/adjudicate_probe.py that replays the CLI on hidden (policy, claims) bundles — a single-day leap-day window (2024-02-29) with day-before/day-after denials, aggregate exhaustion mid-id-sort with truncated partial payment then aggregate_exhausted zeros, duplicate ids resolved by stable original-line order (mixed approved/denied same-id rows), zero-amount claims mapping to ['eligible'], a two-cent claim where the documented coinsurance floor (1.5 cents -> 1) differs from any rounding scheme, exclusion precedence over the window check, and an all-denied set — comparing exact decisions, payable_cents, full reason-code lists including order, and aggregate totals. Any deviation, including a hardcoded visible answer, fails.
tb3-harbor-ledger.notes: Medium: the pipeline has five dependent stages in a documented order (eligibility with exclusion-over-window precedence, deductible, explicit floor at the coinsurance step, per-claim cap, annual aggregate applied in stable ascending-id order with mid-sort truncation), producing exact integer outputs and machine-readable reason codes whose ordering is graded. Quantitative correctness is the dominant dimension (exact cent arithmetic, floor vs round-half-up trap on the two-cent claims, exact-boundary truncation); hidden bundles add adversarial shapes (leap-day, duplicates, zeros, all-denied) so a hardcoded visible output fails, yet the task is pure stdlib with no resource pressure or tool breadth.

tb3-linden-choir.documented_probe: Media/Music skill, symbolic music-theory analysis (no audio): the agent authors /app/analyze.py, a pure-stdlib CLI that reads a JSON chorale score (key + chords with beats, durations, unvoiced note lists) and writes a deterministic functional analysis — diatonic roman numerals with quality and inversion over major and minor keys, phrase-final cadence labels (PAC/IAC/HC/PLAGAL), and rank-pair parallel perfect-interval detection — plus the /app/analysis.json deliverable for the visible C-major fixture. Hidden probes execute /app/analyze.py twice per score on G-major (planted parallel fifths), D-minor (planted parallel octave, deceptive V->VI), E-flat-major (plagal IV->I), all-diminished, duplicated-note, and empty progressions, and compare exact parsed-JSON equality against the probe's own independent recomputation (harness/refanalyze.py) of the documented ruleset; malformed inputs (bad note, off-key chord, bad key, missing fields, invalid JSON, missing file) must be rejected with a non-zero exit and no output file.
tb3-linden-choir.notes: Medium (sum 10): the core is a precise theory-ruleset implementation — triad matching over spelled major/harmonic-minor pools, bass-determined inversion, nested cadence rules with a documented phrase-final definition, and a rank-pair parallel-fifths/octaves algorithm — so reasoning_depth is 2 and correctness is exact (parsed-JSON equality against the verifier's independent recompute, so a hardcoded visible analysis fails). debugging_ambiguity is mild (edge behaviors like identical-note unisons, tiered tie-breaks, and the degree-sign character must match the docs exactly). adversarial_inputs and hidden_case_generalization are both 2: six hidden scores spanning four keys plus planted-parallel, deceptive, plagal, all-diminished, duplicated-note, empty, and malformed cases. Zero tool breadth (stdlib only) and zero resource pressure.

tb3-rowan-statute.documented_probe: Data-processing declaration building: the agent writes a CLI generator (/app/build_declaration.py) that validates raw transaction rows into an exact-reason validation report, aggregates valid rows by (direction, partner_country, commodity_code) with integer cents / milli-kg arithmetic, applies per-direction exemption thresholds (exactly-at-threshold included), and emits a byte-order-sorted declaration CSV. The verifier independently recomputes both outputs from the raw inputs and compares; it also executes the deliverable on a copy of the visible workdir and on three hidden workdirs (boundary aggregates exactly at and one cent below the threshold, duplicated txn_ids incl. rejected duplicates and an empty-unit commodity entry, an all-invalid file with a blank line and a multi-reason row, and an all-valid-but-exempt file yielding an empty declaration), so any hardcoded visible output fails.
tb3-rowan-statute.notes: Medium: five pipeline stages are load-bearing (validate with six documented reason codes plus MALFORMED_ROW, aggregate with exact integer arithmetic, threshold-exempt with an explicit >= boundary, C-locale sort, stable txn_id sort of the report), the visible fixture demos every reason and an exactly-at-threshold inclusion, and the hidden cases push the boundary to the cent, duplicates, degenerate all-invalid and empty-result shapes. The verifier recomputes expected output itself from the hidden fixtures rather than storing answers. Resources are trivial; no tool breadth or pressure.

tb3-vellum-poster.documented_probe: Media/Design skill exercised as verifiable SVG: the agent authors a deterministic parametric poster renderer (/app/render_poster.py) whose output is a pure function of a JSON layout spec, and renders the visible poster (/app/poster.svg). The verifier executes the renderer on the visible spec and on hidden specs (different canvases incl. odd widths, palettes, float layout constants, section counts incl. zero sections, empty/trailing-newline bodies, text with &/<) and independently recomputes the full expected element tree from each spec with its own implementation of the documented r1/fmt/line-count formulas, comparing every tag, attribute value, and text exactly; it also validates /app/poster.svg against the visible spec and re-runs one case for byte-identical determinism.
tb3-vellum-poster.notes: Medium: the layout contract is expressed entirely in prose and tables; the agent must transcribe it into exact deterministic arithmetic (Python round(x,1) half-to-even, format(x,'g') shortest-form output, documented body line-splitting). Correctness is quantitative and exact — every coordinate, size, color and font attribute must match the verifier's independent recompute as strings — so hidden-case generalization (2) and adversarial inputs (2) carry the difficulty: zero-section, empty-body and float-constant hidden specs defeat any hardcoded or spec-ignoring renderer, and a byte-determinism re-run rejects time/randomness-dependent output. Two dependent stages (script plus its rendered artifact, both graded). No tool breadth, resource pressure, or interaction state.

ds-kestrel-client.documented_probe: Three hidden probes exercise the three protocol skills. Probe 1 (multipart): hidden part lists (quotes/backslashes in names and filenames, empty values, binary file content, empty content types, special-char boundaries, unicode, many parts) are re-encoded by an independent reference encoder in the probe and byte-compared against /app/httpkit/multipart.py's multipart_encode output, plus make_boundary determinism and the full build_request bytes. Probe 2 (chunked): hidden chunked streams (multi-chunk, chunk extensions with quoted semicolons, final chunk with extensions, duplicate trailers, no trailers, unicode bodies, malformed sizes, truncation, bad terminators, unterminated trailers, trailing garbage, max_body overflow) are decoded by an independent reference parser and compared field-for-field, with ChunkedError cases asserted. Probe 3 (cookies): a scripted exchange log with an injected clock (default-path computation, domain/path scoping conflicts, Max-Age and Expires expiry, rejection rules, capacity eviction order, cookie_header assembly order) is replayed against an independent reference cookie model; snapshots and Cookie headers are compared at every step. Probes also re-run the visible byte fixtures through the deliverables and compare to independently recomputed expected parses, so hardcoded visible outputs fail hidden cases.
ds-kestrel-client.notes: Medium: the agent implements three documented protocol contracts (exact-byte multipart builder with CRLF discipline and quoting rules; chunked-transfer decoder with extension skipping, trailer surfacing and malformed-stream errors; deterministic cookie store with scoping, eviction and header-ordering rules) plus wiring into the shipped request builder/parser. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (RFC-derived edge rules must be implemented exactly as documented), adversarial_inputs (malformed chunk streams, scoping conflicts, capacity eviction, bad attribute values), hidden_case_generalization (hidden fixtures re-encoded/decoded by independent reference implementations in the probes, exact bytes and exact state), quantitative_correctness (byte-for-byte and state-equality comparisons), interaction_statefulness (the cookie store is a stateful model driven by scripted exchanges with an injected clock). Low tool_breadth (single python toolchain), no resource pressure, low ambiguity because every rule is spelled out.

ds-lint-forge.documented_probe: Linter rule engineering over a shipped mini lint engine (tokenizer + tiny AST + CLI skeleton with line-scoped suppression). The agent authors three rule plugins (forbid-call incl. attribute forms and an inside-function scope rule; shadow-var on a documented block model with for-target/param/def bindings; mut-default for mutable literal defaults), extends suppression with region (stack-nested, unclosed-to-EOF) and next-statement forms, and adds an incremental findings cache keyed by (rules signature, file content hash) with a --stats flag. The verifier runs /app/lintkit/lint.py on hidden minipy sources and independently recomputes the expected findings (its own tokenizer, parser, three rules and suppression semantics) comparing exact sorted JSON per file; cache correctness is checked by running the CLI twice against a fresh /app/lintcache (run 2 must be all hits with identical output) and by mutating a copied hidden file so the content-hash key must miss and produce updated findings.
ds-lint-forge.notes: Medium: the task is staged (rules -> suppression -> cache) but every stage is small and self-contained; reasoning depth comes from the documented scope/block model and suppression precedence, adversarial inputs from nested/overlapping regions, unclosed regions reaching EOF, next-directives aimed at compound headers, for-target and param shadowing and defaults nested inside functions. Hidden sources generalize beyond the visible examples, and the probe recomputes everything independently so hard-coded or shortcut answers fail. Exactness is quantitative (line/col/message JSON equality) and the cache adds one interaction-statefulness dimension; no resource pressure and no unsafe-action penalty.

ds-mistral-manifest.documented_probe: ds-mistral-manifest evaluates a helm-like manifest-merge engine: values precedence (defaults merged with --values layers in order, later overrides earlier, CLI files last), null-deletes-a-key, typed {{ .path }} placeholder substitution, and a per-template array-merge policy table (replace | append | merge-by-key with dotted key paths and deep merge of matching items, including null deletion inside items). The verifier ships an independent reference engine that recomputes canonical outputs from hidden charts and drives /app/render_chart.py through subprocess: the visible case (files re-run into a fresh dir plus the /app/rendered deliverable), hidden charts with 3-layer conflicting overrides, nested merge-by-key conflicts, dotted-key array templates, append-to-absent-path, empty overlays, and a battery of documented error cases (unknown policy, missing from/key/policy, unknown template, missing value path, malformed placeholder, non-list from value, non-list merge target, item missing key, bad values file shape/JSON, bad chart.json, template shape, missing chart.json/templates dir). Every successful case compares the exact emitted file set and canonical JSON bytes; every error case asserts the exact exit code (0/2/3/4) and a stderr token.
ds-mistral-manifest.notes: Medium. The agent authors a single deterministic Python CLI implementing precisely-documented merge semantics. reasoning_depth captures the interplay of layered precedence, null-deletion, structural substitution and the three array policies including deep item merges with dotted key paths; adversarial_inputs covers empty values, empty overlays, null deletion at multiple levels, and ~15 documented error/edge cases; hidden_case_generalization is high because every output is recomputed by an independent reference engine over structurally different hidden charts, so a hardcoded visible render fails; quantitative_correctness is strict exact canonical-JSON and file-set equality. Low tool_breadth (single stdlib CLI), no resource pressure, low ambiguity because every rule and exit code is spelled out.

ds-runner-shard.documented_probe: deepswe-skill (test-harness internals): the agent extends the bundled mini runner /app/harness/runner.py to (1) shard a suite into K launcher bins via documented LPT (longest-processing-time-first) scheduling with deterministic duration-descending/id-ascending and load/lowest-index tie-breaks, (2) implement bail mode with dependency-driven skip cascades (dep-precedence over bail, transitive blocking, deps-before-dependents manifest order), and (3) emit CTRF-like aggregate + per-launcher reports with exact counts, durations, statuses, shard assignment and skip reasons, then deliver /app/run_report for the visible suite with params.json. The verifier executes /app/harness/runner.py on the visible suite (k/bail taken from the delivered params.json, delivered reports must equal regeneration and the independent recompute) and on six hidden suites (uneven durations, cross-shard dep chains, all-fail, all-pass, K > cases, duration ties) under eleven k/bail combinations, independently recomputing every report file and requiring exact JSON equality.
ds-runner-shard.notes: Medium: three coupled sub-deliverables (sharding, bail cascade, reports) with an exact-output contract; the correct LPT ordering (duration desc, id asc) and tie-break rules, the dep-vs-bail skip precedence, transitive dependency blocking across shards, and per-launcher/aggregate arithmetic must all be right at once. Hidden generalization is strong: six suites plus eleven parameter combinations, including degenerate shapes (K larger than the case count producing empty launcher reports, every-case-fails with bail, pure-tie durations that bind on id order, a K=1 whole-suite run). Deterministic simulation only; no wall-clock, randomness, network, or resource pressure.

ds-sash-builder.documented_probe: Probe 1 (canonical window SQL rendering): the agent implements the OverSpec/window_item extension for a shipped mini query builder; the hidden probe re-renders the visible demo's DEMO_SPECS with an independent reference renderer and byte-compares python3 /app/demo.py stdout and /app/demo_out.sql, then drives ~20 hidden matrix queries (all six functions, multi-window selects, window+where+outer-ORDER interplay, call interleaving, empty partition_by/order_by, bare OVER (), five frame combinations, embedded-quote identifiers) through the real Qb API and byte-compares .sql() strings. Probe 2 (API surface): verifier imports /app/qb/window.py, spot-checks window_item output strings, and requires invalid OverSpec constructions (unknown function, wrong arg counts, non-pair or malformed frame) to raise ValueError.
ds-sash-builder.notes: Medium: the agent must write a rendering module whose output is byte-exact against an independent canonical SQL reference across a hidden usage matrix, reusing the shipped builder's quoting/order-entry rules. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (deterministic clause ordering, UPPERCASE keyword/spacing rules, frame-bound vocabulary), adversarial_inputs (invalid functions, arg-count mismatches, malformed frames, embedded-quote identifiers, empty partitions), hidden_case_generalization (20 hidden queries in an unrelated domain with unseen tables/columns/aliases/frames), quantitative_correctness (byte-for-byte canonical strings), and dependent_stages (extension module must integrate with the pre-wired select_window, then the demo regeneration, then the verifier recompute). Low debugging ambiguity because the canonical rules and the shipped core helpers are fully documented; no tools, no resource pressure, no statefulness.

tl-ashward-scan.documented_probe: TBLite-skill gap: idempotent persistence-artifact scanner over a forensic rootfs tree. The agent authors /app/scan_persistence.py (stdlib-only CLI over documented locations: cron.d, crontab files, systemd units incl. an unusual dir, rc.local, shell rc snippets, ld.so.preload, at-job spools) plus /app/findings.json. Hidden probes execute the deliverable against three unseen trees built in the probe — a symlinked-cron.d mix, an allowlisted-hit trap with a differing allowlist and lookalike decoys, and an empty tree — and compare the parsed JSON exactly against an independent reference scanner implementing the documented rules; byte-for-byte idempotency (two runs) and the exit-code contract (0 readable / 2 missing root / 3 write failure) are also enforced.
tl-ashward-scan.notes: Medium: one deliverable CLI must implement seven per-kind artifact grammars with status semantics (active/disabled/allowlisted), a per-root allowlist consulted first, comment/disabled/environment lookalikes that must stay unflagged, exact sort order and JSON types, and byte-level idempotency. Hidden trees force genuine generalization: the reference recomputes expectations from fixtures rather than storing answers, and the allowlisted-hit trap plus a symlinked cron directory penalize hardcoded visible output, embedded visible allowlists, and location-blind scanners. No runtime network, no GPU, pure stdlib, whole oracle+verifier cycle under a minute.

tl-briar-entity.documented_probe: (tblite-skill family) XXE vulnerability analysis and remediation across five XML parsing scripts. The agent runs /app/analyze_xxe.py to produce /app/xxe_audit.json (verdicts per parser with canonical reason strings), then patches every vulnerable parser under /app/parsers/ (rejecting external entity declarations and entity chains deeper than the documented max_entity_depth 6) while preserving documented benign extraction on visible and hidden inputs. The verifier independently probes pristine copies at /opt/pristine/parsers with hidden payloads (a file:// file-read probe referencing a hidden secret, recursive-entity probes at depths 12 and 14), requires the audit verdicts and exact reason sets to match those independent verdicts, requires patched parsers to leak no secret bytes and never expand past depth 6 while reproducing the reference extraction byte-for-byte on four hidden benign documents (nested/unicode, CDATA+char refs, flat declared entity, empty root) and the visible samples, and re-runs the analyzer against pristine copies requiring byte-identical regeneration of the audit.
tl-briar-entity.notes: Medium: run a stdlib-only analyzer that sandbox-probes five SAX/minidom parsers to classify two documented XXE classes (file:// external entity resolution only achievable when a SAX driver enables external GES plus an entity resolver; recursive internal entity expansion) and then patch each vulnerable parser so probes are rejected/neutralized without disturbing benign extraction. Rubric: unsafe_action_penalty 2 (missed leaks must be caught by hidden probes; verify-then-patch staging), dependent_stages 2 (analyze first, patch after; verifier stage order), hidden_case_generalization 2 (different hidden secrets, two recursion depths, four hidden benign shapes), adversarial_inputs 2 (empty-root, CDATA-with-markup, predefined/char refs, flat entity preserved), reasoning_depth 2 (independent reference extractor, chain-depth policy, defeating hardcoded verdicts), resource_pressure 0, interaction_statefulness 0, quantitative_correctness 1 (byte-exact benign output).

tl-crown-pareto.documented_probe: Exercises the tblite-skill multi-objective evolutionary optimization capability: the agent authors a deterministic stdlib-only NSGA-II CLI (fast non-dominated sorting, crowding distance, binary tournament, crossover/mutation with feasibility repair, external elitist archive, exact hypervolume) for two documented problem families: a bounded knapsack with (value, -weight) objectives and continuous problems with closed-form Pareto fronts (f2 = 1 - f1^2; 3-objective f3 = 1 - f1^2 - f2^2). The probe runs /app/nsga.py on three hidden params files (different seeds, sizes, including a 3-objective case) and independently recomputes objectives from the returned encodings (feasibility + exact/rtol match), checks mutual non-domination and exact hypervolume consistency, then applies per-problem quality gates: knapsack hypervolume >= 0.85x of an independent same-seed reference NSGA-II run; saddle IGD-to-analytic-front strictly below 0.9x the median of 5 random-search fronts of identical budget; triplane documented front property (mean|f1^2+f2^2+f3-1| <= 0.05, max <= 0.25, spans >= 0.6) — plus a static check that the core NSGA-II components exist.
tl-crown-pareto.notes: Medium: implement a complete NSGA-II from scratch in pure stdlib with strict reproducibility (single random.Random(seed) stream), exact objective recomputation, exact 2D/3D union-of-boxes hypervolume, and problem-specific quality gates. Nonzero rubric for reasoning_depth (dominance/crowding/archive/tournament design, closed-form front reasoning), debugging_ambiguity (no per-run oracle; only property-based grading with float tolerances), adversarial_inputs (hidden seeds/sizes and a 3-objective problem with a documented front property), hidden_case_generalization (three hidden param sets spanning all problem families; hardcoded visible fronts and single-objective optimizers fail), quantitative_correctness (exact knapsack objectives, exact hypervolume, IGD metric, tight thresholds). Low tool_breadth/resource_pressure: stdlib-only and sub-second-to-few-second runtimes.

tl-ember-tangle.documented_probe: (tblite-skill family) diagnose-and-repair of a seeded race condition in a concurrent asyncio service. The agent must identify the non-atomic read-modify-write across the simulated slow I/O await in the shipped word-count service (naming the exact read/await/write lines of the pristine original in /app/diagnosis.md), repair the merge into a synchronous critical section in /app/svc/wordcount_service.py, and demonstrate that the documented 40-worker load then matches the sequential ground truth. The verifier independently recomputes expected counts from the deterministic schedule rule (seeded randrange draws, round-robin workers), runs the pristine load generator unmodified, re-runs the pristine original service under the same load and requires it to still corrupt, hash-checks the fixtures, and probes 3 hidden corpus/load configs with different worker counts (24x9, 60x5, 12x25) including blank-line, huge-token, mixed-case and whitespace-padded documents.
tl-ember-tangle.notes: Medium: the race is invisible under a sequential run (workers=1 is exact even with the bug), so the agent must reason about cooperative asyncio scheduling to explain why 40 concurrent workers lose increments. Nonzero debugging_ambiguity (bug only manifests under load; exact lost value is nondeterministic), reasoning_depth (interleaving analysis, fix classes: atomic sync merge vs asyncio.Lock), hidden_case_generalization (hidden corpora+worker counts recomputed independently, so hardcoding fails), quantitative_correctness (exact integer equality on every hidden case), resource_pressure (40+ concurrent workers through loopback), interaction_statefulness (shared dict accumulates across many requests), dependent_stages (diagnose -> repair -> verify under documented and hidden loads).

tl-gilded-bandit.documented_probe: tblite-skill: online learning for a nonstationary multi-armed bandit with delayed feedback and abrupt drift. The agent writes /app/policy.py (a Policy class with choose(t, history) and change_point_estimate()) plus /app/eval_report.json. The verifier re-implements the documented seeded bandit simulation independently, re-runs the policy on the visible fixture and three hidden parameter sets (no-drift, three-way rotation, long per-pull delays, different K/seeds/drift steps) and requires regret <= max(0.50 * static_baseline_regret, 0.10 * T) per case, where the static baseline always pulls argmax(pre_probs) and the oracle best-arm schedule is recomputed from the reward matrix. The report must recompute exactly (cumulative/oracle/regret) against the visible re-run and its change-point estimate must match the policy hook and lie within 250 steps of the true drift_step; hardcoded visible fixtures crash or overshoot on the hidden sets.
tl-gilded-bandit.notes: Medium: the core skill is delayed, out-of-order reward attribution plus drift adaptation (restart/sliding-window reasoning) with a quantitative regret bar that discounts the naive always-initial-best baseline by half and floor-budgets the no-drift trap. Delayed feedback makes local debugging genuinely ambiguous (evidence about past pulls arrives late and reordered), and the hidden sets are adversarial (no drift at all, three-way rotation, 30-70-step delays, varying K). A plain UCB1 policy passes the drifting cases but not the long-delay one; an over-explorer fails the no-drift floor; the visible-overfit shortcut fails hidden K/drift checks. Stdlib-only, deterministic seeded runs, cheap CPU loop (T<=3000).

tl-onyx-token.documented_probe: Token-based auth service skill: HMAC-signed JWT-style tokens with claims, expiry, rotation and a revocation blacklist. The deliverable /app/token_service.py is a loopback auth service (login/refresh/logout/me) that must mint tokens byte-identical to an independent recomputation of header.payload.signature (HMAC-SHA256 over the config secret, exact compact claim JSON, per-process jti counter), enforce iat/exp windows with a documented X-Onyx-Now time header and clock skew, rotate refresh tokens (old refresh blacklisted), and persist revocations in /app/state/blacklist.json across process restarts. A hidden flow harness drives the running service over loopback, crafts its own valid/expired/future/tampered/wrong-key/wrong-issuer/missing-claim/wrong-typ/malformed tokens, replays rotated refresh tokens, restarts the process mid-test, and re-runs the whole battery against three generated hidden configs (different secrets, lifetimes, clock skews, users, ports). A hardcoded-response stub fails the recomputed signatures; an in-memory-only blacklist fails the restart probe.
tl-onyx-token.notes: Medium (rubric 13): the security contract is exact and checkable (byte-exact token strings, claim order, HMAC recomputation, jti counter), which drives quantitative_correctness=2; adversarial_inputs=2 from the crafted-token matrix and tamper/replay tests; interaction_statefulness=2 because rotation+logout mutate a persisted blacklist that must survive a mid-test restart; hidden_case_generalization=2 because three hidden configs re-run the identical flow battery through the same deliverable, so any config-hardcoding or visible-only shortcut fails. Moderate reasoning_depth for the claim/clock/blacklist check ordering, moderate debugging_ambiguity for boundary tolerance semantics. No resource pressure.

tl-quartz-partition.documented_probe: tblite-skill: systematic test-case generation via the Category-Partition Method over a TSL-like specification. tl-quartz-partition.notes: Medium: the core is a single self-contained Python deliverable implementing a multi-part deterministic algorithm (parse TSL with properties/values/ranges; strategy-dependent base and default-fill computation; constraint satisfaction via documented minimal-deviation repair; canonical grouping base/single/ordinary/error; unsatisfiable handling; id renumbering under frame_limit). reasoning_depth and debugging_ambiguity are moderate because the exact semantics (fill vs base, exclusion of non-base singles from repair, lexicographic tie-break) are documented but require careful reading and cross-checking against the visible fixture; adversarial_inputs covers malformed specs/params exit codes plus degenerate all-single and unsatisfiable specs; hidden_case_generalization is high because the deliverable must generalize to unseen TSL specs and params variants (hardcoding the visible 9-frame output fails every hidden case); quantitative_correctness enforced by exact JSON equality against an independent recompute and byte determinism between runs.

tl-scroll-changelog.documented_probe: tblite-skill (parse conventional commits, compute per-package semver bumps, emit canonical per-package CHANGELOG.md files for a monorepo): the agent authors a stdlib-only CLI that reads a repo-state snapshot (commits.jsonl / packages.json / last_tag.json) and writes bumps.json + byte-exact changelogs; the verifier executes /app/changelogger.py on the visible state and on 3+ hidden repo states, recomputing bumps and changelog bytes with an independent reference implementation and comparing byte-for-byte, plus error-path probes (missing packages.json, malformed last_tag.json, bad --date must exit nonzero). Rubric: reasoning_depth 2 (grammar + precedence + tie rules), adversarial_inputs 2 (unknown scopes, non-conventional commits, empty messages, breaking docs, malformed JSONL lines, error exits), hidden_case_generalization 2 (three varied hidden states + empty log), quantitative_correctness 2 (byte-exact changelog, version arithmetic, exact hash prefixes). tl-wire-socket.documented_probe: tblite-skill (implement the WebSocket protocol server side: opening handshake + frame codec): the agent hand-builds the RFC-style handshake (SHA-1 + magic GUID -> base64 Sec-WebSocket-Accept, status 101) and frame codec (FIN/opcode/mask/7-16-64-bit lengths, masking XOR, text/binary echo, ping->pong, close echo, fragmentation reassembly, documented close codes) from stdlib only. The verifier's raw-socket probe recomputes the accept value from each presented key, runs masked echo round-trips including 126-byte and 65536-byte payloads (16-bit and 64-bit length fields), fragmentation with interleaved control frames, ping/pong, close-code echo, and a malformed-frame battery (unmasked frames, RSV bits, reserved opcodes, non-minimal lengths, 64-bit MSB, invalid UTF-8), asserting close code + TCP close; it repeats the full battery under 3 hidden configs with different ports and paths, so a canned-response server or hardcoded visible behavior fails.

Hidden_case_generalization comes from 3 hidden configs (different port/path) plus randomized payload batteries, so no visible-only shortcut survives; quantitative_correctness is the exact accept recomputation and byte-for-byte echoes. No resource pressure; single tool (python3 + raw sockets).
